children.text: yaś cakṣur jagataḥ sahasrakarabad dhāmnāṃ ca dhāmā 'rkavan
children.translated_text: He who is the eye of the world, like one of a thousand rays, the radiance of radiances, sun-like,

children.text: mokṣadvāram apāvṛttaṃ ca ravivad dhvāntāntakṛt sūryavat/
children.translated_text: who has opened the gate to liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) like the sun, who destroys darkness like the sun,

children.text: ātmā sarvaśarīriṇāṃ savitṛvat timāṃśuvat kālakṛt
children.translated_text: who is the self (<s>ātman</s>) of all embodied beings like the sun, the maker of time like its rays,

children.text: sādhvīṃ naḥ sa giraṃ karotu savitā yo 'anyair atulyopamaḥ//
children.translated_text: may that <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun), who is incomparably beyond compare, make our speech virtuous!

children.text: vakṣyāmi bhūpam adhikṛtya guṇopapannaṃ
children.translated_text: I shall speak, with regard to a king endowed with virtues,

children.text: vijñātajanmasamayaṃ pravibhktabhāgyam/
children.translated_text: whose birth-time is known and whose fortune is ascertained,

children.text: ajñātasūtim athavā 'viditaiṣya bhāgyaṃ
children.translated_text: or whose birth is unknown and whose future fortune is not determined—

children.text: sāmudrayātrikanimittaśataiḥ pṛthūktaiḥ//
children.translated_text: [I shall speak] by means of hundreds of omens relating to oceanic voyages, extensively described.

children.text: karma 'nyajanmajanitaṃ[K.nyajanmani kṛtaṃ] sad asac ca daivaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> (action) generated in another birth, whether good or bad, constitutes fate (<s>daiva</s>);

children.text: tat kevalaṃ bhavati janmani satkulādye/
children.translated_text: that alone manifests at birth, along with noble lineage and the like.

children.text: bālyāt paraṃ vinayasauṣṭhavapātratā ca[K.'pi]
children.translated_text: After childhood, the capacity for discipline and accomplishment also [manifest],

children.text: puṃdaivajā kṛṣivad ity upapādyam etat[K.ata udyameta]//
children.translated_text: arising from human effort and fate, like agriculture—this is to be demonstrated.

children.text: sāmantakālayasu[K.vasu]dhodyamamantrabhṛtyair
children.translated_text: Through feudatories, time, resources, territory, effort, counsel, and servants,

children.text: daivena ceti kṛṣivan nṛpateḥ phalāptiḥ/
children.translated_text: and through fate—like a farmer, a king obtains his fruit.

children.text: syāc chidram ekam api cet tata eva sarvaṃ
children.translated_text: But if even one of these has a deficiency, everything from that alone

children.text: nāśaṃ prayāti hi dṛteḥ sravaṇād[K.dṛteś caraṇād] iva 'mbhaḥ//
children.translated_text: goes to ruin, like water from a leaking leather bag.

children.text: graharkṣatithyudgamarāśihorā
children.translated_text: If [favorable] planets, stars (<s>nakṣatras</s>), <s>tithis</s> (lunar days), rising [signs], <s>rāśis</s> (zodiacal signs), <s>horās</s> (hours),

children.text: dreṣkāṇabhāgādyanukūlamātram/
children.translated_text: <s>dreṣkāṇas</s> (decans), degrees, and the like, being merely favorable,

children.text: bhaved yiyāsor yadi siddhihetuḥ
children.translated_text: were the sole cause of success for one wishing to march,

children.text: svayaṃ bhaved daivavid eva rājā//
children.translated_text: then the king himself would be an astrologer (<s>daivavid</s>).

children.text: mantrābhiṣekamaṇibandhanaśāntikarma
children.translated_text: If <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulas), consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), gem-binding, pacificatory rites (<s>śāntikarma</s>),

children.text: homopavāsasurayāgajapādimātram/
children.translated_text: <s>homa</s> (fire oblation), fasting (<s>upavāsa</s>), worship of the gods (<s>surayāga</s>), <s>japa</s> (recitation), and such alone

children.text: syāt siddhihetur atha ced vijagīāato[K.vijigīṣato] 'rīṇ
children.translated_text: were the cause of success for one wishing to conquer enemies,

children.text: kasmāt tadā narapatir na bhavet purodhāḥ//
children.translated_text: then why would the royal priest (<s>purodhās</s>) not become king?

children.text: budhārthaśāstrāṇy[K.buddhvā 'rthaśāstrāṇy] api mantriṇo 'pi
children.translated_text: Even ministers who have studied treatises on statecraft (<s>arthaśāstra</s>)

children.text: kuyuḥ praṇāmaṃ na nareśvarāṇām/
children.translated_text: would not bow to kings,

children.text: yady ābhijātyadvipavājipatti
children.translated_text: if the primary dependence on noble birth, elephants, horses, infantry,

children.text: kośādyapekṣā na bhavet pradhānā//
children.translated_text: and treasury were not paramount.

children.text: svadeśe santuṣṭaḥ karituragakośe sati na yo
children.translated_text: A [king] who is content in his own territory, having chariots, horses, and treasury, and does not

children.text: bhaved yāyī saindhaiḥ[K.so 'nyaiḥ] kṛtaparibhavo yāti vilayam/
children.translated_text: go on campaign, when attacked by others, goes to ruin;

children.text: svacakreṇaiva 'sau kṣapitadhanarāṣṭro bhavati vā/
children.translated_text: or, remaining with his own forces alone, he becomes one whose wealth and kingdom are depleted;

children.text: gato yo nādatte[K.'nyān ādatte] sunayacarito nītividhūrān//
children.translated_text: but one who, marching forth, follows good policy and takes [the kingdoms of] those who have abandoned statecraft.

children.text: ulūkasya dhvāṃkṣo niśi valibhujāṃ so 'hni vaśagaḥ
children.translated_text: The owl is subservient to the crow at night, and the crow to raptors by day;

children.text: sthale nakraṃ siṃho mṛgapam udke hanti jalajaḥ/
children.translated_text: on land, the lion kills the crocodile, but in water, the aquatic creature [kills] the lord of beasts.

children.text: abudhyā yaḥ kālaṃ vrajati nṛpatir deśam athavā[K.omitted]
children.translated_text: A king who, through ignorance, marches at the wrong time or to the wrong place,

children.text: hate darpe vākyaṃ smarati viduṣāṃ so 'rivaśagaḥ//[K.this lline omitted]
children.translated_text: when his pride is crushed, remembers the words of the wise—he [becomes] subject to the enemy.

children.text: ripoḥ kṛtvā 'vajñāṃ jitam iti viditvā madabalān
children.translated_text: Having despised the enemy, thinking 'he is conquered,' intoxicated by the power of pride,

children.text: na yatno hātavyaḥ śikhiviṣasamo 'lpo 'pi hi ripuḥ/
children.translated_text: effort must not be abandoned—for even a small enemy is like fire and poison.

children.text: pramatto 'dreḥ kuñjād ayutabalabhāgair api narair
children.translated_text: The lord of elephants, inattentive, [is captured] from a mountain cave by men having even a fraction of ten thousand in strength,

children.text: hato baddhastambhe kakhati[K.baddhaḥ stambhekaṣati] madalekhāṃ dvipapatiḥ//
children.translated_text: and bound to a post, scratches the lines of rut [helplessly].

children.text: vapraprākārayantrapraharaṇaparikhātoya*meyendhanāḍhyaṃ[K.dhānyendhanāḍhyaṃ
children.translated_text: Having made a fortress well-provisioned with ramparts, walls, machines, weapons, moats, water, [immeasurable] and fuel,

children.text: durgaṃ kṛtvā ''tmagupataṃ[K.''tmagulma] dvipaturagabhiṣakśilpiviprābhyupetam/
children.translated_text: self-protected, equipped with elephants, horses, physicians, artisans, and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: lubdhatrastābhimāniprakupitakubhṛtāṃ jñātaśīlair vihīnaṃ
children.translated_text: devoid of the greedy, frightened, proud, angry, and wicked governors whose character is known,

children.text: kṛtvā śūrāptasaṃsthaṃ paraviṣayam iyāc chuddhapārṣṇir narendraḥ//
children.translated_text: having stationed it with brave and trusted men, the king should march into enemy territory with a secure rear.

children.text: budhvā śaktiṃ svaparabalayoḥ sāmam ekapradānaiḥ[K.sāmabhekapradānaiḥ]
children.translated_text: Having assessed the strength of his own and the enemy's forces, [first employing] conciliation (<s>sāma</s>) and gifts (<s>dāna</s>) one by one,

children.text: kṛtvopāyair vyasanasamaropāyasaṃrakṣaṇaiś[K.gamanasamaropāyasaṃsarpaṇaiś] ca/
children.translated_text: then by stratagems, and by measures of protection against calamity and approaches [of the enemy],

children.text: bhaktyā[K.sāmnā] sādhūn dhanavirahitān arthalubdhāṃś ca dānair
children.translated_text: the virtuous should be won through devotion, the destitute through gifts, the greedy through wealth,

children.text: neyād[K.bhedyān] bhedais tribhir api na ye sādhayet tāṃś ca daṇḍaiḥ//
children.translated_text: those who cannot be won by the three [means] should be subdued by force (<s>daṇḍa</s>).

children.text: sāmno jīvaḥ sabhṛgutanayo daṇḍanāthau kujārkau
children.translated_text: <s>Jupiter</s> along with <s>Venus</s> is the lord of conciliation (<s>sāma</s>); <s>Mars</s> and the <s>Sun</s> are the lords of punishment (<s>daṇḍa</s>);

children.text: dānasyenduḥ śikhiyamabudhāḥ sāsurā bhedanāthāḥ/
children.translated_text: the <s>Moon</s> is [lord] of gifts (<s>dāna</s>); <s>Mercury</s> along with <s>Saturn</s> and <s>Rāhu</s> are the lords of dissension (<s>bheda</s>).

children.text: vīryopetair upacayakarair lagnagair vīryagair[K.kendragair] vā
children.translated_text: When [these planets] are endowed with strength, causing increase, placed in the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant) or in <s>kendras</s> (angular houses),

children.text: tat tat siddhiṃ vrajati tad ahaḥsv āṃśakair[K.aṃśake] vāpi teṣāṃ//
children.translated_text: that [respective policy] attains success on those days, or also by the <s>aṃśakas</s> (sub-divisions) of those [planets].

children.text: ṣāḍguṇye sandhir ādau paripaṇaracito vigraho 'syāpakārī[K.'syapākāro]
children.translated_text: Among the six strategies (<s>ṣāḍguṇya</s>), treaty (<s>sandhi</s>) comes first, carefully arranged; war (<s>vigraha</s>) [comes] when the enemy causes harm.

children.text: naitau ced āsanaṃ tat parapuragamanaṃ sarvasaineyna yānam/
children.translated_text: If neither of these [is suitable], then encampment (<s>āsana</s>); marching with the entire army to the enemy's city is [called] campaign (<s>yāna</s>).

children.text: sainyārddhenābhiyukte parapuram api yat tad dvidhāyānam uktaṃ
children.translated_text: When advancing against the enemy's city with half the army, that is called a dual march (<s>dvidhāyāna</s>);

children.text: saṃśleṣo 'nyatra yaḥ syāt sa khalu nigaditaḥ saṃśrayo 'nyo[K.'ntyo] guṇānam//
children.translated_text: alliance (<s>saṃśleṣa</s>) with another [power] elsewhere is declared as seeking refuge (<s>saṃśraya</s>)—the last of the strategies.

children.text: madhyāhne 'rkas tuhinakiraṇo nityam ākrandasaṃjñaḥ
children.translated_text: At midday the <s>Sun</s>, and the <s>Moon</s> always, bear the designation 'lamentation' (<s>ākranda</s>);

children.text: pauraḥ pūrve bhavati dinakṛd yāyisaṃjño 'ntyasaṃsthāḥ[K.'ntyasaṃsthaḥ]/
children.translated_text: the Sun in the east [at sunrise] is [called] 'civic' (<s>paura</s>), and [planets] in the last position [are called] 'marching' (<s>yāyin</s>).

children.text: jīvaḥ sauris[K.sauras] tuhinakiraṇāsyātmajaś ceti paurāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Jupiter</s>, <s>Saturn</s>, the <s>Moon</s>'s son [<s>Mercury</s>], and the Sun's son [<s>Saturn</s>]—these are civic [planets];

children.text: ketur yāyī sabhṛgujakujaḥ siddhikānandanaś ca//
children.translated_text: <s>Ketu</s> is a marcher; <s>Venus</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>, and <s>Mars</s> [are marchers], as is the delightful [<s>Mercury</s>].

children.text: yānaṃ yāyibhir āsanaṃ śubhakarair vīryānvitair nāgarair
children.translated_text: Campaign [is indicated] by the marching [planets]; encampment by the auspicious, strength-endowed civic [planets];

children.text: dvaidhībhāvam iyād yadā śubhakarāḥ paurāḥ sayāyigrahāḥ/
children.translated_text: a dual march occurs when the auspicious civic and marching planets are mixed.

children.text: saumyaiḥ sandhir asadgrahaiś ca balibhir yuddhe 'nukūlair jayaḥ
children.translated_text: Treaty [is indicated] by benefic planets; battle by malefic and powerful ones; victory when favorable [planets are present];

children.text: sarvair apy aśubhapradair narapatir daivāmbitaṃ saṃśrayet//
children.translated_text: when all are inauspicious, the king should seek refuge, overwhelmed by fate.

children.text: kośo hi rājyatarumūlam ato 'sya śākhāḥ
children.translated_text: The treasury is the root of the tree of kingship; from it [grow] its branches;

children.text: pakṣī vipakṣa iva kiṃ nidhanaḥ[K.vidhanaṃ] karoti/
children.translated_text: like a bird without wings, what can one without wealth accomplish?

children.text: annād ivendriyagaṇo vasutas tathā 'nnaṃ
children.translated_text: Just as the sense organs [depend] on food, so food [depends] on wealth—

children.text: tatprāptirakṣaṇavivṛddhiṣu yatnavān syāt//
children.translated_text: therefore one should be diligent in its acquisition, protection, and increase.

children.text: nīcācirāḍhyanṛpavallabhataskarebhyo
children.translated_text: The kingdom must be protected by the king from the lowly, the newly rich, royal favorites, and thieves—

children.text: rāṣṭraṃ nṛpeṇa parirakṣyam ato 'sya kośaḥ/
children.translated_text: and from these, his treasury [must be protected].

children.text: kāle karapraṇayanaṃ ca yathocitānāṃ
children.translated_text: The collection of taxes at the proper time and in appropriate amounts—

children.text: tan[K.taṃ] nārthayed bhavati yena janāpavādaḥ//
children.translated_text: he should not demand that which causes public censure.

children.text: yātrā nṛpasya śaradīṣṭaphalā madhau ca
children.translated_text: A king's military expedition bears desired fruit in autumn and in spring;

children.text: chidre ripor na niyamo 'sti[K.'tra] ca kecid āhuḥ/
children.translated_text: when the enemy has a weakness, there is no restriction [on timing]—so some say.

children.text: chidre 'py arer bhavati daivayutasya siddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Even when the enemy has a weakness, success comes to one who has favorable fate;

children.text: sāmānyam āmiṣam idaṃ pratibhūmipānām//
children.translated_text: this is the general bait for all kings.

children.text: śatror vadhāya sacivaṃ śubhadaivayuktam
children.translated_text: When fate is unfavorable to himself, the king should dispatch a minister endowed with auspicious fate

children.text: ājñāpayen nṛpatir ātmani daivahīne/
children.translated_text: for the destruction of the enemy.

children.text: jahyān na cārtham ati[K.api] daivaparo 'pi bhūtvā
children.translated_text: But one should not abandon effort even while being devoted to fate—

children.text: dṛṣṭe dvipe dvipapadānusṛtiḥ kim artham//
children.translated_text: when an elephant is [already] seen, what is the purpose of following elephant footprints?

children.text: kālo 'bhyupaiti sakṛd eva naraṃ kathaṃcit
children.translated_text: Opportunity (<s>kāla</s>) approaches a man only once somehow;

children.text: prāpnoti tan na samayaṃ[K.sa punaḥ] khalu kālakāṃksī/
children.translated_text: one who waits for the [perfect] time does not obtain that opportunity again.

children.text: kālena gocaragatān anapekṣya bhakṣyān
children.translated_text: The python, though slow-moving, attains success

children.text: mandakramo 'py ajagaraḥ samupaiti siddhim//
children.translated_text: through [patience with] time, not disregarding prey that comes within range.

children.text: durgasthitaṃ phalam apakvam analpayatnāt[K.analpayatnaṃ]
children.translated_text: Fruit situated in a difficult place, unripe, [obtained] with no small effort,

children.text: saṃsiddhim apy upakaroti guṇaṃ na puṃsām/
children.translated_text: even when obtained, does not benefit a man's qualities.

children.text: sādhāraṇaṃ svapatitaṃ ca bhaved yato 'taḥ
children.translated_text: Since it would be commonly available [later] when it has fallen of its own accord,

children.text: kāle 'bhiyuktapatitaṃ rasavat sukhāya//E22
children.translated_text: that which falls at the right time is juicy and [brings] pleasure.

children.text: raktāsitādyā hi yathāmbarasya varṇāḥ sitasyaiṣa bhavanti samyak/
children.translated_text: Just as the colors red, black, and others properly belong to a white sky,

children.text: vilagnatithyādiguṇās tathaiva viśuddhadoṣasya bhavanti yātuḥ//
children.translated_text: so too do the qualities of <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) and the like belong to a traveler whose faults are purified.

children.text: madyāṅganāvāditanṛtyagītāny akṣā vṛthādyā[K.vṛthāṭyā] mṛgayā dyunidrā/
children.translated_text: Liquor, women, instrumental music, dancing, singing, gambling, idle wandering, hunting, daytime sleep,

children.text: parokṣanindeti ca kāmajāni daśaiva vindyād[K.vidyād] vyasanāni puṃsām//
children.translated_text: and speaking ill behind others' backs—these ten vices arising from desire should be known as belonging to men.

children.text: vākpāruṣyaṃ daṇḍapāruṣyam īrṣyāṃ[K.īrṣyā] droho 'sūyā paiśunaṃ sāhasañ ca/
children.translated_text: Harshness of speech, harshness of punishment, jealousy, treachery, envy, slander, and recklessness—

children.text: arthasyoktaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ ca 'ṣṭasaṃkhyaḥ krodhodbhūto varga eṣa pradiṣṭaḥ/
children.translated_text: and the ruining of wealth, making eight in number—this group born of anger has been taught.

children.text: mahad idam anayānām āspadaṃ madyam āhus tanudhanamatisattvaśreyasāṃ karṣaṇāya/
children.translated_text: Liquor is declared to be the great abode of these vices, for the destruction of body, wealth, intellect, character, and well-being;

children.text: samupahatamatiḥ san[K.saṃs] tatpradhānendriyatvād gaṇayati na hi bhakṣyābhakṣyam anyāni caivam//
children.translated_text: one whose mind is impaired, because of the predominance of that sense [of taste], does not distinguish between what should and should not be eaten, and so with other things.

children.text: patnīyaty api mātaraṃ madavaśāt patnīṃ ca mātrīyati
children.translated_text: Under the power of intoxication, one treats one's mother as a wife and one's wife as a mother;

children.text: śvabhrīyaty api mandiraṃ ślathaśilaṃ kūpaṃ ca gehīyati/
children.translated_text: one treats a pit as a mansion and a well with loose stones as a house;

children.text: svalpaṃ vāry udadhīyatīśvaram apāṃ mohāt sthalīyaty api
children.translated_text: a puddle of water as the ocean, and the lord of waters through delusion as dry land;

children.text: mitrīyaty api pārthivaṃ kim aparaṃ kuryān na yan madyapaḥ//
children.translated_text: one treats a king as a friend—what else would a drunkard not do?

children.text: bhūyo 'pi dīvyati jito jayalipsayaiva prāpnoti tac ca saviśeṣataraṃ kadācit/
children.translated_text: Having lost, he gambles again, out of desire for victory; and sometimes he obtains that [loss] even more greatly.

children.text: kṛtvā 'priyāṇi madataḥ parito 'py aṭanti[K.paritapya cānte] bhūyaḥ[K.bhūpaḥ] pivet kim api doṣaviśeṣakāṃkṣī//
children.translated_text: Having committed offenses through pride, roaming about everywhere, the king would drink yet more, seeking yet greater faults.

children.text: abhyāgamotsavabhiṣagvacanopadeśaiḥ kāmaṃ pibed amatilopakṛd aprakāśam[K.āprakāmam]/
children.translated_text: One may drink on occasions of arrivals, festivals, by a physician's advice, and teachings—if it does not cause loss of judgment, and not publicly.

children.text: dyūtaṃ vinendriyasukhāni hitāni yuktyā vijñasya[K.śūnyaṃ hi] jīvitaphalaṃ viṣayair vinā kim//
children.translated_text: Gambling aside, sensory pleasures are beneficial when used wisely—for what is the fruit of life for the learned without sense objects?

children.text: śaucācāravivarjitaḥ śava iva tyaktaḥ suhṛdbāndhavair
children.translated_text: Bereft of purity and proper conduct, like a corpse, abandoned by friends and relatives,

children.text: niśśaṅko nirapatrapo gataghṛṇaḥ kṛcchrād avāptāśanaḥ/
children.translated_text: shameless, without modesty, devoid of compassion, barely obtaining food with difficulty—

children.text: bandhur nāsya nibandhanaṃ na śapatho lokadvayaṃ nekṣyate
children.translated_text: he has no kin, no bond, no oath; neither of the two worlds is seen [by him]—

children.text: māyāvī kulapāṃśalaś ca kitavo doṣākaro[K.doṣārṇavo] niḥsukhaḥ//
children.translated_text: the gambler is a deceiver, a disgrace to his family, a cheat, a mine of faults, and devoid of happiness.

children.text: daivajñamantrisuhṛdāptavacāṃsi rājā yo na ''driyen nijaviceṣṭitaduṣṭabuddhiḥ[K.driyet svamaticeṣṭitaduṣṭabuddhiḥ]/
children.translated_text: A king who, being of corrupt intelligence through his own misconduct, does not heed the words of astrologers, ministers, friends, and trusted advisors—

children.text: so 'gremareṇa[K.sannāyakena] rahito 'ndha iva 'cireṇa hāsyatvam eti patito viṣaye ripūṇām//
children.translated_text: he, like a blind man without a guide, quickly becomes a laughing-stock, having fallen into the domain of enemies.

children.text: medhāvī matimān adīnavacano dakṣaḥ kṣamāvān ṛjur
children.translated_text: Intelligent, wise, of undepressed speech, capable, patient, upright,

children.text: dharmātmāpy[K.dharmātmā tv] anasūyako laghukaraḥ ṣāḍguṇyavic chaktimān/
children.translated_text: righteous, free from envy, nimble-handed, knowledgeable in the six strategies (<s>ṣāḍguṇya</s>), powerful,

children.text: utsāhī pararandhravit kṛtadhṛtir vṛddhikṣayasthānavit
children.translated_text: enthusiastic, knowing the enemy's weak points, of firm resolve, knowing the conditions of growth and decline,

children.text: śūro na vyasanī smaraty upakṛtiṃ[K.upakṛtaṃ] vṛddhopasevī ca yaḥ//
children.translated_text: brave, free from vices, remembering favors done to him, and one who serves the elders—

children.text: parīkṣyakārī na vikasthanaś[K.vikatthanaś] ca dṛḍhapatijño 'tidṛḍhapahārī/
children.translated_text: acting after due examination, not boastful, firm in his allegiances, exceedingly firm in striking,

children.text: jitendriyaḥ syāj jitakopalobhanidrālasasthānaparigrahaś ca//
children.translated_text: with conquered senses, having conquered anger, greed, sleep, laziness, and inertia—

children.text: tyāgī vinītaḥ priyadarśanaś ca vyapetamohaḥ pratipattiyuktaḥ/
children.translated_text: generous, modest, pleasant to look at, free from delusion, endowed with practical wisdom,

children.text: deśasya kālasya ca bhāgavijñaḥ[K.bhāgavid yaḥ] svayaṃ ca yaḥ syād vyavahāradarśī//
children.translated_text: knowing the proper division of place and time, and himself observant of [just] administration—

children.text: śabdārthavin nyāyāpaṭuḥ pragalbhaḥ saṃgrāmavidyākuśalo 'bhijātaḥ/
children.translated_text: knowing the meaning of words, skilled in reasoning, bold, expert in the science of warfare, of noble birth,

children.text: smitābhibhāṣī mitasatyavaktā daivānvito yasya[K.yaś ca] sa dhāma lakṣmyāḥ//
children.translated_text: speaking with a smile, moderate and truthful in speech, and favored by fate—such a one is the abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity).

children.text: guṇaiḥ samastair api saṃprayuktā kanyeva yātrā viguṇāya dattā/
children.translated_text: A military expedition, even if endowed with all qualities, when given to an unqualified [commander]—like a maiden given to an unworthy [groom]—

children.text: karoty akīrtiṃ sukhavittahāniṃ[K.sukhavittahīnāṃ] yātrāntarajñānajaḍasya[K.pātrāntarajñānajaḍasya] dātuḥ/
children.translated_text: produces infamy and loss of happiness and wealth for the giver who is ignorant of the inner [qualities of the] recipient.

children.text: guṇānvitasyaiva guṇaṃ karoti yātrā śubharkṣagrahalagnayogāt/
children.translated_text: A campaign yields good results only for one endowed with virtues, through favorable stars, planets, and ascendant conjunctions;

children.text: vyarthā sadoṣasya guṇānvitā 'pi vīṇeva śabdāśrayavarjitasya//
children.translated_text: even when endowed with virtues, it is useless for one who has faults—like a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) for one devoid of musical ability.

children.text: yātrā viśuddhā 'pi samaṃ pravṛttā pātrānurūpāṇi phalāni dhatte/
children.translated_text: Even a campaign that is pure and undertaken simultaneously produces results according to the capacity of the [respective] recipients;

children.text: jagaty udīrṇā 'pi hi kauśikasya bhā bhānavī naiva tamaḥ pramārṣṭi//
children.translated_text: even the mighty radiance of the sun, though risen upon the world, does not dispel the darkness for an owl.

children.text: vicintya kāryāṇi niśāvasāne dviṣatsuhṛnmaṇḍalasaṃśritānām/
children.translated_text: At the end of night [before dawn], having reflected on the affairs of those dependent on the circles of enemies and friends,

children.text: balārthadeśeṣu niyojitānāṃ samāśritānāṃ ca kṛtākṛtāni//
children.translated_text: and on the accomplished and unaccomplished tasks of those stationed in [matters of] army, resources, and territory,

children.text: anādśritaḥ khyātaguṇaḥ paro 'pi śūro 'thavā sādhujanaḥ praśastaḥ/
children.translated_text: even one who has not sought refuge, if of renowned virtue, or another who is brave, or a good person of repute—

children.text: sampūjanīyo janasaṃprahārtham mameti deśopagato vicintya//
children.translated_text: one who has come to the territory should be honored for the sake of winning over the people, reflecting 'he is mine.'

children.text: saveṇubīṇāpaṇavasvanena gītena pūrvaṃ vyapanītanidraḥ/
children.translated_text: First awakened from sleep by the sound of bamboo flutes, <s>vīṇās</s>, <s>paṇavas</s> (drums), and singing,

children.text: śayyāṃ tyajet tūryaravāvasāne śṛṇvan giro maṅgalapāṭhakānām//
children.translated_text: the [king] should leave his bed at the end of the musical sounds, hearing the voices of those who recite auspicious texts.

children.text: ajñātapūrvāṇi na dantakāṣṭhāny adyān na patraiś ca samanvitāni/
children.translated_text: He should not use tooth-sticks (<s>dantakāṣṭha</s>) that are previously unknown, nor those with leaves attached,

children.text: na cordhvaśuṣkāni[K.yugmaparvāṇi] na pāṭitāni na yugmaparvāṇi[K.cordhvaśuṣkāni] vinā tvacā ca//
children.translated_text: nor those dried on top, nor split, nor those with an even number of nodes, nor those without bark.

children.text: udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukhasaṃsthito vā ṛjv abraṇaṃ tac ca vitastimātram/
children.translated_text: Facing north or facing east,

children.text: adyān narendro viniyamya[K.vinigṛhyā] vācaṃ prakṣālya jahyāc ca śubhapradeśe[K.śucau pradeśe]//
children.translated_text: the king should chew [the tooth-stick], which should be straight, without blemish, and a <s>vitasti</s> (hand-span) in length, having restrained his speech, and after rinsing should discard it in an auspicious place.

children.text: abhimukhapatitaṃ praśāntadiksthaṃ śubham atiśobhanam ūrdhvasaṃsthitaṃ ca/
children.translated_text: [A tooth-stick] that falls facing toward [the user], resting quietly in [its] direction, is auspicious and most beautiful, and [so is one] that stands upright;

children.text: aśubhakaram ato 'nyathā pradiṣṭaṃ sthitapatitaṃ ca karoti miṣṭam[K.mṛṣṭam] annam//
children.translated_text: one that [falls] otherwise is declared inauspicious; one that remains standing or [properly] fallen produces pure food.

children.text: praṇamya devāṃś ca gurūṃś[K.devāṇ svagurūṃś ca] pūrvaṃ datvā ca gāṃ vatsayutāṃ dvijāya/
children.translated_text: Having first bowed to the gods and teachers, and having given a cow with calf to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā mukhaṃ sarpiṣi darpaṇe ca nakṣatram ādau śṛṇuyāt tithiṃ ca//
children.translated_text: having seen his face in ghee and in a mirror, he should first hear the <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion) and the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day).

children.text: śrutvā tithiṃ bhagrahavāsaraṃ[K.bhaṃ grahavāsaraṃ] ca prāpnoti dharmārthayaśāṃsi saukhyam/
children.translated_text: Having heard the <s>tithi</s>, the lunar mansion, the planets, and the day of the week, he attains righteousness (<s>dharma</s>), prosperity (<s>artha</s>), fame, and happiness,

children.text: ārogyam āyur vijayaṃ sutāṃś ca duḥsvapnajātaṃ[K.duḥsvapnaghātaṃ] priyatāṃ ca loke//
children.translated_text: health, long life, victory, sons, the destruction of bad dreams, and popularity in the world.

children.text: dūrvebhadānāñjanatīrthatoyamṛdrocanāsarṣapapuṣpagandhān/
children.translated_text: <s>Dūrvā</s> grass, white mustard (<s>bhadra</s>), collyrium (<s>añjana</s>), sacred water (<s>tīrtha-toya</s>), earth, <s>gorocanā</s> (cow bile pigment), mustard seeds, flowers, and fragrant substances,

children.text: sitāmbaroṣṇīṣasuvaṇaratnāny āsevya kuryād bhiṣajāṃ vacāṃsi//
children.translated_text: white garments, turban, gold, and gems—having employed these, he should carry out the prescriptions of physicians.

children.text: smitaprasannaprathamābhibhāṣitaiḥ prasādadṛṣṭyā karasaṃparigrahaiḥ/
children.translated_text: With smiling, pleasant, first-spoken greetings, with glances of graciousness, with handshakes,

children.text: yathābhirūpaṃ[K.yathānūpaṃ] hṛdayāny api dviṣāṃ prasādayan dharmasabhāṃ samāśrayet//
children.translated_text: winning over even the hearts of enemies in a manner befitting [each person], he should attend the assembly of justice (<s>dharmasabhā</s>).

children.text: vinītaveṣābharaṇaḥ sadakṣiṇaṃ[K.vinītaveṣābharaṇaś ca dakṣiṇaṃ] kara[K.karaṃ] samudyamya vicakṣaṇānvitaḥ/
children.translated_text: With modest dress and ornaments, raising his right hand, accompanied by wise [advisors],

children.text: sukhopaviṣṭaḥ sthita eva vā nṛpaḥ samārimitro vyavahāradarśane//
children.translated_text: the king, comfortably seated or standing, with measured friendliness, should attend to the administration of justice.

children.text: kṣamānvito 'smīti vicintyam etad daṇḍyeṣu daṇḍakṣamaṇaṃ na dharmaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'I am endowed with forbearance'—though he may think this, pardoning the punishable is not righteous conduct (<s>dharma</s>);

children.text: daṇḍaprabhoāvo hi sa durjanasya haste na yo jīvati sādhuvargaḥ//
children.translated_text: for punishment is the authority over the wicked—without it, the community of good people cannot thrive.

children.text: sutarām abhivarddhate 'bhimāno nīcānāṃ kṣamayā 'nviteṣu yasmāt/
children.translated_text: The arrogance of the lowly increases especially because of forbearance shown to them;

children.text: ata ugratareṇa te nivarttyā yena 'nye 'pi khalās tathā na bhūyaḥ//
children.translated_text: therefore they should be checked with greater severity, so that other rogues too may not [behave] so again.

children.text: yasmin gṛhītaḥ[K.gṛhīte] sadṛśāparādho mahājanas trāsam upaiti tasmin/
children.translated_text: When one of equal offense is punished, important people in that [kingdom] become fearful—

children.text: daṇḍo nipātyo manujeśvarena kālāntare 'nyad vyapadiśya kāryam//
children.translated_text: Punishment should be administered by the lord of men; at another time, the matter should be designated differently.

children.text: dvirada iva madena viprayukto viṣarahito bhujago vyasiś ca kośaḥ/
children.translated_text: Like an elephant deprived of rut, a serpent without venom, or a sword in its sheath,

children.text: paribhavam upayāti na 'parādhe yadi manujādhipatiḥ karoti daṇḍam//
children.translated_text: a king incurs contempt if he does not administer punishment for an offense.

children.text: ekasya tulyodarapāṇipādā daṇḍāt prabhītāḥ[K.daṇḍasya bhītāḥ] praṇamanti martyāḥ/
children.translated_text: Those of equal belly, hands, and feet, mortals bow before the punishment of one [king];

children.text: atyugradaṇḍād api codvijante daṇḍo 'parādhapratimaḥ śivāya//
children.translated_text: yet they are alarmed even by excessively harsh punishment—punishment proportionate to the offense leads to welfare.

children.text: duṣṭasya daṇḍaḥ sujanasya pūjā nyāyena kośasya ca saṃpravṛddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: Punishment of the wicked, honor of the virtuous, just increase of the treasury,

children.text: apakṣapāto 'rthiṣu rāṣṭrarakṣā pañcaiva yajñāḥ kathitā nṛpāṇām//
children.translated_text: impartiality toward petitioners, and protection of the realm—these five alone are called the sacrifices of kings.

children.text: śrāntaś ca tasmin viniyujya sādhūn saṃgrāmavidyādivibhaktakālaḥ/
children.translated_text: Wearied by that [duty], appointing good men, dividing his time between the science of warfare and other [duties],

children.text: sarvāṇi kāryāṇi yathākrameṇa kuryān nṛpaḥ pratyaham ātmavāṃś ca//
children.translated_text: the self-possessed king should perform all tasks in due order each day.

children.text: rājñā kāryaṃ pañcame pañcame 'hni kṣaurarkṣe vā śmaśru bhasyodaye[K.tasyodaye] vā/
children.translated_text: The king should have his hair and beard shaved every fifth day, under a shaving-<s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), or at the rising of [the appropriate constellation];

children.text: tyaktvā tārāḥ pañcasaptatripūrvā[K.saptapañcatripūrvā] yātrākāle naiva kāryaṃ na yuddhe//
children.translated_text: avoiding the <s>nakṣatras</s> beginning with the seventy-five and three [i.e., specific inauspicious ones], neither at the time of a military expedition nor in battle.

children.text: ācārasthaḥ sāgarāntāṃ dharitrīṃ bhuṅkte dīrdhaṃ kālam utkhātaśatruḥ/
children.translated_text: One who abides by proper conduct enjoys the earth bounded by the ocean for a long time, having uprooted his enemies;

children.text: yatrā ''cāras tatra dharmasya vṛddhir dharmād bhogān dehabhede 'pi bhuṅkte//E36
children.translated_text: where there is [proper] conduct, there is growth of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness); through <s>dharma</s>, one enjoys pleasures even after the death of the body.

children.text: abhihitaguṇasaṃyutena rājñā kathitaguṇātyayasaṃsthito 'bhiyojyaḥ/
children.translated_text: A king endowed with the aforementioned qualities should attack [an enemy] who is established in the failure of the stated qualities;

children.text: upahatam upalabhya cāsya deśaṃ balam athavā nirupadruto 'bhiyuñjyāt//
children.translated_text: or, having observed that the enemy's territory or army is afflicted, he should attack when [the enemy is] free from [other] troubles.

children.text: pracuramaśakayūkaṃ makṣikādamśapūrvaṃ balam ajaladavṛṣṭyā pāṃśuvātāhataṃ vā[K.pāṃśupātāhataṃ ca]/
children.translated_text: An army abounding in fleas and lice, full of flies and gnats, struck by rain without clouds and by dust and wind,

children.text: piśitarudhiradhānyaprāṇivṛṣṭyā hatam vā[K. ca] karituragamanuṣyā yatra vādhyā na dīnāḥ[K.ca dhyānadīnāḥ]//
children.translated_text: or struck by rains of flesh, blood, grain, and creatures—where elephants, horses, and men are not afflicted but [merely] dispirited—

children.text: śabdāyante muhur api śivā gardabhadhvānatulyaṃ
children.translated_text: where jackals constantly howl with sounds like the braying of donkeys,

children.text: tyaktasnehāḥ parijanasuhṛdvāhanopaskareṣu/
children.translated_text: [where soldiers are] devoid of affection for their attendants, friends, vehicles, and equipment,

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ ko naḥ śaraṇam iti vā vādino yasya sainye
children.translated_text: [saying] 'Alas, who is our refuge?'—in whose army [soldiers] speak thus,

children.text: vidviṣṭā vā pravarapuruṣāḥ so 'bhiyojyo nṛpeṇa//
children.translated_text: or where the best men are hostile—that [enemy] should be attacked by the king.

children.text: nirālasyāvanatavadanāḥ ketanasvapnaśīlā
children.translated_text: [Where soldiers are] sluggish, with downcast faces, prone to sleeping on flagpoles,

children.text: bhraṣṭācārā malinapuruṣacchāyayā ''krāntadehāḥ/
children.translated_text: fallen from proper conduct, their bodies overshadowed by the shadows of impure persons,

children.text: dīrghaśvāsāḥ sajalanayanāḥ śokalobhābhibhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: sighing deeply, with tearful eyes, overcome by grief and greed—

children.text: sainye yasya dvijagurusuhṛddveṣiṇaś caiva yodhāḥ//
children.translated_text: in whose army the warriors are hostile to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, elders, and friends—

children.text: akāraṇaprodgataromakūpā jaye nirāśāḥ prakṛter apetāḥ/
children.translated_text: [where] the hair-pores of men stand up without cause, [where they are] hopeless of victory, estranged from their nature,

children.text: amaṅgalāceṣṭitajātahāsāḥ sainye narā yasya sa cābhiyojyaḥ//
children.translated_text: [where they] laugh at inauspicious gestures—he whose army has such men should also be attacked.

children.text: kapotakolūkamadhūni yasya samāśrayante dhvajacāmarāṇi/
children.translated_text: He whose banners and <s>cāmaras</s> (yak-tail fans) are frequented by pigeons, owls, and bees,

children.text: chatrāyudhādīni[K.chatrāyudhādyāni] ca so 'bhiyojyo yasyāthavā 'syajalāśayānām[K.'nāhatatūryaśabdāḥ]/
children.translated_text: as well as his umbrellas and weapons—he should be attacked; or he whose reservoirs [show omens].

children.text: pratīpagatvaṃ saritām iṣoś ca śoṣo 'thavā 'śoṣyajalāśayānām/
children.translated_text: The reverse flowing of rivers and arrows, or the drying up of reservoirs that should not dry up,

children.text: avārideśe salilapravṛtir ahaitukaṃ[K.avaikṛte] cāpsu tarec chilā vā//
children.translated_text: the appearance of water in a waterless place, or a stone floating in water without cause—

children.text: bhaṅgapātacalanāny animittaṃ rodanāni ca surapratimānām/
children.translated_text: the breaking, falling, and shaking of divine images without cause, and their weeping,

children.text: agnirūpam anilena vinā vā niścalāni ca yadā pracalanti//
children.translated_text: and a fiery appearance without wind, or when stationary things begin to move—

children.text: prasūtivaikṛtyam akālapuṣpāṇy āraṇyasattvasya purapraveśaḥ/
children.translated_text: abnormal births, untimely flowers, the entry of wild animals into the city,

children.text: pradoṣakāle kṛkavākuśabdā himāgame ca 'nyabhṛtaḥ pralāpāḥ[K.'nyabhṛtapralāpāḥ]//
children.translated_text: the sounds of cocks at dusk, and the cries of the <s>cuckoo</s> in winter—

children.text: dīrghaṃ dīnaṃ saṃhatāḥ sārameyāḥ krośanty uccair nityam eva 'nṛtau ca/
children.translated_text: when dogs howl together, long and pitifully, always loudly, even when not in [heat],

children.text: hanyur yoṣā yoṣito nirghṛṇāś ca dṛṣyaṃ nityaṃ[K.śvetaḥ kāko] naktam idrāyudhaṃ vā[K.ca]//
children.translated_text: and women strike women mercilessly, or the rainbow is constantly seen at night—

children.text: tilā vitailā yadi vā 'rddhatailā[K.rddhatailāḥ] sasyasya vṛddhir yadi vā 'tiriktā/
children.translated_text: if sesame seeds are devoid of oil or half-oiled, if the growth of crops is excessive,

children.text: annasya vairasyam asṛk tarūṇāṃ śuṣkapraroho virujāṃ praṇāśaḥ//
children.translated_text: if food tastes bad, if trees bleed, if dried-up [trees] sprout, or if plants are destroyed—

children.text: vihāya sarpākhuviḍālamatsyān svajātimāṃsāny upabhuñjate vā/
children.translated_text: if, abandoning serpents, mice, cats, and fish, [animals] eat the flesh of their own kind,

children.text: vrajanti vā maithunam anyajātyāṃ dīptāś ca nityaṃ vihagā mṛgāś ca//
children.translated_text: or if they mate with other species, and if birds and animals are constantly agitated—

children.text: bhaṅgaḥ pātas toraṇendradhvajānāṃ śītoṣmānāṃ vyatyayo bhūvidāraḥ/
children.translated_text: the breaking and falling of arches, <s>Indra</s> banners, and flags; the reversal of hot and cold; the splitting of the earth;

children.text: nimnoccānāṃ tuṅgatā nimnatā ca[K.vā] chāyā cā[K.vā] 'rkasya ''bhimukhyena yātā//
children.translated_text: high ground becoming low and low ground becoming high; and the shadow of the sun going in the opposite direction—

children.text: tryahātiriktaḥ pavano 'ticaṇḍo gandharvasaṃjñasya bhavet purasya/
children.translated_text: a very fierce wind lasting more than three days would indicate [the destruction] of a <s>gandharva</s> city;

children.text: vyaktir bhavec ca 'hani tārakāṇāṃ naktaṃ ca tārāgaṇasaṃpraṇāśaḥ//
children.translated_text: the appearance of stars during the day, and the disappearance of the host of stars at night—

children.text: prāsādaveśmavasudhāśaragulmanimneṣv āvāsakā balibhujām anapatyatā vā/
children.translated_text: in palaces, houses, grounds, arrows, thickets, and low places, the dwellings of crows becoming without offspring,

children.text: ekāṇḍajatvam[K.ekātmajatvam] athavā bhuvi maṇḍalāni kurvanti cakrakam ivopari vā bhramantaḥ//
children.translated_text: or [crows] producing only one egg, or making circles on the ground, or hovering above—

children.text: ulkā 'bhighātena tamo 'tidīptyā vakrātivakrena suto dharitryāḥ/
children.translated_text: by the striking of meteors, by extreme brightness of darkness, by the extremely retrograde [motion] of the son of the earth [<s>Maṅgala</s>/Mars],

children.text: ketur gatisparśana -- dhūpanena cāreṇa pīḍāṃ kurute 'rkaputraḥ//
children.translated_text: a comet by its course, contact, and fumigation, and <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), the son of the sun, causes affliction.

children.text: tribhis tribhir bhair atha kṛttikādyair nipīḍitair[K.niṣpīḍitair] bhūpatayo 'bhiyojyāḥ/
children.translated_text: Kings associated with groups of three <s>nakṣatras</s> beginning with <s>Kṛttikā</s>, when [those stars are] afflicted, should be attacked:

children.text: pāñcālanātho magadhādhipaś ca kaliṅgarāḍ ujjayinīpatiś ca//
children.translated_text: the lord of <s>Pāñcāla</s>, the ruler of <s>Magadha</s>, the king of <s>Kaliṅga</s>, and the lord of <s>Ujjayinī</s>;

children.text: ānarttarāṭ saindhavahārahorau[K.saindhavahārahaurau] madreśvaro 'nyaś ca kuraṅganāthaḥ[K.kulindanāthaḥ]/
children.translated_text: the king of <s>Ānarta</s>, the rulers of <s>Sindhu</s> and <s>Hārahūra</s>, the lord of <s>Madra</s>, and another, the lord of <s>Kuraṅga</s>;

children.text: ete hi kūrmāṅgasamāśritānāṃ viśeṣapīḍām upayānti bhūpāḥ//
children.translated_text: these kings, who are associated with the limbs of the <s>Kūrma</s> (cosmic tortoise), undergo special affliction.

children.text: aṅgeṣu sūryo yavaneṣu candro bhaumo hy avantyāṃ magadheṣu saumyaḥ/
children.translated_text: The Sun rules <s>Aṅga</s>, the Moon the <s>Yavanas</s>, <s>Maṅgala</s> (Mars) <s>Avantī</s>, <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) <s>Magadha</s>,

children.text: sindhau gurur bhojakaṭe ca[K.bhojakaṭeṣu] śukraḥ sauraḥ surāṣṭre viṣaye babhūva//
children.translated_text: <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) <s>Sindhu</s>, <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) <s>Bhojakaṭa</s>, and <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) <s>Surāṣṭra</s>—each has its domain.

children.text: mleccheṣu ketuś ca tamaḥ kaliṅge yāto[K.jāto] yato 'taḥ paripīḍayanti[K.paripiḍitās te]/
children.translated_text: <s>Ketu</s> rules the <s>Mlecchas</s>, and <s>Rāhu</s> (the shadow) <s>Kaliṅga</s>; from whichever [direction planets] go, they afflict

children.text: svajanmadeśān paripīḍayanti tato[K.te 'to] 'bhiyojyā kṣitipena deśāḥ//
children.translated_text: their own birth-countries; therefore, those countries should be attacked by the king.

children.text: sampūjyante bhairavoccānunādai[K.bhairavoccānurāvai] raktair māṃsais tālajaṅghādayo vā/
children.translated_text: [Where] they are worshipped with terrifying loud cries, with blood, with flesh, with [offerings involving] palm-trunks and legs,

children.text: dṛśyante vā yātudhānāḥ prabhūtā bhraṣṭaśrīkaḥ so 'pi deśo 'bhiyojyaḥ//
children.translated_text: or where many <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons) are seen—that country whose glory has declined should also be attacked.

children.text: deśabhraṃśo yair nimittaiḥ pradiṣṭas tās tā vārttā vakti loke viśaṅkaḥ/
children.translated_text: The signs by which the downfall of a country has been indicated—one who fearlessly reports such news in the world,

children.text: tyaktvā deśaṃ yānti yaṃ bhikṣukā vā gamyo deśo so 'py asādhupravṛttaḥ//
children.translated_text: or a country which mendicants leave—that country of bad conduct is also [ripe] to be attacked.

children.text: rogābhibhūtaṃ viṣadūṣitaṃ vā yathā vināśābhimukhaṃ śarīram/
children.translated_text: Just as a body overcome by disease or corrupted by poison, facing destruction,

children.text: vaidyaḥ prayogaiḥ sudṛḍhaṃ karoti rāṣṭraṃ tathā śāntibhir agrajanmā//E23
children.translated_text: is made firm by a physician through treatments, so a kingdom [is restored] by a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> through <s>śānti</s> (pacification) rites.

children.text: dehaḥ kośo yoddhā vāhyaṃ mantraḥ śatrur mārgo 'py āyuḥ/
children.translated_text: The body is the treasury, the warrior is the conveyance, the counsel is the enemy, the path is also the lifespan,

children.text: cittaṃ karma prāptir mantrī prāglagnādyā bhāvāś cintyāḥ//
children.translated_text: the mind is <s>karma</s> (action), the attainment is the minister—the houses beginning with the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant) should be considered [in this order].

children.text: trilābhavarjaṃ ravisauribhaumā[K.ravisaurabhaumā] nighnanti no karmaṇi sūryabhaumau[K.sūryabhaumāḥ]/
children.translated_text: The Sun, <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), and <s>Maṅgala</s> (Mars), except in the three gain [houses], destroy; the Sun and Mars [especially so] in action;

children.text: puṣṇanti saumyā ripurāśivarjyam astaṃ[K.ripurāśivarjam na 'staṃ] bhṛgur mṛtyuvilagnam induḥ//
children.translated_text: the benefics nourish, except in the enemy's sign; <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) in the setting [house], <s>Candra</s> (Moon) in the death and ascendant [houses] [are harmful].

children.text: tithyudgamendukaraṇarkṣadinakṣaṇeṣu śuddheṣv[K.pāpeṣv] abhīṣṭaphaladā nṛpater yathā syāt/
children.translated_text: When the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), the rising, the Moon, the <s>karaṇa</s>, the <s>nakṣatra</s>, the day, and the moment are pure,

children.text: yātrā tathā param idaṃ kathayāmi guhyaṃ śiṣyāya nai 'tad acirād hy uṣitāya dadyāt//
children.translated_text: the military expedition will yield the desired fruit for the king. I shall now tell this supreme secret; one should not give it to a student who has not stayed long [in study].

children.text: yogaiḥ kṣitipā vinirgatāḥ śakunais taskaracāraṇādayaḥ/
children.translated_text: Kings set out [successfully] by [astrological] <s>yogas</s> (combinations); thieves and spies by omens;

children.text: nakṣatrabalair[K.nakṣatraguṇair] dvijātayaḥ kṣaṇavīryād itaro jano 'rthabhāk//
children.translated_text: <s>brāhmaṇas</s> by the power of <s>nakṣatras</s>; other people gain their objectives by the power of the moment.

children.text: yad yad yogavaśād vrajaty agadatāṃ dravyair viṣaṃ yojitam
children.translated_text: Just as poison combined with substances becomes a cure through [astrological] <s>yogas</s>,

children.text: saṃyuktaṃ madhunā ghṛtaṃ ca viṣatāṃ gacched[K.gacchad] yathā dṛśyate/
children.translated_text: and just as ghee combined with honey is seen to become poisonous,

children.text: tadvad yogasamudbhavaṃ prakurute hitvā grahaḥ svaṃ phalaṃ
children.translated_text: so a planet, abandoning its own result, produces [effects] born of [astrological] <s>yogas</s>—

children.text: yasmāt tena samudyato 'smi gadituṃ yogān vicitrān imān//
children.translated_text: therefore I have undertaken to describe these various <s>yogas</s>.

children.text: lagne gurur budhabhṛgū hibukātmajasthau ṣaṣṭhau kujārkatanayau dinakṛt tṛtīyaḥ/
children.translated_text: When <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) is in the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) and <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) in the fourth and fifth houses, <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) and <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) in the sixth, the Sun in the third,

children.text: candraś ca yasya daśamo bhavati prayāṇe tasya 'bhivāñchitaphalāptir alaṃ nṛpasya//
children.translated_text: and the Moon in the tenth at the time of departure—that king fully obtains the desired result.

children.text: horātṛtīyaripulābhagataiḥ krameṇa jīvārkibhaumaravibhir bhṛguje 'nukūle/
children.translated_text: When <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), <s>Maṅgala</s> (Mars), and the Sun are positioned in the ascendant, third, sixth, and eleventh houses respectively, with <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) and Mercury favorable,

children.text: yāto 'tidṛptam api śatrubalaṃ nihanti naiśaṃ tamisram iva tigmam ayūkhakālī[K.ayūkhamālī]//
children.translated_text: one who has set out destroys even the most formidable enemy army, as the brilliant sun [destroys] the darkness of night.

children.text: udayārinabhaḥ sthalagair[K.udayārinabhasthalagair] dinakṛdyamaśītakaraiḥ/
children.translated_text: When the Sun, <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), and the Moon occupy the ascendant, sixth, tenth, and fourth houses,

children.text: na bhavanty arayo 'bhimukhā hariṇā iva keśariṇaḥ//
children.translated_text: enemies do not stand before [the king], like deer before a lion.

children.text: gurur udaye ripurāśigato 'rko yadi nidhane na ca[K.ca na] śītamayūkhaḥ/
children.translated_text: When <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) is in the ascendant and the Sun in an enemy's sign, or in the seventh house, and the Moon is not [there],

children.text: bhavati gato 'tra śaśī 'va narendro ripuvanitānanatāmarasānām//
children.translated_text: the king who has set out in this [configuration] becomes [like the bee] to the lotus-faces of his enemies' wives.

children.text: śukavākpatibudhair dhanasaṃsthaiḥ saptame śaśini lagnagate 'rke/
children.translated_text: When <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), the lord of speech [<s>Guru</s>/Jupiter], and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) are in the second house, the Moon in the seventh, and the Sun in the ascendant,

children.text: nirgato nṛpatir eti kṛtārtho vainateyavad ahiṃ[K.arīn] vinigṛhya//
children.translated_text: the king who has set out achieves his purpose, subduing enemies like <s>Garuḍa</s> [subdues] serpents.

children.text: mūrttivittasahajeṣu saṃsthitāḥ śukracandrasutatigmaraśmayaḥ/
children.translated_text: When <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), the Moon, <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), and the Sun are stationed in the first, second, and third houses,

children.text: yasya yānasamaye raṇānale tasya yānti śalabhā iva 'rayaḥ//
children.translated_text: at the time of his departure, the enemies of that [king] enter the fire of battle like moths.

children.text: sūryendū valavarjitau valayutau janmeśalagneśvarau
children.translated_text: When the Sun and Moon are without strength [but] with strength, [when] the lords of the birth [sign] and ascendant [are favorable],

children.text: pātāle daśame 'pi vā śaśisuto lagnasthito vākpatiḥ/
children.translated_text: when the son of the Moon [<s>Budha</s>/Mercury] is in the fourth or tenth house, and the lord of speech [<s>Guru</s>/Jupiter] is in the ascendant,

children.text: ṣaṭsaptāṣṭamavarjiteṣu bhṛgujaḥ sthāneṣu yasya sthito
children.translated_text: when <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) is positioned in houses other than the sixth, seventh, and eighth,

children.text: yātus tasya na vidviṣo raṇamukhe tiṣṭhanti yoṣā iva//
children.translated_text: the enemies of that departing [king] do not stand in the face of battle, like women.

children.text: saure bhaume[K.vā] lagnage 'rphe[K.'rke] khamadhye karmaṇy āye[K.vā] bhārgave candraje ca/
children.translated_text: When <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) or <s>Maṅgala</s> (Mars) is in the ascendant, the Sun in the mid-heaven, <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) in the tenth or eleventh,

children.text: yāyād bhūpaḥ[K.bhūpālaḥ] śatrudeśaṃ nihantuṃ dṛptaṃ śatruṃ[K.vā] kālavat[K.kālayat] krūraceṣṭaḥ//
children.translated_text: the king should march to destroy the enemy's country, crushing the proud enemy like Death, with fierce deeds.

children.text: lābhaśatrusahajeṣu yamārau saumyaśukraguravo balayuktāḥ/
children.translated_text: When <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) and <s>Maṅgala</s> (Mars) are in the eleventh, sixth, and third houses, and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), and <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) are endowed with strength,

children.text: gacchato yadi tato 'sya dharitrī sāgarāmburasanā vaśam eti//
children.translated_text: if they are behind him as he goes, then the earth with its ocean-bordered waters comes under his control.

children.text: pāpās tṛtīye hibuke ? jīvo bilagne śaśalāñchano 'ste/
children.translated_text: When malefics are in the third and fourth houses, <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) is in the ascendant, and the Moon is in the seventh house,

children.text: yasyodyame tasya balaṃ ripūṇāṃ kṛtaṃ kṛtaghnesv iva yāt nāśam//
children.translated_text: at the time of that [king's] departure, the strength of his enemies goes to destruction, like a favor done to ungrateful people.

children.text: candre 'stage devagurau vilagne jñaśukrayoḥ karmaṇi lābhage 'rke/
children.translated_text: When the Moon is in the seventh, the divine preceptor [<s>Guru</s>/Jupiter] in the ascendant, <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) and <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) in the tenth, the Sun in the eleventh,

children.text: saurārayor bhrātṛgayoś ca yāto nṛpaḥ svabhṛtyān iva śāsti śatrūn//
children.translated_text: and <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) and <s>Maṅgala</s> (Mars) in the third and sixth—the king who has set out commands his enemies as if they were his own servants.

children.text: gurau vilagne yadi vā śaśāṅke ṣaṣṭhe ravau karmagate 'rkaputre/
children.translated_text: When <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) or the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the sixth, <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) in the tenth,

children.text: sitajñayor bandhusutasthayoś ca yātrā janitrī 'va hitāni dhatte//
children.translated_text: and <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) in the fourth and fifth—the military expedition yields benefits like a mother.

children.text: patyau girāṃ lagnagate 'vaśeṣair ekādaśārthopagatair yiyāsoḥ/
children.translated_text: When the lord of speech [<s>Guru</s>/Jupiter] is placed in the ascendant, and the remaining [planets] occupy the eleventh and second houses for the one wishing to depart,

children.text: vidāryate śatrubalaṃ samantād dharmo yathā hetuśatair yugānte//
children.translated_text: the enemy's army is torn apart on all sides, as <s>dharma</s> [is destroyed] by a hundred arguments at the end of an age.

children.text: triṣaṇṇavāntyeṣv abalaḥ śaśāṅkaś cāndrir balī yasya guruś ca kendre/
children.translated_text: When the Moon is weak in the third, sixth, ninth, and twelfth [houses], the son of the Moon [<s>Budha</s>/Mercury] is strong, and <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) is in an angle,

children.text: tasya 'riyoṣābharaṇaiḥ priyāṇi priyāḥ priyāṇāṃ janayanti sainye//
children.translated_text: the beloved women [of the enemy], adorned with the ornaments of enemy women, produce joy for the beloveds of [that king's] army.

children.text: kendropagatena vīkṣite guruṇā trayāyacaturthage site/
children.translated_text: When <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) occupying an angle aspects [the horoscope], with <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) in the third, fourth [houses],

children.text: pāpair anavāṣṭasaptamair[K.anavāṣṭasaptagair] vasu kiṃ tan na yad āpnuyād gataḥ//
children.translated_text: with malefics not in the sixth, seventh, or eighth—what wealth would one not obtain upon departing?

children.text: lagnārikarmahibukeṣu śubhekṣite jñe dyūnāntyalagnarahiteṣv aśubhagraheṣu/
children.translated_text: When <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) aspected by benefics is in the ascendant, sixth, tenth, or fourth houses, and malefics are absent from the seventh, twelfth, and ascendant,

children.text: yātur bhayaṃ na bhavati prataret samudraṃ yady aśmanā[K.'pi] kim uta śatrusamāgameṣu[K.uta 'risamāgameṣu]//
children.translated_text: there is no danger for the departing one; he could cross the ocean on a stone, let alone [succeed] in encounters with enemies.

children.text: yasyo 'dayāstāricatustrisaṃsthāḥ śukrāṅgiro 'ṅgāraka --- saumyasaurāḥ/
children.translated_text: He whose [horoscope has] <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Maṅgala</s> (Mars), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), and <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) positioned in the ascendant, seventh, sixth, fourth, third, and [other houses]—

children.text: dviṣadbalastrīvadanāni tasya klāntāni kāntān avalokayanti//
children.translated_text: the weary and beautiful faces of his enemies' women gaze upon their beloved ones [departing for war].

children.text: pūrvoktayoge dhanago budhaś cec chaśāṅkasūryau ca daśāyasaṃsthau/
children.translated_text: In the aforementioned <s>yoga</s>, if <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) is in the second house, and the Moon and Sun are in the tenth and eleventh,

children.text: asmin gatasya 'likulopagītā nānāvanotthā dviradā bhavanti//
children.translated_text: for one who has set out in this [configuration], the elephants [he captures] become like those sung by swarms of bees in various forests.

children.text: sūryādayo 'risahajāmbaraśatrulagnabandhvāyagāḥ suraguror divasaś ca[K.divaso 'pi] yasya/
children.translated_text: He whose [chart has] the Sun and other [planets] in the sixth, third, tenth, sixth, ascendant, fourth, and eleventh houses, and it is the day of the divine preceptor [<s>Guru</s>/Jupiter, i.e., Thursday],

children.text: yāne 'risainyam upagacchati tasya nāśaṃ ma māṃsakaśravaṇakeṣv[K.mīmāṃsakaśravaṇakeṣv] iva tīrthapuṇyam//
children.translated_text: when he sets out, the enemy's army meets destruction, like the merit of holy places [is destroyed] among the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> and <s>Śravaṇakas</s>.

children.text: trinidhanatanusaptamārisaṃsthāḥ kujasitajīvabudhā raviś ca yasya/
children.translated_text: When <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), and the Sun occupy the third, seventh, first, seventh, and sixth houses,

children.text: khalajanajanite 'va lokayātrā na bhavati yasya cirāya śatrusenā//
children.translated_text: the enemy's army does not last long, like the livelihood of the world produced by wicked people.

children.text: kujaravijayute 'ribhe[K.'tibhe] gatānāṃ sukhasahajopagatiḥ sitārkajīvaiḥ/
children.translated_text: When <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) and the Sun are victorious, occupying the sixth sign, and <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), and <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) enter the fourth and third,

children.text: ripubalam[K.parabalam] upayāti nāśam āśu śrutam adhanasya kuṭumbacintayaiva[K.kuṭumbacintaye 'va]//
children.translated_text: the enemy's army quickly meets destruction, like the wealth of a poor man consumed by family worries alone.

children.text: lagnatridharmāridaśāyageṣu sitārkijīvendukujendujeṣu/
children.translated_text: When <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), the Moon, <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) are in the ascendant, third, ninth, sixth, tenth, and eleventh houses,

children.text: sārke budhe ca 'ribalaṃ vināśam āyāti guhyaṃ piśuneṣv ivo 'ktam//
children.translated_text: together with <s>Maṅgala</s> (Mars) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), the enemy's army goes to destruction, like a secret [spoken] among tale-bearers.

children.text: ekāntararkṣe bhṛgujāt kujād vā saumye sthite sūryasutād guror vā/
children.translated_text: When <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) is stationed one sign away from <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) or <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), or from <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) or <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter),

children.text: pradhvasyate[K.pradhvaṃsate] 'rir na cirād gatasya veṣādhiko bhṛtya ive ''śvarasya//
children.translated_text: the enemy of the departing [king] is destroyed before long, like an overdressed servant [is dismissed] by his master.

children.text: ekāntarā yadi gatā bhaveneṣu ṣaṭsu pṛṣṭhasthitasya[K.pṛṣṭhasthitaś ca] suraśatruguroḥ[K.suraśatruguruḥ] prayāṇe/
children.translated_text: If [the planets] are placed one sign apart in six houses, with the teacher of the <s>Asuras</s> [<s>Śukra</s>/Venus] behind [the king] at departure,

children.text: yātasya nātra ripavo prahasanti vīryaṃ viṣṇor ivoddhṛtagadārathavādapāṇeḥ//
children.translated_text: the enemies of the departing one do not laugh at [his] valor—like those [who face] <s>Viṣṇu</s> with his mace, chariot, and conch in hand.

children.text: nirantaram yadi bhavaneṣu pañcasu grahāḥ sthitā divasakareṇa varjitāḥ/
children.translated_text: If the planets, excluding the Sun, are placed continuously in five houses,

children.text: yiyāsator[K.yiyāsato] yadi ca bhavanti pṛṣṭhatas tadā parān balabhid iva 'vakṛntati//
children.translated_text: and if they are behind the one wishing to depart, then he cuts down his foes as <s>Indra</s> the Destroyer of Fortresses [cuts down his enemies].

children.text: bṛguputramahendragurū gamane sahitau yadi bhaṃ yugapat tyajataḥ/
children.translated_text: If <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), and <s>Mahendra</s> [the Sun] simultaneously leave a <s>nakṣatra</s> together when setting out,

children.text: jñagurū yadi vā 'ṃśakam ekagatau[K.ekam itau] samare surarāḍ[K.amararāḍ] iva bhāti tadā//
children.translated_text: or if <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) and <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) occupy the same <s>aṃśa</s> (degree), then [the king] shines in battle like <s>Indra</s>, the king of the gods.

children.text: nistriṃśavakropagate ca vakre vakreṇa vakraṃ nṛpatiṃ[K.nṛpatir] nihanyāt/
children.translated_text: And when <s>Vakra</s> (Mars, retrograde) is positioned in [the sign of] swords and curves, the retrograde [planet] would slay a king [who is himself] crooked,

children.text: pānaprasaktaṃ niśi vā prasuptaṃ tasyai 'va ca 'ste yadi vā 'ṃśakaḥ syāt//
children.translated_text: either one addicted to drink or asleep at night, or if its <s>aṃśaka</s> (degree-subdivision) falls in that very [sign].

children.text: putro dharitryā dinakṛt sutaś ca yadā tyajetāṃ yugapan navāṃśam/
children.translated_text: When the son of the earth (<s>Mars</s>) and the son of the day-maker (<s>Saturn</s>) simultaneously leave the <s>navāṃśa</s> (ninth-part division),

children.text: tadā hy avaskandagato narendro bhuṅkte ripūn tārkṣya iva dvijihvān//
children.translated_text: then the king, having descended upon [the enemy], devours his foes as <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) devours serpents.

children.text: budhabhārgavamadhyagate himagau hibukopagate ca nṛpaḥ praviśan[K.pravasan]/
children.translated_text: When the moon is positioned between <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) and <s>Bhārgava</s> (Venus), and also when positioned in the fourth house (<s>hibuka</s>), the king setting forth

children.text: puruhūtadiśaṃ yadi vā 'ntakṛtaḥ puruhūtayamapratimo bhavati//
children.translated_text: in the direction of <s>Puruhūta</s> (<s>Indra</s>, the east) or of <s>Antakṛt</s> (<s>Yama</s>, the south) becomes unequaled like <s>Indra</s> and <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: sitendujau caturthagau niśākaraś ca saptame/
children.translated_text: When Venus and the Moon are in the fourth house, and the Moon is in the seventh,

children.text: yadā tadā gato nṛpaḥ praśāsty arīn vinā raṇān[K.raṇāt]//
children.translated_text: then the king who has set forth rules over his enemies without battles.

children.text: śaśini caturthagṛhaṃ samupete budhasahite 'stagate bhṛguputre/
children.translated_text: When the Moon has reached the fourth house, accompanied by <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), and the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) has set,

children.text: gamanam avāpya patir manujānāṃ jayati ripūn samareṇa vinai 'va//
children.translated_text: the lord of men, having undertaken his march, conquers his enemies without battle itself.

children.text: kṣititanayayutān navāṃśakād yadi śatame[K.śatago] bhṛgujo 'thavā guruḥ/
children.translated_text: If the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) or <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), conjoined with the son of the earth (<s>Mars</s>), is in the hundredth <s>navāṃśa</s>,

children.text: śataguṇam api hanty arer balaṃ viṣam iva kāyam asṛkpathopapannam[K.asṛkpathopagam]//
children.translated_text: he destroys even a hundredfold army of the enemy, as poison [destroys] a body that has entered the path of the blood.

children.text: śatāṃśakād ūrdhvam avasthite budhe yamārayos tatra gatasya bhūbhṛtaḥ/
children.translated_text: When <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) is positioned beyond the hundredth degree-subdivision, and the king is positioned in the [house] of <s>Yama</s> (eighth) and enemies,

children.text: prayāti nāśaṃ samare dviṣaḍ balaṃ yathā 'rthibhāvopagatasya gauravam//
children.translated_text: the army of the foe goes to destruction in battle, just as the dignity of one who has fallen into the state of a beggar.

children.text: nakṣatram ekaṃ yugapat praviṣṭau yadā dharitrītanayāmarejyau/
children.translated_text: When the son of the earth (<s>Mars</s>) and <s>Amarejya</s> (Jupiter) simultaneously enter the same <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion),

children.text: kuryāt tadā 'ntaṃ dviṣatāṃ balasya drauṇir yathā 'rer niśi sauptikena//
children.translated_text: then [the king] would make an end of the enemy's army, as <s>Drauṇi</s> (<s>Aśvatthāman</s>) [destroyed the enemy] at night by the nocturnal raid (<s>sauptika</s>).

children.text: ṛkṣaṃ gurujñau budhabhārgvau vā yadā praviṣṭau yugapat sametau/
children.translated_text: When <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) and <s>Jña</s> (Mercury), or <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) and <s>Bhārgava</s> (Venus), simultaneously enter the same <s>ṛkṣa</s> (asterism),

children.text: arthān avāpnoti tadā vicitrān chātraḥ sutīrthān[K.sutīrthād] gurupūjayaiva[K.gurupūjaye 'va]//
children.translated_text: then [the king] obtains various riches, as a student [obtains them] from a good co-disciple through the worship of the teacher alone.

children.text: yātrādigīśād yadi pañcame 'nyo gṛhe graho vīryayuto 'vatiṣṭhet/
children.translated_text: If another planet endowed with strength is positioned in the fifth house from the lord of the direction of the campaign,

children.text: samudyatāśākathitāni bhaṅktvā phalāni vīryān nayati svakāṣṭhām//
children.translated_text: it overturns the results declared by the rising sign and, by its strength, leads [affairs] toward its own direction.

children.text: eko 'pi jīvajñasitāsitānāṃ kujāt trikoṇe ravito 'tha ve 'nduḥ/
children.translated_text: If even one among <s>Jīva</s> (Jupiter), <s>Jña</s> (Mercury), <s>Sita</s> (Venus), or <s>Asita</s> (Saturn) is in trine from <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), or the Sun or the Moon,

children.text: yatro 'dyatas tatra na yāti yātā tayor balīyān nayati svakāṣṭhām//
children.translated_text: from the place where the campaign is launched, the campaigner does not go [in vain]; the stronger of those two leads [affairs] toward its own direction.

children.text: janmodayarkṣaṃ hibukāstasaṃsthaṃ yasya 'śubhair dṛṣṭayutaṃ na saumyaiḥ/
children.translated_text: He whose birth-<s>nakṣatra</s> or rising-<s>nakṣatra</s> is positioned in the fourth or seventh house (<s>hibuka</s> or <s>asta</s>), aspected or conjoined by malefics and not by benefics—

children.text: sa śāṇḍilīṃ prāpya yathā garutmān danyaṃ[K.dainyaṃ] gato 'bhyeti hatasvapakṣaḥ//
children.translated_text: like <s>Garutmān</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) who, having encountered <s>Śāṇḍilī</s>, went to wretchedness with his own wings broken.

children.text: horāṣṭame janmagṛhāṣṭame vā svāc chatrubhāc chatrugṛhodaye vā/
children.translated_text: In the eighth from the <s>horā</s> (hour-lord), in the eighth from the birth-house, in the rising of the enemy-house from one's own enemy-house,

children.text: tadrāśipair vā gamanaṃ vilagne tulyaṃ narāṇāṃ viṣabhakṣaṇena//
children.translated_text: or with the lords of those signs in the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant)—departure for men is equal to eating poison.

children.text: ripunidhanavilagne svāt triṣaḍlābhage vā
children.translated_text: When the enemy, death, and <s>lagna</s> [houses] from one's own are the third, sixth, or eleventh [houses],

children.text: balavati bhavaneśe sve kṛśe śatrupakṣe/
children.translated_text: when the lord of one's own house is strong and the enemy's side is weak,

children.text: anabhimukhadigīśe dikpatau susthite ca
children.translated_text: when the lord of the direction is not facing [the enemy's] direction, and the lord of the direction is well-placed,

children.text: vrajati yadi yatheṣṭaṃ prāpnuyāt tatra yatā//
children.translated_text: if one marches, the campaigner would obtain [success] as desired.

children.text: kendratrikoṇeṣu śubhāḥ praśastās teṣv eva pāpā na śubhapradāḥ syuḥ/
children.translated_text: Benefics in the <s>kendra</s> (angular) and <s>trikoṇa</s> (trine) houses are auspicious; malefics in those very [houses] would not bestow good results.

children.text: papo 'pi kāmaṃ balavan niyojyaḥ kendreṣu śūnyaṃ na śivāya kendram[K.lagnam]//
children.translated_text: Even a malefic, if strong, should be employed in the <s>kendras</s>; a <s>kendra</s> that is empty is not auspicious.

children.text: saumyaiś ca pāpaiś ca catuṣṭayasthaḥ kṛcchreṇa siddhiṃ samupaiti yātā/
children.translated_text: The campaigner whose [ascendant] is occupied by both benefics and malefics attains success with difficulty,

children.text: prapātapātapratighātavakrair[K.prapātayānapratighātavakrā] nadī 'va dhātrīdharakandareṣu//
children.translated_text: like a river in mountain gorges, with cascades, falls, obstructions, and bends.

children.text: guro[K.gurau] vilagne bhṛguje 'risaṃsthe candre 'ṣṭame hanti gato 'risenām/
children.translated_text: When <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) is in the <s>lagna</s> and the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) is in the sixth house, with the Moon in the eighth, [the king] who has marched destroys the enemy army,

children.text: viṣṭaṃ[K.vṛṣṭiṃ] yathā dakṣiṇamārgacārī rūkṣo athavā[K.yadā] hrasvatanuś ca śukraḥ//
children.translated_text: like the rain when <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) is moving on the southern path, or when [Venus] is dry and diminished in body.

children.text: siṃhājataulimithunā[K.siṃhājataulimithunaṃ] mṛgakarkaṭau ca sveśānvitā yadi bhavati[K.bhavati] yasya śaniś ca lagne/
children.translated_text: If <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) with its own lord is in the <s>lagna</s> in Leo, Virgo, Libra, Gemini, Capricorn, or Cancer,

children.text: tatsainikāḥ parabalaṃ ksapayanti yātur mūrkhasya vittam iva cāraṇacāṭukārāḥ[K.cāraṇacāṭacakṣāḥ(?)]//
children.translated_text: the soldiers of that campaigner destroy the enemy's army, as flatterers and minstrels [destroy] the wealth of a fool.

children.text: udaye gurusaumyabhārgavaiḥ sahaje 'rkārkikujaiś ca gacchataḥ/
children.translated_text: With <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Saumya</s> (Mercury), and <s>Bhārgava</s> (Venus) in the ascendant, and the Sun, <s>Ārkī</s> (Saturn), and <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) in the third house, for one who marches,

children.text: na bhavanty arayo raṇe sthirāḥ kitavānām iva vittasaṃcayāḥ//
children.translated_text: enemies do not stand firm in battle, like the accumulated wealth of gamblers.

children.text: jātakoktanṛpayogagatānām pratyahaṃ[K.pratidinam] bhavati rājyavivṛddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: For those who have attained the royal <s>yogas</s> stated in <s>Jātaka</s> (nativity), there is daily increase of dominion,

children.text: vātaghūrṇitam iva 'rṇavayānam parabalaṃ hi samupaiti vināśam//
children.translated_text: for the enemy's army goes to destruction, like a ship on the ocean tossed by the wind.

children.text: horā''śrite[K.horāśrite] devagurau prayātā krūragrahaiḥ karmaṇi lābhagair vā/
children.translated_text: When the divine teacher (<s>Guru</s>/Jupiter) occupies the <s>horā</s> and [the king] has set forth, with cruel planets in the tenth or eleventh house,

children.text: kṛtvā ripūṇāṃ kṣayam akṣatāṅgaḥ svayaṃ[K.kṣayaṃ] kṣitīśo 'kṣayakośam eti[K.'kṣayakośa aiti]//
children.translated_text: having accomplished the destruction of his enemies with limbs unharmed, the lord of the earth himself attains an inexhaustible treasury.

children.text: lābhārthalagneṣu śubhā raviḥ khe yasya ''rasaurau sahaje 'ribhe vā/
children.translated_text: For one who has benefics in the eleventh, first (<s>lagna</s>), and [other houses], with the Sun in the sky, and Mars and Saturn in the third or sixth house,

children.text: tasya 'rthakośaḥ samupaiti vṛddhiṃ lābho[K.lobho] yathā pratyaham arthavṛddhyā//
children.translated_text: his treasury of wealth attains increase, as greed [increases] daily through the growth of wealth.

children.text: svoccapagair jīvakujārkajārkair ebhyas tribhir vā kathitaikalagne/
children.translated_text: With <s>Jīva</s> (Jupiter), <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>Ārkaja</s> (Saturn), and <s>Arka</s> (Sun) in their exaltation, or with three of these in one ascendant,

children.text: rājñaḥ praṇāśaṃ samupaiti śatruḥ saukhyaṃ dvibhāryasya yathā 'dhanasya//
children.translated_text: the enemy of the king goes to destruction, like the happiness of a penniless man with two wives.

children.text: eko 'pi jīvārkakujārkajānāṃ svocce vilagne svagṛhe yadī 'nduḥ/
children.translated_text: Even if one among <s>Jīva</s> (Jupiter), <s>Arka</s> (Sun), <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), or <s>Ārkaja</s> (Saturn) is in its exaltation in the <s>lagna</s>, with the Moon in its own house,

children.text: jātasya[K.yātasya] yānty atra parāḥ praṇāśam mahākulānī 'va kuṭumbabhedaiḥ//
children.translated_text: the enemies of the one who has marched go to destruction, like great families through the divisions of the household.

children.text: lagnāc caturthe atibale śaśāṅke[K.vibalaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ] yogād vinā candrabalena yātā[K.yātaḥ]/
children.translated_text: When the Moon is exceedingly strong in the fourth from the <s>lagna</s>, [the king] who has marched by the strength of the Moon alone, without [other] <s>yogas</s>,

children.text: labdhā 'pi lakṣmīṃ bahuratnapūrṇāṃ[K.lakṣmīr bahuratnapūrṇā] kṣipraṃ kṣayaṃ yāti yathā śaśāṅkaḥ//
children.translated_text: even the prosperity obtained, full of many jewels, quickly goes to decay, just as the Moon [wanes].

children.text: yeṣāṃ game navamapañcamakaṇṭakasthāḥ saumyās tṛtīyaripulābhagatāś ca pāpāḥ/
children.translated_text: Those whose march has benefics in the ninth, fifth, and <s>kendra</s> positions, and malefics in the third, sixth, and eleventh positions,

children.text: āyānti te svabhavanāni punaḥ kṛtārthā dattā dvijātiṣu purā vidhivad yathārthāḥ//
children.translated_text: they return to their own homes having accomplished their purpose, like wealth given to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> according to proper rites that returns in due course.

children.text: pūrvāditas triparivartagatair ajādyair bhaiḥ saptakair analabhāc ca gamo jayāya/
children.translated_text: With the signs beginning from Aries in three rotations from the east, march in the seven [asterisms] from <s>Anala</s> (Kṛttikā) is [conducive] to victory,

children.text: vāyuagnidiksthaparighasya samārddhagaiś ca maitrāśvihastagurubheṣu ca sarvadikṣu//
children.translated_text: and also with those at the half-positions of the <s>parigha</s> (barrier) placed in the wind-fire direction, and in [the asterisms] <s>Maitrā</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, and those of <s>Guru</s> in all directions.

children.text: pūrveṇāindraṃ[K.pūrveṇāi ''ndraṃ] dakṣiṇena ''japādaṃ rohiṇyo 'taś ca 'ryamākhyaṃ ca śūlam/
children.translated_text: From the east, the <s>Aindra</s> [asterism]; from the south, <s>Ajapāda</s>; from <s>Rohiṇī</s> onward, the <s>śūla</s> (trident) called <s>Āryaman</s>.

children.text: kāmaṃ yāyāt sāmparāyeṣu kāryeṣv evaṃ dvāre[K.advāre 'pi] projjhya śūlāni tāni//
children.translated_text: One may go freely in matters of life-and-death urgency, having disregarded those <s>śūla</s> tridents, even at the doorless [times].

children.text: vivarjayet tvāṣṭrayamoragāṇām ardham dvitīyaṃ gamane jayepsuḥ/
children.translated_text: One who desires victory in march should avoid the second half of [the asterisms] of <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> (Citrā), <s>Yama</s> (Bharaṇī), and <s>Raga</s> (Revatī),

children.text: pūrvārdham āgneyamaghānilānāṃ svātīm[K.svātim] maghāṃ co 'śanasaḥ samastām//
children.translated_text: the first half of <s>Āgneya</s> (Kṛttikā), <s>Maghā</s>, and <s>Anila</s> (Svāti), and the entirety of <s>Svāti</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, and <s>Uśanas</s> (Śatabhiṣaj).

children.text: utpātapāpagrahapīḍite bhe ye yānti bhūrigrahasaṃyute vā/
children.translated_text: Those who march when the <s>nakṣatra</s> is afflicted by portents, evil planets, or conjoined with many planets,

children.text: te pūrvavittāny api nāśayanti dhātuprasaktā iva mūrttikendrāḥ[K.vārtikendrāḥ]//
children.translated_text: they destroy even their prior wealth, like those addicted to minerals [destroy] the core of their bodies.

children.text: ravisitakujarāhusauricandrā[K.ravisitakujarāhusauracandrā] jñaguruyutāḥ purataḥ kramād digīśāḥ/
children.translated_text: The Sun, Venus, Mars, <s>Rāhu</s>, Saturn, Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter are the lords of directions in order from the front.

children.text: vrajati yadi lalāṭage digīśe patati tato drumavat sarittaṭātsaḥ[K.sarittaṭasthaḥ]//
children.translated_text: If the lord of the direction is in the forehead [position, i.e., the front], [the king] who marches falls from there like a tree from a riverbank.

children.text: yāto 'yanasya pratilomakāṣṭhāṃ yaḥ syāt svatantro[K.sutantro] 'pi jitaḥ pareṣāṃ/
children.translated_text: One who has marched against the direction of the <s>ayana</s> (solstice), even if self-reliant, is conquered by others,

children.text: sa kevalavyākaraṇābhiyuktaḥ[K.kevalaṃ] vyākaraṇābhiyuktaḥ kāvyajñagoṣṭhyām iva hāsyam eti//
children.translated_text: like one skilled only in grammar who becomes a laughingstock in an assembly of poets.

children.text: ayanena gato 'rkasomayor dyuniśaṃ vā sthitayoḥ pṛthak pṛthak/
children.translated_text: One who has marched in the <s>ayana</s> of the Sun and Moon, or while they are stationed separately by day and night,

children.text: viduṣām iva sarvaśāstravit[K.śabdaśāstravit] samavāye dviṣatāṃ virājate//
children.translated_text: shines among the enemy host, like one versed in all <s>śāstras</s> in an assembly of scholars.

children.text: tithiṃ caturthīṃ navamīṃ caturdaśīṃ vihāya viṣṭiṃ karaṇaṃ ca gacchataḥ/
children.translated_text: Avoiding the fourth, ninth, and fourteenth <s>tithis</s> (lunar days), and the <s>viṣṭi</s> (inauspicious) <s>karaṇa</s>, for one who marches,

children.text: bhavanti cāmīkaravājivāraṇāś caturthipūrvāś ca tadāptivāraṇāḥ//
children.translated_text: there come gold, horses, and elephants; and the fourth and preceding [tithis] are also preventers of [the enemy's] gains.

children.text: ṛkṣe[K.rikte] tithau vā vyatipātaduṣṭe yo yāti mohāt khalu vaidhṛte vā/
children.translated_text: One who marches from delusion on an empty <s>tithi</s>, or one afflicted by <s>Vyatipāta</s> or <s>Vaidhṛti</s>,

children.text: sa nāśam āyāty acireṇa yātā[K.rājā] rāje 'va daivajñavilomaceṣṭaḥ//
children.translated_text: that campaigner comes to destruction swiftly, like a king whose actions are contrary to the astrologer's [advice].

children.text: ārogyam ṛkṣeṇa dhanaṃ kṣaṇena kāryasya siddhis tithinā śubhena/
children.translated_text: Health [is determined] by the <s>nakṣatra</s>, wealth by the <s>kṣaṇa</s> (moment), success of the undertaking by the auspicious <s>tithi</s>,

children.text: rāśyudgamena 'dhvani siddhim āhuḥ prāyaḥ śubhāni[K.sukhāni] kṣaṇadākareṇa//
children.translated_text: success on the journey by the rising sign—they say that auspiciousness [comes] mostly from the Moon.

body.text: na rājate bhūriguṇānvitā 'pi vyarhtabyayasya kṣitipasya yātrā/
body.translated_text: Even if endowed with many virtues, the campaign of a king with wasted expenditure does not shine,
like the wedding procession of an old man afflicted [with age], proud of his wealth, when <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) has disappeared.

children.text: pratiśukrabudhāśanivṛṣṭihatā dig adhaḥ kurute nṛpatiṃ gamane/
children.translated_text: A direction that is struck by counter-Venus, Mercury, thunder, or rain brings the king low on his march,

children.text: madirāmuditā madanākulitā pramade 'va kulam paraveśmaratā//
children.translated_text: like a woman delighted by wine, agitated by passion, and given to the homes of others brings her family [low] through her wantonness.

children.text: vīryānvitair yāyibhir ātmabhadraiḥ kleśaṃ[K.kleśed] vinā hanti camūm arīṇām/
children.translated_text: [A king] with valiant, self-disciplined soldiers destroys the army of enemies without hardship,

children.text: trailokyalābhe 'py asamāptakāryāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ yathā cīraphalāmbutuṣṭaḥ//
