children.translated_text: like one satisfied with bark-garments, fruits, and water [destroys] the thirst for unfinished desires even in gaining the three worlds.

children.text: sarpis tilaudanaṣaiḥ[K.tilodanajhaṣaiḥ] payasā ca bhuktvā pūrvādi vāraṇarathāśvanarair gatasya/
children.translated_text: Having eaten ghee, sesame-rice, and fish with milk, and having marched with elephants, chariots, horses, and men beginning from the east,

children.text: soḍhum pratāpam arayo na nrpasya śaktā gandhadvipasya kalabhā iva gandhadānam[K.dānagandham]//
children.translated_text: the enemies are not able to withstand the prowess of the king, like young elephants [cannot withstand] the rut-fluid of a great tusker.

children.text: ekataś ca sakalāni nimittāny ekataś ca manasaḥ pariśuddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: On one side are all the omens, on the other is the purity of the mind.

children.text: cetaso 'sti[K.'pi] sahasā na[K.'sti] raṇe bhīr māruto 'pi vijayājayahetuḥ//
children.translated_text: If the mind does not suddenly have fear in battle, even the wind becomes a cause of victory, not of defeat.

children.text: bhūriśūravaravājikuñjarā jñātayuddhagatayo 'bhimāninaḥ/
children.translated_text: Those who have many brave warriors, excellent horses, and elephants, who know the ways of battle and are proud—

children.text: kva 'pi yānti ghanatūlarāśivan mārutābhihatavakṣaso 'rayaḥ//
children.translated_text: the enemies, struck in the chest by the wind, go to some [distant] place like a mass of thick cotton.

children.text: anulomagate[K.anulomagatau] pradakṣiṇe surabhau dehasukhe 'nile gataḥ/
children.translated_text: When the wind blows favorably, clockwise, fragrant, and pleasant to the body, one who has marched

children.text: timirāṇi gabhastimān iva prasabhaṃ hanti balāni vidviṣām//
children.translated_text: forcefully destroys the armies of the foe, as the sun [destroys] darkness.

children.text: upapattir ayatnato yadā tṛṇapānāśanaratnavāsasām//
children.translated_text: When there is an effortless occurrence of grass, water, food, jewels, and garments,

children.text: pramadākṣitināgavājināṃ vijayadvāram apāvṛtaṃ tadā//
children.translated_text: and of women, land, elephants, and horses—then the gate of victory is opened.

children.text: lagnasya ye 'ṃśā hy uditā[K.uditā] graho yas teṣu sthito lagnaphalaṃ sa dhatte/
children.translated_text: Whatever degrees of the <s>lagna</s> have risen, and whatever planet is stationed in those [degrees], that [planet] bears the result of the <s>lagna</s>.

children.text: yas tān atītaḥ sa bhaved dvitīyaḥ sthāneṣu śeṣeṣv api cintyam etat[K.cintanīyam]//
children.translated_text: The one that has passed those [degrees] would be [as if] in the second [house]; this should be considered for the remaining positions as well.

children.text: gato 'nukūlair grahabhāgnimārutair mano 'bdavidyutsvanavṛṣṭikārmukaiḥ/
children.translated_text: One who has marched with favorable planets, fire, and wind, [accompanied by] favorable clouds, lightning, sounds, rain, and rainbows,

children.text: ripoḥ pramathnāti raṇājire camūṃ dvipaḥ samūlāṃ sarasī 'va padminīm//
children.translated_text: crushes the enemy's army on the battlefield, as an elephant [uproots] a lotus-bed, root and all, in a lake.

children.text: daivena hīnaḥ parabhīṣaṇārthaṃ yāto 'tikṛcchreṇa nayaty ahāni/
children.translated_text: One who has marched, bereft of [divine] fortune, for the purpose of terrifying the enemy, spends his days with extreme difficulty,

children.text: svaśaktyatīto nṛpaveśmanī 'va kṛtvā pratijñām prativādibhītaḥ//
children.translated_text: like one who, having made a pledge beyond his own power in the king's court, is afraid of the opponent.

children.text: daivānvitaḥ sādhujanopakārī prabhāvamantrodyamaśaktiyuktaḥ/
children.translated_text: One who is endowed with [divine] fortune, who benefits good people, who possesses might, counsel, energy, and power,

children.text: bhuṅkte mahīṃ samyag avāpya yātrāṃ sasahyavindyācalapāriyātrām//
children.translated_text: having duly undertaken the campaign, rules the earth together with the <s>Sahya</s>, <s>Vindhya</s>, and <s>Pāriyātra</s> mountains.

children.text: gocareṇa śubhadaḥ śaśī na ced aṣṭavargapariśodhito 'pi[K'tha] vā/
children.translated_text: If the Moon does not bestow auspiciousness through its transit (<s>gocara</s>), or even if purified through the <s>aṣṭavarga</s> system,

children.text: pūrvavāyur iva puṣpakālajo yāyinām phalavināśakṛd bhavet//
children.translated_text: it would destroy the results for those on campaign, like the east wind during the flowering season [destroys] blossoms.

children.text: āśritya candrasya balābalāni grahāḥ prayacchanti śubhāśubhāni/
children.translated_text: Depending on the strength or weakness of the Moon, the planets bestow auspicious and inauspicious results,

children.text: manaḥsametāni yathendriyāṇi karmārhatāṃ[K.karmaṇyatāṃ] yānti na kevalāni//
children.translated_text: just as the senses, accompanied by the mind, attain fitness for action—not independently.

children.text: sarvataḥ kṣutam aśobhanam uktaṃ goḥ kṣutaṃ[K.gokṣutam] maraṇaṃ eva karoti/
children.translated_text: Sneezing is said to be inauspicious from all directions; the sneezing of a cow causes death itself.

children.text: kecid āhur aphalaṃ bakād ca[K.hi balād] yad vṛddhapīnasitabālākṛtaṃ ca//
children.translated_text: Some say that the sneezing caused involuntarily by elders, the fat, the fair, or children is without result.

children.text: śakunatithibhalābhe chattraśayyāsanādyaṃ padam api vijigīṣuś cālayec chradadhānaḥ[K.chraddhadhānaḥ]/
children.translated_text: One who desires to conquer should, with faith, move even the umbrella, bed, seat, and other items [only after considering] omens, <s>tithis</s>, and [planetary] strength,

children.text: yadi śakunanimittasvapnacetoviśuddhir[K.śakunanimitte 'sya svacetoviśuddhir] na bhavati tad aniṣṭaṃ sarvakāryeṣu yānam//
children.translated_text: for if there is no purity of omens, signs, dreams, and mind, then the journey is inauspicious in all undertakings.

children.text: dinakṛddivase tathā 'ṃśake yātrā lagnagate 'thavā ravau/
children.translated_text: A campaign on the day of the Sun, or in its degree-subdivision, or when the Sun is in the <s>lagna</s>,

children.text: saṃtāpāyati smarāturā[K.smarāturaṃ] veśye 'vā 'rthavivarjitaṃ naram//
children.translated_text: torments a man devoid of wealth, like a courtesan [torments] one afflicted by passion.

children.text: udaye śaśino 'ṃśake 'hni vā bhavati gato na cireṇa durmanāḥ//
children.translated_text: On the day of the Moon's rising, or in its degree-subdivision, one who has marched becomes disheartened before long,

children.text: pramadām iva jātayauvanāṃ[K.yātayauvanāṃ] ratyarthaṃ samavāpya karkaśaḥ//
children.translated_text: like a rough man who, for the sake of pleasure, has obtained a woman past her youth.

children.text: bhaumodaye 'ṃśe 'hani vā 'sya yātrā karoti bandhaṃ vadham arthanāśam/
children.translated_text: A campaign on the day of <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars), or in its degree-subdivision or its day, brings about imprisonment, slaughter, and loss of wealth,

children.text: saṃsevitā 'pāpaparāṅmukhena manobhavāndhena parāṅgane 'va//
children.translated_text: like [a passion] indulged in by one blinded by desire, turning away from virtue, with another man's wife.

children.text: budhasya lagnāṃśakavāsareṣu yātrā naraṃ prīṇayati prakāmam/
children.translated_text: On the days, degree-subdivisions, and weekdays of <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), a campaign delights a man exceedingly,

children.text: bhāvānuraktā pravarāṅgane 'va vidagdhaceṣṭā madanābhitaptam[K.madanābhibhūtam]//
children.translated_text: like a skilled and beautiful woman, devoted in affection, [delights] one tormented by passion.

children.text: guror vilagnāṃśadineṣu yātrā śubhānu[K.hitānu]bandhepsitakāmadā ca/(Bṝ 5.31--33)
children.translated_text: A campaign on the days, degree-subdivisions, and weekdays of <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) is auspicious, bringing desired wishes and [connected with] beneficial [results],

children.text: jāye 'va bhartur manaso 'nukūlā kulābhivṛddhyai ratidā hitā ca//
children.translated_text: like a wife who is agreeable to her husband's mind, for the growth of the family, pleasure-giving, and beneficial.

children.text: yātrā bhṛgor aṃśadinodayeṣu prīṇāti kāmair vividhair yiyāsum//
children.translated_text: A campaign at the rising, degree-subdivisions, and days of <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) delights the campaigner with various pleasures,

children.text: vilāsinī kāmavaśopayātam bhāvair anekair madanāture 'va//
children.translated_text: like a seductive woman [delights] one who has come under the sway of desire, with many moods, one tormented by passion.

children.text: dyulagnabhāgeṣu śaneś ca yātrā prāṇacchidādīn pracinoti[K.pratanoti] doṣān/
children.translated_text: A campaign on the days, degree-subdivisions, and [ascendant] portions of <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) brings about faults such as loss of life and the like,

children.text: anyaprasaktā vanite 'va mohāt saṃṣevitā[K.mohān niṣevitā] manmathamohitena//
children.translated_text: like [a relationship] indulged in by one deluded by desire with a woman who is attached to another.

children.text: lagnena hīnā 'nyaguṇānvitāpi prītiṃ na yātrā manasaḥ karoti/
children.translated_text: A campaign devoid of [proper] <s>lagna</s>, even if endowed with other virtues, does not bring joy to the mind,

children.text: svalaṅkṛtā rūpasamanvitā 'pi prabhraṣṭaśīlā vanite 'va puṃsaḥ//
children.translated_text: like a woman endowed with beauty and well-adorned, but of fallen character, [does not bring joy] to a man.

children.text: lagnasya śuddhiḥ śakunair nimittair vijñāyate 'ntaḥkaraṇena samyak/
children.translated_text: The purity of the <s>lagna</s> is rightly known through omens, signs, and the inner mind,

children.text: ananyabhāvāśrayasaṃpravṛttaiḥ kaulī 'va puṃsaś caritair videśe//
children.translated_text: like [the character of] a woman of good family [is known] by her conduct in a foreign land, arising from devotion to none other [than her husband].

children.text: chāyā śubhāśubhaphalāni nivedayantī lakṣyā manuṣyapaśupakṣiṣu lakṣaṇajñaiḥ/
children.translated_text: The shadow (<s>chāyā</s>), which reveals auspicious and inauspicious results, should be observed by those who know the signs in humans, animals, and birds,

children.text: tejoguṇān bahir api pravikāśayantī dīpaprabhā sphaṭikaratnaghaṭasthitaiva[K.sphaṭikaratnaghaṭasthite 'va]//
children.translated_text: manifesting the qualities of radiance even externally, like the light of a lamp placed within a vessel of crystal gem.

children.text: snighadvijatvaṅnakharomakeśā chāyā sugandhā ca mahīsamutthā/
children.translated_text: A shadow that has smooth, healthy skin, nails, body-hair, and head-hair, that is fragrant and arises from the earth,

children.text: tuṣṭyarthalābhābhiudayān karoti dharmasya ca 'hany ahani pravṛddhim//
children.translated_text: it brings contentment, gain of wealth, and prosperity, and day by day an increase of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: snigdhā sitā ca haritā nayanābhirāmā saubhāgyamārdavasukhābhyudayān karoti/
children.translated_text: Unctuous, white, and green, delightful to the eyes—it brings good fortune, gentleness, comfort, and prosperity.

children.text: sarvārthasiddhijananī jananī 'va cāpyā[K.''pyā] chāyā phalaṃ tanubhṛtāṃ śubham ādadhāti//
children.translated_text: The shadow that is the mother of the accomplishment of all aims, like a mother herself, bestows auspicious fruit upon embodied beings.

children.text: caṇḍā 'dhṛṣyā padmahemāgnivarṇā yuktā tejovikramaiḥ sapratāpaiḥ/
children.translated_text: Fierce, indomitable, of the color of lotus, gold, and fire, endowed with radiance, valor, and burning heat—

children.text: āgneyī 'ti prāṇināṃ syāj jayāya kṣipraṃ siddhiṃ vāñchitārthasya dhatte//
children.translated_text: called "fiery," it would bring victory to living beings and swiftly grants the accomplishment of desired aims.

children.text: malinaparuṣakṛṣṇā pāpagandhā 'nilotthā janayati vadhabandhavyādhyanarthārthanāśān/
children.translated_text: Turbid, rough, and black, of foul smell, arising from the wind—it produces slaughter, imprisonment, disease, calamity, and loss of wealth.

children.text: sphaṭikasadṛśarūpā bhāgyayuktā 'tyudārā nidhir iva gaganotthā śreyasāṃ svacchavarṇā//E40
children.translated_text: Resembling crystal in form, endowed with fortune, exceedingly noble—born from the sky, of clear hue, it is like a treasury of blessings.

children.text: puruhūtahutāśayamā nirṛtir varuṇānilayakṣaśivāś ca diśām/
children.translated_text: The lords of the directions are <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Nirṛti</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Yakṣa</s> [<s>Kubera</s>], and <s>Śiva</s>;

children.text: punar arkasitāratamoravijāḥ śaśisaumyabṛhaspatayaḥ patayaḥ//
children.translated_text: again, the lords [of the directions in terms of planets] are the Sun, Venus, Mars, <s>Rāhu</s>, Saturn, the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter.

children.text: śacyā sahairāvaṇagaḥ savajro haimo 'thavā dārumayo mahendraḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Mahendra</s> [<s>Indra</s>], mounted on <s>Airāvaṇa</s> together with <s>Śacī</s>, holding the thunderbolt, made of gold or of wood,

children.text: vicitramālyadhvajaraktacandanaiḥ saumyopahāreṇa ca pūjanīyaḥ//
children.translated_text: is to be worshipped with varied garlands, banners, red sandalwood, and gentle offerings.

children.text: atha mantram[K.mantraḥ:] <abhī shu naḥ sakhīnām> iti japtvā purataḥ prandarasya/
children.translated_text: Then, having recited the <s>mantra</s> "<s>abhī ṣu naḥ sakhīnām</s>" before <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: puruhūtadiśaṃ nṛpo 'bhiyuñjyāt puruhūtaṃ hṛdaye niveśya samyak//
children.translated_text: the king should set forth toward <s>Indra</s>'s direction [the east], having duly installed <s>Indra</s> in his heart.

children.text: tāmrajā pratikṛtiḥ sahasrago raktacandanakṛtānulepanā/
children.translated_text: The image of the Sun-born [<s>Agni</s>] should be made of copper, anointed with red sandalwood paste,

children.text: raktavastrakusumadhvajārcitā[K.dhvajācitā] sūryakāntamaṇibhir vibhūṣitā//
children.translated_text: worshipped with red garments, flowers, and banners, and adorned with <s>sūryakānta</s> (sun-stone) gems.

children.text: <ā kṛṣṇa> pūrvaṃ yadivā 'py <ud u tyaṃ> mantraṃ samāvartya raveḥ purastāt/
children.translated_text: Having first recited the <s>mantra</s> "<s>ā kṛṣṇa</s>" or "<s>ud u tyam</s>" before the Sun [<s>Agni</s>],

children.text: kṣīraudanena pratipūjya yāyāt prācīm puraskṛtya dineśaśakrau//
children.translated_text: and worshipping with milk-rice, one should set forth eastward, keeping the Sun and <s>Indra</s> foremost.

children.text: agnes tanuḥ kanakenaiva kāryā raktaā[K.raktaṃ] dhvajaṃ kusumaṃ candanaṃ ca/
children.translated_text: The image of <s>Agni</s> should be made of gold; red should be the banner, flower, and sandalwood.

children.text: ājyam balir hutabhugvijigīṣor[K.hutabhugdigjigīṣor] mantro[K.mantraṃ] <ghṛtaṃ ghṛtayonaṃ[K.ghṛtayoneḥ]> pibeti[K.paṭhec ca]//
children.translated_text: Clarified butter is the offering for one who wishes to conquer [in] <s>Agni</s>'s direction; the <s>mantra</s> is "<s>ghṛtaṃ ghṛtayonam</s>"—one should recite it.

children.text: kāryaś citro ditisutagurur vāmayorṣāddhakāyo[K.yamo vā 'rdhakāyo] nānārūpāḥ kusumabhalayas tasya citro dhvajaś ca/
children.translated_text: The image of the preceptor of the <s>Daityas</s> [<s>Yama</s>] should be made variegated, half-bodied; his banners and offerings should be of various forms and colors;

children.text: <śukrajyotiḥ> prabhṛti ca japen[K.paṭhen] mantram asya 'gratas tau kṛtvā yāyād bhṛgujadahanau jetum icchus[K.icchaṃs] tad āśām//
children.translated_text: one should recite the <s>mantra</s> beginning with "<s>śukrajyotiḥ</s>" before him, and having placed both [<s>Śukra</s> and <s>Agni</s>] in front, one wishing to conquer that direction should set forth.

children.text: ayomayam prodyatadaṇḍahastaṃ yamaṃ sakṛṣṇadhvajapuṣpagandham[K.sakṛṣṇa\-.dhvaja\-.puṣpa\-.gandhaiḥ]/
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>'s image should be made of iron, with an upraised staff in hand, accompanied by black banners, flowers, and fragrances.

children.text: tilaudanair[K.tilodanair] arcya samāṃsamadyair <yamena dattaṃ> ca japo 'sya kāryaḥ//
children.translated_text: Worshipping with sesame-rice, meat, and liquor, the recitation of "<s>yamena dattam</s>" should be performed.

children.text: mūrttiḥ syād rudhirākhyasaṃjñamaṇinā[K.rudhirākṣasaṃjñamaṇinā] bhaumasya raktāḥ srajo raktāni dhvajacandanāni kusumaiḥ pakvānnamāṃsair baliḥ/
children.translated_text: The image of <s>Mars</s> [<s>Bhauma</s>] should be made with a gem called "blood-stone"; the garlands should be red, and the banners, sandalwood, and flowers red; the offering should be cooked rice and meat. The praise of the son of Earth [<s>Mars</s>] begins with "<s>agnir mūrdhā</s>." Thus, with <s>Yama</s> and <s>Mars</s> as lords of the direction, the king should place them before him and proceed southward.

children.text: <agnir mūrdha[K.mūrdhā]>padaiḥ stutiḥ kṣitisutasyaivaṃ yamāṅgārakau diṅnāthau gamane 'grato narapatiḥ kṛtvā vrajed dakṣiṇam[K.dakṣiṇām]//
children.translated_text: The praise of the son of Earth [<s>Mars</s>] begins with "<s>agnir mūrdhā</s>." Thus, with <s>Yama</s> and <s>Mars</s> as lords of the direction, the king should place them before him and proceed southward.

children.text: bhairavāpratikṛtiḥ paṭe kṛtā sarvagandha[K.puṣpa]phalapuṣpa[K.dhūpa]pūjitā/
children.translated_text: An image of <s>Bhairava</s> should be drawn on cloth, worshipped with all fragrances, fruits, flowers, and incense.

children.text: <eṣa te> nirṛtimantracodanā kṛṣṇaraktakusumadhvajāmbarā//
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> invocation for <s>Nirṛti</s> is "<s>eṣa te</s>"; [the image should be adorned] with black and red flowers, banners, and garments.

children.text: suradārumayaḥ śaśāṅkaśatruḥ kusumādyair asitaiḥ kṛtopahāraḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Rāhu</s> [the enemy of the Moon] should be made of <s>devadāru</s> wood, with offerings of dark items.

children.text: nirṛtisahitaḥ[K.nirṛter mahitaḥ] svadikprayāṇe stutimantro 'sya ca kīrtitaḥ <kayā naḥ>//
children.translated_text: Together with <s>Nirṛti</s>, honored for a journey in that direction [southwest]; the <s>mantra</s> of praise for him is declared to be "<s>kayā naḥ</s>."

children.text: paścād vrajed rajatamayaṃ jaleśvaraṃ pāśānvitam saha gadayā 'bjapūjitam/
children.translated_text: Proceeding westward, [one should worship] <s>Varuṇa</s>, the lord of waters, made of silver, equipped with a noose and mace, worshipped with lotuses,

children.text: kṛtvaudanair balim api yāvākānvitaṃ[K.yāvākācitaṃ] <ye te śataṃ[K.(lacuna)śaṃ]> varuṇa[K.varuṇaṃ] iti stuyād dvijaḥ//
children.translated_text: making an offering of rice mixed with barley-gruel; the twice-born should praise <s>Varuṇa</s> with "<s>ye te śatam</s>."

children.text: saurer arcā nīlakācā ṛśāṅgī pūjyā kṛṣṇair vastramālyopahāraiḥ/
children.translated_text: The image of <s>Saturn</s> should be of blue glass, gaunt-limbed, worshipped with black garments, garlands, and offerings.

children.text: <śaṃ no devī> 'ty eṣa mantro 'parāśāṃ jetuṃ yāyāt tau puraskṛtya devau//
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is "<s>śaṃ no devī</s>"; to conquer the western direction, one should set forth placing those two deities foremost.

children.text: vāyor mūrttiḥ śvetamṛdbhir vidheyā pūjyā śvetaiḥ puṣpavastradhvajādyaiḥ/
children.translated_text: The image of <s>Vāyu</s> should be fashioned of white clay, worshipped with white flowers, garments, banners, and the like.

children.text: mantro <vāto vā mano ve> 'ti jāpyo vāyavyāśām prasthitasye ''śvarasya//
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> "<s>vāto vā mano ve</s>" should be recited for the lord setting forth toward the northwest direction.

children.text: mantraḥ somasyā<''pyāyasve> 'ty anyac chvetaṃ sragvastrādyam/
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> for <s>Soma</s> is "<s>āpyāyasve</s>"; the rest—garlands, garments, etc.—should be white.

children.text: vāyuṃ somaṃ ca 'gre kṛtvā yāyād rājā vāyoḥ kāṣṭhām//
children.translated_text: Having placed <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Soma</s> in front, the king should proceed toward <s>Vāyu</s>'s quarter [northwest].

children.text: hāṭakamūrtiṃ[K.hāṭakīm mūrtiṃ] kuryād dhanadasya vibhūṣitāṃ[K.bhūṣitāṃ] ratnaiḥ sagadāñ ca[K.sarvaiḥ sagadāṃ ca]/
children.translated_text: One should make a golden image of <s>Dhanada</s> [<s>Kubera</s>], adorned with jewels and bearing a mace.

children.text: pūjitāṃ sragvastrādyaiś ca vicitrai <rakṣasām bhāgo 'si> 'ty eṣa hi mantraḥ//
children.translated_text: Worshipped with various garlands, garments, and the like; the <s>mantra</s> is "<s>rakṣasāṃ bhāgo 'si</s>."

children.text: sauvarṇaṃ rajatāsane nṛmithunaṃ candrātmajasyeṣyate hāridraudana\-.miṣṭa\-.gandha\-.kusumair gandhaiś ca saṃpūjitam[K.tat pūjitam]/
children.translated_text: A golden image of a human couple on a silver seat is prescribed for <s>Mercury</s> [son of the Moon]; worshipped with turmeric-rice, pleasant fragrances, flowers, and perfumes.

children.text: <udbudhyasva> japaś ca tasya kathitaḥ syād brahmayajñeti ca[K.brahmayajñādinā] gacched uttarato dhaneśvarabudhau dhyāyan puraskṛtya ca//
children.translated_text: The recitation prescribed for him is "<s>udbudhyasva</s>," along with the <s>Brahmayajña</s>; one should proceed northward, meditating on and placing <s>Kubera</s> and <s>Mercury</s> foremost.

children.text: gotvagjāpyati bhairavā[K.gotvagjā pratibhairavā] pratikṛtir bhasmotkaṭā śūlino dadhnā codanaṣaṃyutena ca[K.omitted] balir[K.balibhir] mantro <namaḥ śambhave>/
children.translated_text: The image of <s>Bhairava</s> [<s>Śiva</s>], made of cow-skin, smeared with ashes, bearing a trident, with an offering of curd mixed with rice—the <s>mantra</s> is "<s>namaḥ Śambhave</s>."

children.text: mūrttiḥ syān maṇito guror vimalikā[K.vimalakāt] pītaṃ tu vastrādikaṃ[K.vastrādi yan] mantraś ca 'sya<bṛhaspater[K.bṛhaspate]> iti tayor yāyād diśam pūjya tau//
children.translated_text: The image of <s>Jupiter</s> [the preceptor] should be made of a clear gem; the garment and the rest should be yellow; his <s>mantra</s> is "<s>Bṛhaspate</s>"; having worshipped those two, one should proceed in their direction [northeast].

children.text: diṅnāthaṃ kuladevatāṃ svanagare yeṣāṃ kṛtāc ca ''layās tān sampūjya yathānurūpa\-.balibhir dadyād balim bhautikīm[K.bhautikam]/
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the lord of the direction and the family deity in one's own city, and [the deities of] whatever temples have been built, with appropriate offerings, one should give the earthly oblation,

children.text: kṛtvā pāyasamadyamāṃsapalalair bhakṣyaiś ca nānāvidhair bālakṛīḍanakaiḥ sugandhakusumair[K.sugandhikusumair] mūlaiḥ phalaiḥ svādubhiḥ//
children.translated_text: prepared with milk-pudding, liquor, meat, cakes, various edibles, children's playthings, fragrant flowers, roots, and sweet fruits.

children.text: rathyāpuradvāranadītaṭeṣu catuṣpathāṭṭālakaniḥkuṭeṣu/
children.translated_text: In streets, city gates, riverbanks, crossroads, watchtowers, shrines,

children.text: guhaikavṛkṣādiṣu ye vasanti te pūjanīyāḥ pramathā yathāvat//
children.translated_text: caves, solitary trees, and such places—the <s>Pramathas</s> (attendants of <s>Śiva</s>) dwelling there should be duly worshipped.

children.text: namo 'stu vaḥ śakrahutāśadaṇḍabhṛtkṣapācarāmbhaḥpatimātariśvanāḥ[K.nām]
children.translated_text: "Homage to you, O hosts who attend upon <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s> the staff-bearer, <s>Rākṣasas</s> of the night, <s>Varuṇa</s> the lord of waters, <s>Vāyu</s>,

children.text: kuberarudrāhisuparṇaśaktibhṛtpiśācadaityānucarāś ca ye gaṇāḥ>//
children.translated_text: <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Suparṇas</s>, <s>Śakti</s>-bearers, <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Daityas</s>, and all your retinue!"

children.text: kusumaśaraśarīraspardhinaḥ kāmarūpā vividhasurabhivastrāḥ sragviṇo[K.vividha\-.surabhivastrasragviṇo] 'sahyavīryāḥ/
children.translated_text: "[You who are] rivaling the body of <s>Kāma</s> the flower-arrowed, of forms at will, clad in various fragrant garments, garlanded, of irresistible valor,

children.text: pavanasadṛśavegā mānino nityahṛṣṭās taruṇadinakaratviṭspardhitejodadhāṇāḥ>//
children.translated_text: swift as the wind, proud, ever joyful, bearing splendor that rivals the radiance of the young sun!"

children.text: <lambakroḍā hrasvā dīrghāḥ khañjaikākṣāḥ śuṣkāḥ sthūlāḥ/
children.translated_text: "[Some] with pendulous bellies, short, tall, lame, one-eyed, emaciated, or stout,

children.text: nānāpakṣivyāloṣṭrāsyā vaktrair hīnāḥ kroḍāsyāś ca>//
children.translated_text: with faces of various birds, serpents, camels—some faceless, and some with boar-faces!"

children.text: <bahuvaktraśirobhujapādadṛśaḥ kṛkalāsabhujaṃgakṛtābharaṇāḥ/
children.translated_text: "With many faces, heads, arms, feet, and eyes, adorned with lizards and serpents as ornaments,

children.text: vikaṭā mukuṭotkaṭaratnabhṛtas taruṇārkataḍiddhutabhukkapilāḥ>//
children.translated_text: terrible, wearing diadems set with prominent gems, tawny like the young sun, lightning, fire, and smoke!"

children.text: <bhramaratamāladvipagavalābhāḥ kṣitidharameghapratimaśarīrāḥ[K.kṣitidhara\-.megha\-.pratibhaśarīrāḥ]/
children.translated_text: "Of the hue of bees, <s>tamāla</s> trees, elephants, and cows, with bodies resembling mountains and clouds,

children.text: aśaninipātasvanasaninādā[K.manādā] drutagamane ca sva[K.śva]sanamanogāḥ>//
children.translated_text: roaring with the sound of thunderbolts, and in swift movement [fast as] wind and thought!"

children.text: <simuśalagadāśmaśaktiśūladrumasaśarāsanabāṇacakrahastāḥ/
children.translated_text: "Bearing swords, clubs, maces, stones, lances, tridents, trees, bows with arrows, and discuses in hand,

children.text: kaṇaya[K.kaṇapa]parighakuntamuṣṭimāyā laguḍakuṭhāraśataghnīdhāriṇaś ca>//
children.translated_text: and also wielding iron bars, javelins, fists, illusions, cudgels, axes, and hundred-slaying weapons!"

children.text: <gṛhṇantu[K.gṛhṇīta] pramathagaṇā baliṃ sabhūtā bhūbhartrā vijigīṣuṇā niveditaṃ vaḥ/
children.translated_text: "May the hosts of <s>Pramathas</s>, together with the <s>Bhūtas</s>, accept this offering presented by the lord of the earth who desires conquest!

children.text: jitvā 'rīn dviguṇam ato baliṃ vicitraṃ dāsyāmaḥ svaviṣayam etya vaḥ prasādāt>//
children.translated_text: Having conquered the enemies, we shall give you a doubled and varied offering upon returning to our own domain, by your grace!"

children.text: <rājā vaḥ śaraṇam upāgataḥ sabhṛtyaḥ sāmātyaḥ sasutakalatramitrabandhuḥ/
children.translated_text: "The king, with his servants, ministers, sons, wives, friends, and kinsmen, has come to you for refuge.

children.text: rakṣārtham manujapateḥ sahāyakṛtyaṃ kruvīdhvaṃ ripubalasaṃkṣayāya ca 'sya>//
children.translated_text: For the protection of the lord of men, render your aid and for the destruction of his enemy's forces!"

children.text: <svapne nimittam athavā manujeśvarasya yac chabdam[K.chadhvam] ekatamam asya jayājayāya/
children.translated_text: "In a dream, or an omen, or a sound—whichever one—give a sign to the lord of men regarding his victory or defeat.

children.text: evaṃ bhavaty upakṛtaṃ sumahad bhavadbhiḥ kāryaṃ kariṣyati yathā bhavatāṃ prasādāt>//E29
children.translated_text: Thus a very great service will have been rendered by you; and he shall do what is to be done, by your grace!"

children.text: madayantikā 'śvagandhā madanaphalavacāmadhūni śasyante/
children.translated_text: <s>Madayantikā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>madanaphala</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and honey are recommended [for the bath]

children.text: prathamarkṣe bharaṇīṣu ca[K.(tu)] siddhārthakabhadradāruvacāḥ//
children.translated_text: under the first <s>nakṣatra</s> [<s>Aśvinī</s>]; and under <s>Bharaṇī</s>, white mustard, <s>bhadradāru</s>, and <s>vacā</s>.

children.text: nyagrodhaśirīṣāśvatthapatragandhāś ca kṛttikāsnāne/
children.translated_text: Under <s>Kṛttikā</s>, the bath should use the leaves and fragrances of banyan, <s>śirīṣa</s>, and <s>aśvattha</s>.

children.text: bahubījapraśastatoyair jayārthino rohiṇīsnānam//
children.translated_text: The bath under <s>Rohiṇī</s> for one seeking victory should use water with many seeds and auspicious [substances].

children.text: muktākāñcanamaṇisaṃyuktena 'mbhasā mṛigāṅkarkṣe/
children.translated_text: Under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, with water mixed with pearls, gold, and gems.

children.text: raudre vacāśvagandhāpriyaṃgumiśrair jalaiḥ kathitam//
children.translated_text: Under <s>Ārdrā</s>, it is prescribed with waters mixed with <s>vacā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>.

children.text: āditye gomayagoṣṭhamṛdbhir atha gauraśālibhiḥ puṣye/
children.translated_text: Under <s>Punarvasu</s> [the Sun's <s>nakṣatra</s>], with cow-dung and earth from a cow-pen; and under <s>Puṣya</s>, with white <s>śāli</s> rice,

children.text: siddhārthasahasradvaya[K.siddhārthadvisahasraiḥ]priyaṃgumadayantikābhiś ca//
children.translated_text: two thousand white mustard seeds, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, and <s>madayantikā</s>.

children.text: valmīkaśatān mṛdbhiḥ nāge[K.sārpe] pitrye ca devanirmālyaiḥ/
children.translated_text: Under <s>Āśleṣā</s> [the Serpent <s>nakṣatra</s>], with earth from ant-hills; under <s>Maghā</s> [the Ancestral], with offerings removed from deities.

children.text: pūrvāsu phalgunīṣu ca salavaṇaghṛtaśāḍvalaiḥ proktam//
children.translated_text: Under <s>Pūrvā Phalgunī</s>, the bath is prescribed with salt, clarified butter, and green grass.

children.text: śatapuṣpayā priyaṃgvā mustābhiś cottarāsu kruvīta/
children.translated_text: Under <s>Uttarā Phalgunī</s>, it should be done with <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, and <s>mustā</s>.

children.text: haste sarogirimṛdā citrāyāṃ devanirmālyaiḥ//
children.translated_text: Under <s>Hasta</s>, with earth from a lake and mountain; under <s>Citrā</s>, with offerings removed from deities.

children.text: svātau jalaruhakusumair aindrāgnye[K.aindrāgne] matsya[K.musta]padmakakṣaudraiḥ/
children.translated_text: Under <s>Svāti</s>, with lotus flowers; under <s>Viśākhā</s>, with fish, lotuses, and honey.

children.text: maitre saridubhayamṛdā haritālamṛdā ca māhendre//
children.translated_text: Under <s>Anurādhā</s>, with earth from both banks of a river; and under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, with orpiment-earth.

children.text: bhadrāsane śamīmayapatrasahasradvayāmbubhir mūle//
children.translated_text: Under <s>Mūla</s>, seated in the auspicious posture, with water [infused with] a thousand <s>śamī</s> leaves.

children.text: samadhūkapadmamatsyaiḥ snānam aṣāḍhāsu pūrvāsu//
children.translated_text: Under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, the bath should be with <s>madhūka</s>, lotus, and fish.

children.text: kuryād uśīracandanapadmakamiśreṇa vāriṇā vaiśve/
children.translated_text: Under <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, with water mixed with <s>uśīra</s>, sandalwood, and <s>padmaka</s>.

children.text: nadyubhayakūlasaṃgamamṛtkanakaiḥ kīrtyate śravaṇe//
children.translated_text: Under <s>Śravaṇa</s>, it is prescribed with earth and gold from the confluence of both banks of a river.

children.text: ghṛtabhadradārumadhubhiś ca vāsave vārune ghṛtakṣaudraiḥ/
children.translated_text: Under <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, with ghee, <s>bhadradāru</s>, and honey; under <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>, with ghee and honey,

children.text: samadanaphala[K.samadanaphalaiḥ]sahadevāmbuśūkamadayantikāmiśraiḥ//
children.translated_text: mixed with <s>madanaphala</s>, <s>sahadevā</s>, water, husk, and <s>madayantikā</s>.

children.text: śrīvāsakaḥ priyaṃguś ca ''je syād uttarāsv agurugandhāḥ/
children.translated_text: Under <s>Pūrvābhādrapadā</s>, <s>śrīvāsaka</s> and <s>priyaṅgu</s>; under <s>Uttarābhādrapadā</s>, <s>aguru</s> fragrances are

children.text: śastāḥ sapadmakośīracandanā mānavendrāṇām//
children.translated_text: recommended along with <s>padmaka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and sandalwood for the lords of men.

children.text: revatyāṃ vṛṣabhadvipaviṣāṇakośaiḥ ca sarpimadhupūrṇaiḥ[K.sasarpimadhupūrṇaiḥ]/
children.translated_text: Under <s>Revatī</s>, with horns of bulls and elephants [used as vessels] filled with ghee and honey,

children.text: gorocanāñjanayutaiḥ salilaiś ca yiyāsataḥ puṃsaḥ[K.yiyāsatām puṃsām]//
children.translated_text: combined with <s>gorocanā</s> and collyrium in the waters—for the man about to set forth.

children.text: girivalmīkanadīmukhakūladvayaśakrapādamṛdbhir ataḥ/
children.translated_text: Then, with earth from mountains, ant-hills, river-mouths, both banks, and the base of <s>Indra</s>'s [banner-post],

children.text: dvipavṛṣaviṣāṇapārthivagaṇikādvārāhṛtābhiś ca//
children.translated_text: and [earth] brought from the doors of elephants, bulls, kings, and courtesans—

children.text: giriśikharān mūrdhānaṃ valmīkamṛdā ca śodhayet[K.śocayet] karṇau/
children.translated_text: one should purify the head from a mountain-peak, the ears with ant-hill earth,

children.text: nadyubhayakūlasaṃgamamṛdbhiḥ prakṣālayet pārśve//
children.translated_text: wash the sides with earth from the confluence of both riverbanks,

children.text: indrasthānād grīvāṃ bāhū karivṛṣabhayor vishāṇāt[K.vishāṇāgrāt]/
children.translated_text: the neck from <s>Indra</s>'s [banner] post, the arms with [earth from near] the tusks of elephants and bulls,

children.text: hṛdayaṃ ca[K.omitted] nṛpadvārāt[K.nṛpatidvārāt] kaṭim api veśyāghṛhadvārāt//
children.translated_text: the chest from the king's gate, and the waist from the gate of a courtesan's house.

children.text: akṣatamāṣāḥ svinnāstilasahitās taṇdulā dadhi ca gavyam[K.akṣatamāṣā ādyaṃ tilasahitas taṇḍulaś ca dadhigavyam]/
children.translated_text: Unbroken grains, black beans, cooked sesame-mixed rice, curd, and cow's [products]—

children.text: vṛṣata[K.vṛṣabha]piśitaṃ mṛgasya ca pañcānām āśvinādīnām//
children.translated_text: and the flesh of a bull and of a deer—[these are] for the five [<s>nakṣatras</s>] beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s>.

children.text: rudhiravilāpanapāyasavihaga[K.bhujaṃga]māṃsāni śāṃkarādīnām/
children.translated_text: Blood, ointment, milk-pudding, bird-meat, and snake-flesh—for [the <s>nakṣatras</s>] beginning with <s>Śaṃkara</s> [<s>Ārdrā</s>].

children.text: pitrye tilaudanaṃ ṣaṣṭikānnam ṛkṣadvaye parataḥ[K.ca tatparataḥ]//
children.translated_text: Under the Ancestral [<s>Maghā</s>], sesame-rice; under the pair of <s>Phalgunī nakṣatras</s>, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>-rice; and thereafter—

children.text: prāśyāḥ priyaṃgucitrāṇḍajaphalaṃ[K.priyaṃgucitrāṇḍajāḥ palaṃ] yāvakaṃ kulatthāś ca/
children.translated_text: one should eat <s>priyaṅgu</s>, variegated eggs, fruit, barley-gruel, and <s>kulattha</s> beans.

children.text: madhusasarpiṣī[K.madhusarpiṣī] ca hastān mūlāny āpaḥ [mūlāmbhaḥ] saktavo 'pi[K.omitted] mūlāt//
children.translated_text: Honey and ghee are [for] <s>Hasta</s>; roots and water [for] <s>Mūla</s>; and barley-meal also [for] <s>Mūla</s>.

children.text: śravaṇādīnāṃ adyāt[K.bhakṣyāḥ] śāliśākaṃ[K.śāliḥ śākaṃ] biḍālamāṃsaṃ ca/
children.translated_text: For [the <s>nakṣatras</s>] beginning with <s>Śravaṇa</s>, one should eat <s>śāli</s> rice, vegetables, and cat-meat,

children.text: ājaṃ yatheṣṭamāṃsaṃ ca śaktavo[K.susaktavo] māṣasaṃpṛktāḥ//
children.translated_text: goat-meat, any desired meat, and barley-meal mixed with black beans.

children.text: prācīṃ gajena yāyād rathena yāmyāṃ hayena vāruṇyām/
children.translated_text: One should proceed eastward by elephant, southward by chariot, westward by horse,

children.text: narayānenodīcīṃ sarvaṃ datvā digīśāya//
children.translated_text: and northward by a human-borne conveyance, having given everything to the lord of the direction.

children.text: prācyādi ghṛtaṃ tilaudanaṃ matsyāṇ kṣīraṃ iti pradakṣiṇam/
children.translated_text: In the east, etc., [one should eat] ghee, sesame-rice, fish, and milk respectively, going clockwise;

children.text: adyān nrpatir yathādiśaṃ nakṣatrābhihitaṃ ca siddhaye//
children.translated_text: the king should eat according to the direction and what is prescribed for the <s>nakṣatra</s>, for success.

children.text: asvādu cyutamakṣikānuviddhaṃ[K.cyutakacamakṣikānuviddhaṃ]
children.translated_text: Food that is tasteless, fallen, contaminated by flies,

children.text: durgandhi kṣayakṛd abhūri yac ca daghdam/
children.translated_text: foul-smelling, causing decay, scanty, or burnt [is inauspicious].

children.text: susvinnaṃ śuci[K.mṛdu] ruciraṃ mano 'nukūlaṃ
children.translated_text: Well-cooked, pure, attractive, agreeable to the mind,

children.text: svādv annaṃ bahu vijāya[K.ca jayāya] yānakāle//E22
children.translated_text: tasty food in abundance [is auspicious] for victory at the time of march.

children.text: vedī śubhā śulva[K.śilpa]vidhānadṛṣṭā diksthānamānābhydhikā[K.dik\-.sthāna\-.mānānadhikā] na hīnā/
children.translated_text: The fire-altar should be auspicious, constructed according to the rules of the <s>Śulva</s> [geometry], with the directional positions and measurements neither excessive nor deficient.

children.text: bhraṣṭapramāṇa[K.bhraṣṭā pramāṇena] prakaroti[K.karoti] bhaṅgaṃ digvakrasaṃsthā ca na[K.na ca] siddhidā syāt//
children.translated_text: One of faulty measurements causes disaster; and one placed crookedly in direction would not grant success.

children.text: prāgbhāgahīnā nagarasya neṣṭā purodhasāṃ[K.purodhaso] dakṣiṇabhāgavakrā/
children.translated_text: An altar deficient on its eastern side is inauspicious for the city; one crooked on the southern side [is inauspicious] for the chief priest.

children.text: narendrajāyāśubhadā parasyām udag baleśasya nṛpasya madhye//
children.translated_text: On the western side, it brings misfortune to the queen; on the northern, to the army commander; in the center, to the king.

children.text: sattvair alīḍhaṃ na pipīlamakṣikāmalāvilaṃ vā[K.tad] vijayapradaṃ haviḥ/
children.translated_text: An oblation that has been licked by animals, or contaminated by ants, flies, or impurities, does not grant victory.

children.text: dravyāṇy anūnāni paṭuḥ purohito juhoti samyag vijayāya bhūbhṛtām//
children.translated_text: With implements complete and proper, the skilled <s>purohita</s> (chief priest) offers the oblation duly for the victory of kings.

children.text: gandhamālyacarukumbhabhājanasrukkuśavyajanasarpiṣāṃ yadā/
children.translated_text: When regarding the fragrance, garlands, ritual porridge, water-pots, vessels, <s>sruk</s>-ladle, <s>kuśa</s> grass, fans, and clarified butter,

children.text: bhaṅgavismṛtinipātahīnatā pārthivasya na bhavet tadā śubham[K.tadā bhavec chivam]//
children.translated_text: there is no breakage, forgetfulness, falling, or deficiency—then it is auspicious for the king.

children.text: śāntāyāṃ diśi yadi śaṅkhatūryaśabdāḥ saptīnāṃ plutamibhabṛṅhitāni[K.rutagajabṛṃhitāni] vā syuḥ/
children.translated_text: If, in a peaceful direction, sounds of conches and trumpets, or the leaping of horses and the trumpeting of elephants,

children.text: puṃsāṃ vā pramuditaceṣṭitapralāpāḥ śrūyante yadi ca jayo 'sti homakāle//
children.translated_text: or the joyful gestures and speeches of men are heard—then there is victory at the time of the <s>homa</s> (fire oblation).

children.text: apratirathaḥ samasto yātrāliṅgas tathā 'bhayaś ca[K.'bhayasya] gaṇaḥ/
children.translated_text: The entire group named <s>Apratirathaḥ</s> (Invincible) along with the <s>Yātrāliṅga</s> (Signs of March) and the <s>Abhaya</s> (Fearless) group,

children.text: svastyayanaśarmavarmā 'parājitāḥ puṣpasaṃjñāś ['parājitā ''yuṣyasaṃjñāś] ca//
children.translated_text: <s>Svastyayana</s>, <s>Śarman</s>, <s>Varman</s>, <s>Aparājita</s> (Unconquered), and those named after flowers [or named <s>Āyuṣya</s> (Longevity)],

children.text: indraś candraś citi[K.candreti] gaṇo yat[K.yaṃ] te candraś ca bhūtabhūteti/checked
children.translated_text: The group called <s>Indra</s>, <s>Candra</s>, and also <s>Bhūtabhūta</s>—

children.text: sūktaṃ mahāvyāhṛtayo mantrāśīrvaiṣṇavā[K.sūktamahāvyāhṛtayaḥ prājāpatyāś ca ye] mantrāḥ//
children.translated_text: The <s>Sūkta</s> (hymn), the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great sacred utterances), the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [or <s>Prājāpatya</s>] <s>mantras</s>—

children.text: prājāpatyāś coktā home[K.uktāḥ kāle (lacuna) rājño] nirgacchato 'nu gamane ca/
children.translated_text: The <s>Prājāpatya</s> (relating to <s>Prajāpati</s>) [mantras] are prescribed for the <s>homa</s> (fire oblation) [at the time] when the king departs and for the procession.

children.text: agnipurohitasaṃsthāny ato[K.home 'gniprohitasaṃsthāni] nimittāni vakṣyāmi[K.gṛhṇīyāt]//
children.translated_text: Now I shall describe the omens connected with the fire, the <s>purohita</s> (royal priest), and the arrangement.

children.text: kṛte 'pi yatne 'tikṛśaḥ [ū.'pi kṛZaḥ] kṛśānur yātavyakāṣṭhāvimukho natārciḥ/
children.translated_text: If, despite effort, the fire is exceedingly thin, turned away from the wood to be consumed, with a bent flame,

children.text: vāmīkṛtāvartaśikho [ū.vāme kṛtāvartaśikho] 'tidhūmo vicchinnasākampavilīnamūrtiḥ//
children.translated_text: With a leftward-spiraling crest of flame, excessively smoky, with an interrupted, trembling, and fading form—

children.text: śimaśimāyati[K.śimiśimāyati,ū.simisimāyati] yasya [ū.cāsya] havir hutaṃ sura\-.dhanuḥ\-.sadṛśaḥ kapiśo [ū.kapilo] 'thavā/
children.translated_text: If the offering sizzles when offered, or the fire is of a rainbow-like brownish [or tawny] color,

children.text: rudhirapītakababhruharicchaviḥ paruṣamūrttir aniṣṭakaro 'nalaḥ//
children.translated_text: Or of blood-red, yellow, brown, or greenish hue, of rough form—such a fire is inauspicious.

children.text: śvakharakarabha [ū.kharakarabhaka]vānarānurūpo nigaḍavibhīṣaṇaśastrarūpabhṛd vā/
children.translated_text: Or if it resembles a dog, donkey, camel, or monkey, or bears the form of fetters, frightful objects, or weapons,

children.text: śavarudhiravasāsthivasta[K.ū.majja]gandho hutabhug aniṣṭaphalaḥ sphuliṅgakṛc ca//
children.translated_text: Or smells of corpses, blood, fat, bones, or marrow—such a sacrificial fire yields inauspicious results and produces sparks.

children.text: carmavipāṭanatulyaninādo jarjaramandavi[K.mandravi,ū.dardura]rūkṣaravo vā/
children.translated_text: If it makes a sound like the splitting of leather, or a crumbling, faint, and harsh noise,

children.text: ākulayaṃś ca purohitasabhyān [ū.purohitamartyān] dhūmacayair[K.ū.dhūmalavair] aśivāya [ū.na śivāya] hutāśaḥ//
children.translated_text: And confuses the <s>purohita</s> and the officiants with clouds of smoke—such a fire portends misfortune.

body.text: svāhāvasānasamaye svayam ujjvalārciḥ snigdhapradaksiṇaśikho[K.snigdhaḥ pradaksiṇaśikho] hutabhug nṛpasya/
body.translated_text: At the conclusion of the <s>svāhā</s> offering, if the fire blazes up on its own with bright flames, with a smooth, clockwise-turning crest—such a sacrificial fire of the king
Brings under his control the earth, adorned with the beautiful necklaces of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the daughter of the Sun, girdled by the ocean.

children.text: hārakundakusumendu[K.ū.kumudendu]saṃnibhaḥ saṃhato 'ṅgasukhado mahodayaḥ/
children.translated_text: Resembling a necklace, <s>kunda</s> flowers, the moon—compact, pleasing to the body, and portending great prosperity—

children.text: aṅkuśābjajalavāraṇacchavir[K.ū.aṅkuśātapanivāraṇākṛtir] hūyate 'lpatapasāṃ na [ū.'lpa upamāna] havyabhuk//
children.translated_text: With the appearance of an elephant-goad, a lotus, water, and a parasol—the sacrificial fire does not accept offerings from those of little austerity.

children.text: cāmīkarāśokakirīṭaratna[K.kuraṇṭakābja]vaidūryanīlotpalasaṃnibhe 'gnau/
children.translated_text: When the fire resembles gold, <s>aśoka</s> flowers, a crown, jewels, <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl), and blue lotuses—

children.text: na dhvāntam antar bhavane 'vakāśaṃ karoti ratnāṃśuhṛtaṃ[K.hataṃ] nṛpasya//
children.translated_text: No darkness finds room within the palace of the king, being dispelled by the rays of jewels.

children.text: yeṣāṃ rathaughārṇavameghadantināṃ samaḥ svano[K.samasvano] 'gnir yadi vā 'pi dundubheḥ/
children.translated_text: Those whose fire has a sound equal to the roar of a multitude of chariots, ocean, clouds, or elephants, or of a drum—

children.text: teṣāṃ madāndhebhaghaṭāvaghaṭṭitā bhavanti yāne timirābilā [timiropamā] diśaḥ//
children.translated_text: For them, the directions in battle become dark as caves, struck by the collision of their maddened war-elephants.

children.text: dhvajakumbhahayebhabhūbhṛtām anurūpe vaśam eti bhūbhṛtām/
children.translated_text: When the fire resembles banners, water-jars, horses, elephants, or mountains, the earth comes under the king's control—

children.text: udayāstadharādharādharā himavadvindhyapayodharā dharā//
children.translated_text: The earth with mountains high and low, from horizon to horizon, bearing the <s>Himavat</s> and <s>Vindhya</s> ranges.

children.text: dviradamadamahīsarojalājair ghṛtamadhunā[K.ghṛtamadhunoś] ca hutāśane sagandhe/
children.translated_text: When the fragrant fire is fed with elephant-rut fluid, earth from a lake, rice-grains, clarified butter, and honey,

children.text: praṇatanṛpaśiromaṇiprabhābhir bhavati puraś churitā nṛpasya dīptiḥ[K.puraś churiteva bhūr nṛpasya]//
children.translated_text: The radiance of the king is adorned in front by the luster of the crest-jewels of prostrating kings.

children.text: agnyāśritaṃ yat phalam uktam asmiṃs nṛjātakarmādiṣu[K.taj jātakarmādiṣu] pauṣṭikeṣu/
children.translated_text: Whatever result has been stated here regarding fire, in birth ceremonies and other <s>pauṣṭika</s> (prosperity-promoting) rites,

children.text: yajñeṣu sarveṣu ca vahnikāryeṣv evaṃ vaded yasya yathānurūpam//E19
children.translated_text: And in all sacrifices and fire-related rituals—so one should declare it as appropriate for each [occasion]. //E19//

children.text: janmarkṣam ādyaṃ daśaman tu karmaṃ[K.daśamaṃ ca karma] sāṃghātikaṃ ṣoḍaśam ṛkṣam ādyāt/
children.translated_text: The birth <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism) is the first; the tenth is called <s>karma</s> (action); the <s>sāṃghātika</s> (collective) asterism is the sixteenth from the first;

children.text: aṣṭādaśaṃ syāt samudāyasaṃjñaṃ vaināśikaṃ viṃśatibhāt tṛtīyam[K.viṃśatibhis tribhiś ca]//
children.translated_text: The eighteenth is known as <s>samudāya</s> (aggregate); the <s>vaināśika</s> (destructive) is the twenty-third;

children.text: yat pañcaviṃśaṃ khalu mānasaṃ tat ṣaḍṛkṣa evaṃ puruṣas tu sarvaḥ/
children.translated_text: And the twenty-fifth is indeed the <s>mānasa</s> (mental). Thus every person has six asterisms.

children.text: rājño navarkṣāṇi vadanti jātideśābhiṣekaiḥ sahitāni tāni//
children.translated_text: For a king, they declare nine asterisms, those [six] combined with the asterisms of birth, country, and coronation.

children.text: rājño 'bhiṣekarkṣam uśanty amiśraṃ sādhāraṇe dve saha ṣaḍbhir ādyaiḥ/
children.translated_text: The coronation asterism of a king is considered unmixed; two common [asterisms] together with the first six.

children.text: kimtv atra doṣāś ca guṇāś ca sarve pradhānam ekaṃ puruṣaṃ bhajante//
children.translated_text: But herein, all the faults and merits pertain primarily to one person.

children.text: kūrmopadiṣṭāni hi deśabhāni rājño 'bhiṣekāhani ca ''bhiṣekam/
children.translated_text: The regional asterisms taught by <s>Kūrma</s> (the Tortoise [Purāṇa]) and the coronation [asterism] on the day of the king's consecration—

children.text: yā jātayaś bhasya[K.ca 'pi] bhavanty atas tā vargāṃś ca vakṣyāmi yathākrameṇa[K.vakṣyāmi daivajñanirākulārtham]//
children.translated_text: The classes [of asterisms] that belong to him—those and the groups I shall describe in due order.

children.text: pūrvātrayaṃ sānalam agrajānāṃ rājñāṃ tu puṣyeṇa sahottarāṇi/
children.translated_text: The first three, together with the fiery [<s>Kṛttikā</s>], belong to the foremost kings; and <s>Puṣya</s> along with the northern [asterisms] [belong to them too].

children.text: sapauṣṇamaitraṃ pitṛdaivataṃ ca prajāpater bhaṃ ca kṛṣīvalānām//
children.translated_text: <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, and the asterism of the ancestors (<s>Maghā</s>), and the asterism of <s>Prajāpati</s> (<s>Rohiṇī</s>)—these belong to farmers.

children.text: ādityahastābhijidāśvināni vaṇigjanānāṃ pravadanti bhāni/
children.translated_text: <s>Āditya</s> (<s>Punarvasu</s>), <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Abhijit</s>, and <s>Aśvinī</s> are declared to be the asterisms of the merchant class.

children.text: mūlatrinetrānilavāruṇāni bhāny ugrajāteḥ prabhaviṣṇutāyāḥ//
children.translated_text: <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Trinettra</s> (<s>Ārdrā</s>), <s>Anila</s> (<s>Svāti</s>), and <s>Vāruṇa</s> (<s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>) are the asterisms of the fierce caste, [endowed with] power.

children.text: saumyendra[K.aindra]citrāvasudaivatāni sevājanasvāmyam upāgatāni/
children.translated_text: <s>Saumya</s> (<s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>), <s>Aindra</s> (<s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>), <s>Citrā</s>, and <s>Vasudaivatā</s> (<s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>) are associated with lordship over servants.

children.text: sārpaṃ viśākhāśravaṇe bharaṇyaś cāṇḍālajāter abhinirdiśanti[K.iti nirdiśanti]//
children.translated_text: <s>Sārpa</s> (<s>Āśleṣā</s>), <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Śravaṇa</s>, and <s>Bharaṇī</s> designate the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) class.

children.text: raviravisutabhogam āgataṃ kṣitisutabhedanavakradūṣitaṃ/
children.translated_text: That [asterism] which has come under the sway of the Sun or Saturn, which is vitiated by the cutting or cruel [aspect] of Mars,

children.text: grahaṇagatam atho 'lkayā hataṃ niyatamukhākara[K.niyatam uṣākara]pīḍitaṃ ca yat//
children.translated_text: Or which is in eclipse, or struck by a meteor, or afflicted by a fixed malefic—

children.text: tad upahatam iti pracakṣate prakṛtiviparyayajātam[K.yātam] eva vā/
children.translated_text: That is declared to be afflicted, or even if it has undergone a reversal of its natural [qualities];

children.text: nigaditapara[K.pari]vargadūṣitaṃ[K.dūṣaṇaṃ] kathitaviparyayagaṃ samṛddhaye//
children.translated_text: An asterism corrupted by the defects of the stated hostile group [becomes favorable] if the reversal is declared to be for prosperity.

children.text: rogābhiyāgamavittanāśakalahā[K.rogābhiyāgamavittanāśakalahāḥ] sampīḍite janmabhe
children.translated_text: Disease, attack, loss of wealth, and strife [come] when the birth asterism is afflicted;

children.text: siddhiṃ karma na yāti karmaṇi hate bhedās tu sāṃghātike/
children.translated_text: Actions do not succeed when the <s>karma</s> [asterism] is struck; there are divisions when the <s>sāṃghātika</s> is afflicted;

children.text: dravyasyopacitasya sāmudayike saṃpīḍite saṃkṣayo
children.translated_text: When the <s>samudāya</s> [asterism] is afflicted, there is destruction of accumulated wealth;

children.text: vaināśe tu bhavanti kāyavipadaś cittāsukhaṃ mānase//
children.translated_text: In the <s>vaināśika</s>, there are bodily calamities; in the <s>mānasa</s>, mental unhappiness.

children.text: nirupadrutabho nirāmayaḥ sukhabhāg puṣṭatanur[K.naṣṭaripur] dhanānvitaḥ/
children.translated_text: One whose [six] asterisms are unafflicted is free from disease, enjoys happiness, has a robust body, and is endowed with wealth.

children.text: ṣaḍupadrutabho vinaśyati tribhir anyaiś ca saha 'vanīśvaraḥ//
children.translated_text: One whose six asterisms are afflicted perishes, and with three others, so does the lord of the earth.

children.text: na bhavati śarīrapīḍā yasya vinā śāntibhir bhapīḍāyām/
children.translated_text: There is no bodily suffering for one [whose asterism is afflicted] without the pacificatory rites for the affliction of the asterism;

children.text: tasya śarīravipattiḥ pākānte devalaḥ prāha//
children.translated_text: <s>Devala</s> has declared that his bodily misfortune [comes] at the end of the ripening [period].

children.text: sarveṣāṃ pīḍāyāṃ dinam ekam upoṣito 'nalaṃ juhuyāt/% VḍhP 1.89.1--13
children.translated_text: When all [asterisms] are afflicted, one should fast for one day and make offerings to the fire,

children.text: sāvitryā kṣīrataroḥ samidbhir amaradvijānuraktaḥ[K.rataḥ]//
children.translated_text: With fuel from the milk-tree, [reciting] the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [mantra], devoted to the gods and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.

children.text: gokṣīrasitavṛṣabha[K.vṛṣa]śakṛnmūtraiḥ patraiś ca pūrṇakośāyāḥ/
children.translated_text: Bathing with cow's milk, white bull dung, urine, and leaves of the <s>pūrṇakośā</s> plant—

children.text: snānaṃ janmani duṣṭe svācāravatāṃ harati pāpam//
children.translated_text: When the birth [asterism] is corrupted, this removes sin for those who observe proper conduct.

children.text: karmaṇi madhughṛtahomo daśāham akṣāramadyamāṃsādaḥ/
children.translated_text: For the <s>karma</s> [asterism], a <s>homa</s> of honey and ghee for ten days, abstaining from salt, liquor, meat, and the like;

children.text: dūrvāpriyaṃgusarṣapaśatapuṣpaśatāvarīsnānam//
children.translated_text: Bathing with <s>dūrvā</s> grass, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, mustard seeds, <s>śatapuṣpa</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>.

children.text: sāṃghātike 'bhitapte[K.tu tapte] māṃsamadhukrauryamanmathāṃs tyaktvā/
children.translated_text: When the <s>sāṃghātika</s> is heated, one should give up meat, honey, cruelty, and lust;

children.text: snāto[K.dānto] dūrvāṃ juhuyād dānaṃ dadyād yathāśakti//
children.translated_text: Having bathed, one should offer <s>dūrvā</s> grass in the fire and give charity according to one's ability.

children.text: sāmudayike 'pi[K.tu] dadyāt kāñcanarajatāny upahate[K.upadrute] dhiṣṇye/
children.translated_text: For the <s>samudāya</s> too, one should give gold and silver when the asterism is afflicted;

children.text: vaināśike 'nnapānaṃ vasudhāṃ ca guṇāṇvite dadyāt//
children.translated_text: For the <s>vaināśika</s>, one should give food, drink, and land endowed with good qualities.

children.text: mānasatāpe homaḥ saroruhaiḥ pāyasair dvijāḥ pūjyāḥ/
children.translated_text: When the <s>mānasa</s> is heated, a <s>homa</s> with lotuses; <s>brāhmaṇas</s> should be honored with milk-rice;

children.text: gajamadaśirīṣacandanabalātibalavāriṇā snānam//E18% ḥere Kern's version ends.
children.translated_text: Bathing with water infused with elephant-rut, <s>śirīṣa</s>, sandalwood, <s>balā</s>, and <s>atibalā</s>. //E18// [Here Kern's version ends.]

children.text: ārirādhayiṣuṇā narādhipaṃ vāraṇāśritam idaṃ śubhāśubham/
children.translated_text: One who wishes to please the king should know this auspicious and inauspicious [lore] connected with elephants;

children.text: jñeyam ādaravatā vipaścitā vāraṇeṣu nṛpater jayasthitiḥ//
children.translated_text: A wise person who is attentive [should know] that the king's victory and stability depend on elephants.

children.text: sārddhaṃ hastaśataṃ dairghyā sāvaṃśaṃ vipulā śatam/
children.translated_text: One hundred and fifty <s>hastas</s> (cubits) in length including the extension, one hundred in width,

children.text: caturastrā 'thavā vṛttā vārī vāraṇavṛddhidā//
children.translated_text: Either square or round—such an enclosure promotes the welfare of elephants.

children.text: daśāvagāhena karā vistīrṇā daśa copari/
children.translated_text: The water-trench is ten <s>karas</s> (cubits) deep and ten wide on top;

children.text: adhaḥkhātasya padavī hastamātrā prakīrtitā//
children.translated_text: The pathway of the underground excavation is declared to be one <s>hasta</s> in measure.

children.text: karttavyaṃ pūrvato dvāram uttaraṃ vā śubhāvaham/
children.translated_text: The gate should be made on the eastern or northern side, which is auspicious;

children.text: dakṣiṇaṃ paścimaṃ vā 'pi na karttavyaṃ kathañ cana//
children.translated_text: On the southern or western side, it should never be made.

children.text: meḍhakastambhamāt tṛṇāṃ vṛkṣāgraṃ nāvanau kṣipet/
children.translated_text: From the top of the post, one should not cast straw [or tree-tops] into the enclosure;

children.text: pūrvāprāc cottarāgrāc ca saṃyojyā nityam argalā//
children.translated_text: The bolt should always be fitted from the east facing east or from the north facing north.

children.text: daśa vistārato dvāraṃ pārśvayos tasya mātṛkāḥ/
children.translated_text: The gate is ten [cubits] in width; on both sides of it are the mother-pillars,

children.text: caturdaśa karotsedhā niḥkhātya caturaḥ karān//
children.translated_text: Fourteen [cubits] in height, sunk four <s>karas</s> into the ground.

children.text: ṣaṭ ṣaṇmeḍhāntarasthāś ca meḍhakāḥ pañca pañca ca/
children.translated_text: Six, with six intervals between the posts, and the posts are five [each],

children.text: caturhastanikhātās te samucchrāyān vadāmy ataḥ//
children.translated_text: Sunk four <s>hastas</s> into the ground—I shall now state their heights.

children.text: ṣaṭ saptāṣṭanavotsedhā daśa veti yathākramam/
children.translated_text: Six, seven, eight, nine, and ten [cubits] in height respectively;

children.text: nava vā daśa vā vedhā mātṛkā yāḥ ṣaḍaṅgulāḥ//
children.translated_text: The mother-pillars are nine or ten in diameter, six <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths) [in some measure].

children.text: vedhahānyāvaśeṣāḥ syur mātṛkāḥ kramaśo 'parāḥ/
children.translated_text: The remaining mother-pillars are successively diminished by the diameter;

children.text: iti dvārasamāso 'yaṃ vāryyās saṃparikīrttitaḥ//
children.translated_text: This is the summary of the gate of the elephant enclosure.

children.text: madhvābhadantāḥ suvibhaktadehā na copadigdhā na kṛśāḥ kṣamāś ca/
children.translated_text: Elephants that are sweet-toothed, with well-proportioned bodies, neither anointed [with paint] nor thin, and are patient,

children.text: gātraiḥ samaiś cāpasamānavaṃśā vārāhatulyair jaghanaiś ca bhadrāḥ//
children.translated_text: With even limbs, of a lineage equal to none, with haunches like a boar—these are <s>bhadra</s> (noble) elephants.

children.text: vakṣo 'tha kakṣā valayaḥ ślathaś ca lambodaras tvagvṛhatī galaś ca/
children.translated_text: The chest, armpit, and loose girdle, a pendulous belly, thick skin, and the throat—

children.text: sthūlā ca kukṣiḥ saha mecakena saiṃhī ca dṛgmandamataṅgajasya//
children.translated_text: And a stout belly, along with a dark color, and the lion-like eyes of a sluggish elephant [characterize the <s>manda</s> type].

children.text: mṛgās tu hrasvādharabālameḍhrās tanvaghrikaṇṭhadvijahastakarṇāḥ/
children.translated_text: The <s>mṛga</s> (deer-type) elephants have short lower lip, young, and small phallus, thin legs, neck, teeth, trunk, and ears,

children.text: sthūlekṣaṇāś ceti yathoktacihnaiḥ saṅkīrṇanāgā vyatimisracihnāḥ//
children.translated_text: And large eyes—those with the described marks. Mixed elephants (<s>saṅkīrṇa</s>) have mixed characteristics.

children.text: pañconnatiḥ sapta mṛgasya dairghyam aṣṭau ca hastāḥ pariṇāhamānam/
children.translated_text: The <s>mṛga</s>'s height is five [cubits], its length seven, and its circumference is eight <s>hastas</s>;

children.text: ekadvivṛddhāv atha mandabhadrau saṃkīrṇanāgo 'niyatapramāṇaḥ//
children.translated_text: Increasing by one and two respectively for the <s>manda</s> and <s>bhadra</s> types; the mixed elephant has no fixed measurement.

children.text: bhadrasya varṇo harito madasya mandasya hāridrikasannikāśaḥ/
children.translated_text: The color of the <s>bhadra</s> type's rut-fluid is green, of the <s>manda</s>'s it is like turmeric,

children.text: kṛṣṇo madaś cābhihito mṛgasya saṃkīrṇanāgasya mado vimiśraḥ//
children.translated_text: The rut-fluid of the <s>mṛga</s> is declared to be black; that of the mixed elephant is of mixed [color].

children.text: sthapatir ataḥ prayato gajaśālāṃ narapatimandiradaksiṇabhāge/
children.translated_text: Thereafter, the architect, purified, should construct the elephant stable on the southern side of the king's palace,

children.text: avaniguṇān avalokya vidadhyāt kṛtabalihomasurācanaśāntiḥ//
children.translated_text: Having examined the qualities of the ground, with offerings, <s>homa</s>, worship of the gods, and pacificatory rites completed.

children.text: yātudhānaditisarpasaṅkulā sannikṛṣṭavibudhadvijālayā/
children.translated_text: Ground infested with <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>Diti</s>'s progeny, and serpents, in proximity to temples of the gods and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: śarkarāsthicayabhasmadūṣitā pārthivadviradadoṣadā mahī//
children.translated_text: Defiled with pebbles, bones, and ash—such earth is harmful to the king's elephants.

children.text: kiñcid abhyunnatā bhūḥ praśastadrumā gobhir adhyāsitā sādhu madhye samā/
children.translated_text: Ground slightly elevated, with auspicious trees, grazed by cows, level in the middle,

children.text: bhūritoyā 'ghanā hṛddṛgāhlādinī śalyadoṣair vinā sānunādasvanā//
children.translated_text: Abundant in water, not barren, pleasing to the heart and eyes, free from thorns and defects, with a resonant echo—

children.text: snigdhapallavadrumā pradakṣiṇāmbuvāhinī/
children.translated_text: With trees of lush foliage, and water flowing clockwise—

children.text: svarāṣṭravṛddhidā mahī hitā 'tha nāgavājinām//
children.translated_text: Such ground promotes the prosperity of one's own kingdom and is beneficial for elephants and horses.

children.text: bhadramandamṛgamiśradantināṃ śvetaraktakanakopamāsitāḥ/
children.translated_text: For <s>bhadra</s>, <s>manda</s>, <s>mṛga</s>, and mixed-type elephants, the grounds are white, red, golden, and dark respectively.

children.text: bhūmayo dviradapuṣṭivṛddhidā bhūbhṛtām api yaśaḥ sukhāvahāḥ//
children.translated_text: Such grounds promote the nourishment and growth of elephants and bring fame and happiness to kings.

children.text: jyeṣṭhā caturviṃśatir eva hastā dvidvyūnite madhyajaghanyaśāle/
children.translated_text: The foremost [elephant stable] is exactly twenty-four <s>hastas</s>; reduced by two each for the middle and lowest stables.

children.text: vistāratas taddviguṇāś ca dīrghāstambhāś ca vistārasamucchritāḥ syuḥ//
children.translated_text: In width, they are twice that in length; the pillars should be as tall as the width.

children.text: jyeṣṭho 'ṅgulāni bahulo daśaṣaḍyutāni madhyas tu pañcadaśa kanyas?o 'ṅgulonaḥ/
children.translated_text: The foremost pillar is sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> in girth; the middle is fifteen; the lowest is one <s>aṅgula</s> less.

children.text: stambhapramāṇavipulāḥ kramaśo niṣaṅgāḥ proktāṅgulārddhasadṛśaṃ bahulatvam eṣām//
children.translated_text: The brackets are as wide as the pillar-measure successively; their thickness is declared to be half an <s>aṅgula</s>.

children.text: sarvāsu śālāsu ca kaṇṭakasya hasto 'rdhayuktaḥ pariṇāha uktaḥ/
children.translated_text: In all stables, the circumference of the post (<s>kaṇṭaka</s>) is stated to be one and a half <s>hastas</s>.

children.text: kaṇṭapramāṇena samunnataś ca talapravandho dṛḍhadārubandhaḥ//
children.translated_text: As high as the post-measure, the tying-beam is firmly bound with strong wood.

children.text: alindabhittau tu gavākṣakeṣu kuryād guṇadvārakajālakāṃś ca/
children.translated_text: On the veranda-wall, in the windows, one should make lattice-screens and door-grilles.

children.text: nirbyūhayuktāsu ca vedikāsu kāryā bibhūṣā parito mayoktā//
children.translated_text: On the railings equipped with projections, ornamentation all around should be made, as I have described.

children.text: kamalotpalahaṃsayugapramathaiḥ pramadāyugapatravihaṅgaghaṭaiḥ/
children.translated_text: With lotuses, blue lotuses, pairs of swans, <s>pramathas</s> (demon attendants), pairs of women, leaf-patterns, birds, water-jars,

children.text: vividhais tarubhiḥ saśukabhramaraiḥ phalapallavapuṣpabharāvanataiḥ//
children.translated_text: Various trees with parrots and bees, bending under the weight of fruits, leaves, and flowers,

children.text: vyālakakuñjaramatsyamṛgendraiḥ kandamrṇālalatāṃkuraśobhaiḥ/
children.translated_text: Serpents, elephants, fish, lions, bulbs, lotus-stalks, creeper-shoots, and splendid [designs],

children.text: vāricaraiś ca citā makarādyaiḥ śikṣitaśilpivinirmitarūpā//
children.translated_text: And aquatic creatures such as <s>makaras</s> (sea-monsters) and others—fashioned by trained sculptors.

children.text: dvārocchrāyāḥ kuñjarāṇām atulyā vistāro 'sya tryaṃśahīnaḥ sa eva/
children.translated_text: The height of the gateway should match the elephants' [height]; its width is the same less one-third.

children.text: hīno bhūyaś cātmaṣaṣṭhāṃśakena śālād dvāraṃ prāgudak ca praśastam//
children.translated_text: Further reduced by one-sixth of itself—the gateway from the stable is auspicious if facing east or north.

children.text: vicitranirvyūhamṛgendrapañjaraṃ kapāṭameḍhārgalasuprayojitam/
children.translated_text: With a varied projecting structure and a lion-cage, well-fitted with door-panels, posts, and bolts,

children.text: suvedikālaṅkṛtam īkṣaṇapriyaṃ praveśanaṃ nirgamanāya cāparam//
children.translated_text: Adorned with fine railings, pleasing to the eye—one [door] for entry and another for exit.

children.text: candanārjunaśirīṣamadhūkā devadārusaralāñjanaśālāḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Candana</s> (sandalwood), <s>arjuna</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>madhūka</s>, <s>devadāru</s> (deodar), <s>sarala</s> (pine), <s>añjana</s>, <s>śāla</s>,

children.text: rohiṇīkhadiracampakaśākāḥ syandanaś ca sakadambaviśokāḥ//
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>khadira</s> (acacia), <s>campaka</s>, <s>śāka</s> (teak), <s>syandana</s>, together with <s>kadamba</s> and <s>aśoka</s>—

children.text: śītāḥ śivāś ca dvipabandhanārtham ete drumāḥ puṣṭikarā dvipānām/
children.translated_text: These trees, cool and auspicious, are for tying elephants and are nourishing for elephants.

children.text: stambhārtham anye 'pi hi sāravantaḥ kāryāḥ praśastā guṇasaṃprayuktāḥ//
children.translated_text: Other trees too that are heartwood-bearing should be used for pillars—auspicious ones endowed with good qualities.

children.text: pūrvābhimukho nibadhyate yaḥ kṣipraṃ sa karoti vikramam/
children.translated_text: An elephant that is tied facing east quickly achieves valor,

children.text: rājñas samareṣv anirjito dīrghaṃ cāyur avāpnuyād gajaḥ//
children.translated_text: Is undefeated in the king's battles, and attains long life.

children.text: dakṣiṇadigvadanasya ca bandho jīvitanāśakaro dviradasya/
children.translated_text: But tying an elephant facing south brings destruction of its life;

children.text: dhānyadhanakṣayam āśu ca kuryān mantrijanasya narādhipateś ca//
children.translated_text: And it quickly causes loss of grain and wealth for the counselors and the king.

children.text: paścān mukhaṃ bandham avāpya nāgo nityaṃ bhaved roganipīḍitāṅgaḥ/
children.translated_text: An elephant tied facing west shall always have a body afflicted by disease,

children.text: nāśañ ca vittasya karoti rājñas tasmāt sa yāmyāparadigvivarjyaḥ//
children.translated_text: And causes destruction of the king's wealth—therefore [the elephant] should be kept away from the south and west directions.

children.text: udaṅmukhaṃ bandham upaiti nāgo yo 'rthasya vṛddhiṃ sa karoti bhartuḥ/
children.translated_text: An elephant that is tied facing north promotes the increase of its master's wealth,

children.text: prāpnoti puṣṭiṃ cirajīvitāñ ca saṃgrāmakāleṣv aparājayañ ca//
children.translated_text: Attains nourishment and long life, and [brings] invincibility in times of battle.

children.text: suṣirordhvaśuṣkakoṭarakolākṣapranthibahulaśūlāgrāḥ/
children.translated_text: Posts that are hollow, dry on top, with holes, cavities, eyes [in the wood], knots, many thorns at the tip,

children.text: madhunilayamūlahīnāgrakuñjaballīvraṇānugatāḥ//
children.translated_text: Homes of bees, lacking roots, with tips, thickets, creepers, and wounds—

children.text: vāmāvarttaḥ śṛṅgī kuṇilo 'vanato 'nujātaviddhaś ca/
children.translated_text: A post with a leftward spiral, horned, stunted, bent, naturally fissured or pierced,

children.text: pitṛvanajaḥ sthūlāprastrikubjako drāṇikāvahutaḥ?//
children.translated_text: Born in a cremation ground, thick, flat-topped, hunchbacked, or offered in a fire—

children.text: sthūlagranthir vajreṇa cūrṇitaś cāśubhapradāḥ/
children.translated_text: Or with thick knots or shattered by lightning—all these are inauspicious

children.text: sarve bandhārthe nāgānām ataḥ phalāni pravakṣyāmi//
children.translated_text: For tying elephants. Now I shall declare the results [of various posts].

children.text: māsān ṣaḍūrdhvasuṣire stambhe ca bandhamāsādya/
children.translated_text: An elephant tied to a hollow post or [hollow] pillar will, within six months,

children.text: maraṇam upayāti nāgo nipīḍito vātarogeṇa//
children.translated_text: Meet death, afflicted by diseases of wind (<s>vāta</s>).

children.text: mriyate koṭaraviddhe kolākṣe 'ndhatvam āpnuyād nāgaḥ/
children.translated_text: An elephant tied to a post with a cavity dies; at one with an eye [in the wood], the elephant becomes blind.

children.text: kṣutpīḍāṃ granthicite mṛtyuṃ śūlena śūlāgre//
children.translated_text: affliction by hunger from a knotted post, and death from a post with a spike at the top.

children.text: mūlāgrakubjahīneṣu maraṇam abdāt sahaiva hastinyāḥ/
children.translated_text: From posts with tips that are root-like, humpbacked, or deficient, death of the elephant occurs within a year;

children.text: śṛṅgini mṛtyur madhudūṣite ca maraṇaṃ kṛmigadena//
children.translated_text: from a horned post, death; and from one contaminated with honey, death from worm disease.

children.text: gātrasya bhavati bhaṅgo ballīduṣṭe ghrāṇāvakīrṇe ca/
children.translated_text: There is fracture of the limbs from a post damaged by creepers and one with a damaged nose;

children.text: vāmāvartte nṛpater vinaśyate vāhanaṃ sarvam/
children.translated_text: from a post with a leftward spiral, all the vehicles of the king are destroyed.

children.text: mṛdgarbhe kuṇilākhye nṛpateḥ samahājanasya maraṇāya/
children.translated_text: From a post called <s>kuṇilā</s> with an earthen interior, death comes to the king together with his great retinue;

children.text: nāgasya tu trikubje bhavati badho yudhyataḥ stambhe//
children.translated_text: but for an elephant, from a triple-humped post there is slaying; and from a rigid post, death in battle.

children.text: anujātaviddhabaddhaḥ sukumāro vāraṇo maraṇam eti/
children.translated_text: An elephant that is born after [another], wounded, bound, or delicate meets death;

children.text: varṣadvayena mṛtyuḥ pitṛvanajāte nibaddhasya//
children.translated_text: death within two years for one born in the ancestral forest when bound.

children.text: sthūlāgrānatayor maraṇam eti māse 'ṣṭame mahāmātraḥ/
children.translated_text: From posts with thick tips or bent ones, a chief minister meets death in the eighth month;

children.text: dviradasya kṣutpīḍā baddhasya droṇikābahule//
children.translated_text: the elephant suffers hunger when bound to a post that has many troughs.

children.text: sthūlagranthir visphoṭamṛtyukṛd dantino dvitīye 'bde/
children.translated_text: A thick-knotted post causes death by boils for the elephant in the second year;

children.text: aśanihate vijñeyaḥ ṣaṇmāsād dantināṃ mṛtyuḥ//
children.translated_text: when struck by lightning, the death of elephants should be known within six months.

children.text: pradakṣiṇāvarttamanojñavṛtasusnigdhaṛjvavraṇasāravantaḥ/
children.translated_text: Posts that spiral clockwise, are attractive, round, very smooth, straight, scar-free, and strong,

children.text: doṣair vihīnā vijayāya śuddhāḥ stambhā dvipānāṃ balapuṣṭidāḥ syuḥ//
children.translated_text: free from defects, pure, lead to victory and give strength and nourishment to elephants.

children.text: yaḥ sampātaḥ karṇasūtra?dvayasya tasmād dhastaṃ sārddham utsṛjya kāryaḥ/
children.translated_text: The intersection of the two ear-strings—from that [point], releasing one and a half <s>hastas</s> (cubits), the post should be made

children.text: diśy aiśānyāṃ bandhanārthaṃ dvipānāṃ stambho rājñaḥ śreyase dantinaś ca//
children.translated_text: in the northeast direction for binding elephants; [such] a post leads to the welfare of the king and the elephant.

children.text: āgneyyāṃ dvipamaraṇaṃ nṛpārthahānir nairṛtyāṃ samaraparābhavārthanāśau/
children.translated_text: In the southeast, death of the elephant and loss of the king's wealth; in the southwest, defeat in battle and loss of wealth;

children.text: mārutyāṃ bhavati mataṅgajasya rogaḥ stambho 'taḥ śivadiśi ropitaḥ śivāya//
children.translated_text: in the northwest, disease of the elephant arises; therefore, a post planted in the auspicious [northeast] direction leads to welfare.

children.text: jyeṣṭho daśocco nava madhyamaś ca stambho 'ṣṭahastaḥ kathitaḥ kanīyān/
children.translated_text: The best post is ten [<s>hastas</s>], the middling nine, and the minimum post is said to be eight <s>hastas</s>;

children.text: sarve nikhātāś caturaś ca hastān mānādhikonāś ca śivāya na syuḥ//
children.translated_text: all should be buried four <s>hastas</s> [deep]; those exceeding or falling short of the measure would not be auspicious.

children.text: syād viṃśatir dvitricaturvihīnā mūle 'ṅgulānāṃ pṛthutā krameṇa/
children.translated_text: The breadth at the base should be twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths), decreasing by two, three, and four successively;

children.text: dvyūnāni tāny eva hi mastake syuḥ paryantaveṣṭā triguṇāni tāni//
children.translated_text: those same [measurements] minus two should be at the top; the circumferential binding is three times those [measurements].

children.text: tāmrauṣṭhatāluvadanāḥ kalaviṅkanetrāḥ snigdhonnatāgradaśanāḥ pṛthulāyatāsyāḥ//(Bṝ 21.2, Bṣ 66.6)
children.translated_text: With copper-colored lips, palate, and mouth; eyes like the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird; smooth, prominent front teeth; broad and long face—

children.text: cāponnatā yatanigūḍhanimagnavaṃśās tanvekaromacitakūrmasamānakumbhāḥ//
children.translated_text: with bow-shaped arched [trunk], concealed and sunken spine, with slender single-haired forehead bumps resembling a tortoise—

children.text: vistīrṇakarṇahanunābhilalāṭaguhyāḥ kūrmonnatair dvinavaviṃśatibhir nakhaiś ca/(Bṝ 21.3, Bṣ 66.7)
children.translated_text: with broad ears, chin, navel, forehead, and private parts; with nails numbering twenty-nine, raised like a tortoise—

children.text: rekhātrayopacitavṛttakarāḥ suba?lā dhanyāḥ sugandhimadapuṣkaramārutāś ca//
children.translated_text: with palms adorned with three lines, full and round, well-proportioned; fortunate, with fragrant rut-fluid and a vigorous breath—

children.text: dīrghāṅguliraktapuṣkarāḥ sajalāmbhodaninādavṛṃhiṇaḥ/(Bṝ 21.4, Bṣ 66.8)
children.translated_text: with long toes, red rut-discharge, trumpeting like rain-bearing clouds—

children.text: bṛhadāyatavṛttakandharā dhanyā bhūmipater mataṅgajāḥ//
children.translated_text: with large, long, and round neck—these are the fortunate elephants of a king.

children.text: nirmadābhyadhikahīnanakhāṅgān kubjavāmanakameṣaviṣāṇān/(Bṝ 21.5, Bṣ 66.9)
children.translated_text: Those without rut-fluid, with excessive or deficient nails and limbs, humpbacked, dwarfed, with ram's horns—

children.text: dṛśyakośaphalapuṣkaradīnān śyāvanīlaśavalāsitatālūn//
children.translated_text: with visible testicles, poor fruit-marks and rut-spots, of dark, blue, piebald, or black palate—

children.text: svalpavaktraruhamatkuṇaṣaṇḍhān hastinīñ ca gajalakṣaṇayuktām/(Bṝ 21.6, Bṣ 66.10)
children.translated_text: with sparse facial hair, resembling bugs, impotent; and a she-elephant endowed with [male] elephant characteristics—

children.text: garbhinīñ ca nṛpatiḥ paradeśaṃ prāpayed atibirūpaphalās te//
children.translated_text: and a pregnant one—the king should send [these] to another country; they bear extremely ugly results.

children.text: dantamūlapariṇāhadīrghatāṃ dviḥpramucya parato 'sya kalpayet/(Bṝ 21.7)
children.translated_text: Having measured twice the circumference and length at the base of the tusk, one should fashion its further [portion];

children.text: śyāvapū?timalaraktadarśanaṃ pāpasattvasadṛśaṃ ca pāpadam//
children.translated_text: one of dark, foul, dirty, or red appearance, resembling an evil creature, gives evil results.

children.text: pārthivopakaraṇākṛtiṃ yadā cihnam udvahati kalpite rade/(Bṝ 21.8)% hn B
children.translated_text: When, upon the fashioned tusk, a mark appears bearing the shape of a royal insignia,

children.text: śrījayārthavalavṛddhayas tadā snigdhaśuklarucirāś ca śobhanāḥ//
children.translated_text: then [it indicates] increase of glory, victory, wealth, and strength; smooth, white, and beautiful [tusks] are auspicious.

children.text: dakṣiṇe śubham atīvaśobhana pāpam apy ativirūpam anyataḥ/(Bṝ 21.9)
children.translated_text: On the right [tusk], auspicious [marks are] very beautiful; evil [marks], being very ugly, [appear] on the other [left tusk];

children.text: jāpyatā bhavati tad viparyaye vistaro 'nyamunibhiḥ prakīrttitaḥ//
children.translated_text: the reverse of that is to be recited [i.e., the opposite applies]; the details are proclaimed by other sages.

children.text: mūlamadhyadaśanāgrasaṃsthitā devadaityamanujāḥ kramāt tataḥ/(Bṝ 21.10)
children.translated_text: Deities, demons, and humans are stationed at the base, middle, and tip of the tusk respectively;

children.text: sphītamadhyaparipelavaṃ phalaṃ śīghramadhyacirakālasaṃbhavam//
children.translated_text: the fruit is abundant in the middle and slight at the ends; it arises quickly in the middle and over a long time [at the ends].

children.text: dantabhaṅgaphalam atra dakṣiṇe bhūpadeśabalavidravapradam/(Bṝ 21.11)
children.translated_text: The result of tusk-breaking on the right [tusk] is this: it gives [loss of] territory, country, and army through rout;

children.text: vāmataḥ sutapurohite bhayaṃ hanti bhṛtyajanadāranāyakān//
children.translated_text: on the left side, it brings danger to sons and the family priest, and destroys servants, dependents, wives, and leaders.

children.text: ādiśed ubhayabhaṅgadarśanāt pārthivasya sakalaṃ kulakṣayam/(Bṝ 21.12)
children.translated_text: From observing breakage on both [tusks], one should predict the complete destruction of the king's lineage;

children.text: saumyalagnatithibhādibhiḥ śubhaṃ varddhate śubham ato 'nyathāparam//
children.translated_text: with auspicious ascendant, <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), <s>nakṣatra</s>, etc., the auspicious [result] increases; otherwise, the opposite.

children.text: kṣīramiṣṭaphalapuṣpapādapaiś cāpagātaṭavighaṭṭanena vā/(Bṝ 21.13)
children.translated_text: By [contact with] milk-bearing trees, sweet fruit trees, flower trees, and by rubbing against river banks,

children.text: vāmamadhyaradabhaṅgakhaṇḍanaṃ śatrunāśakṛd ato 'nyathāparam//
children.translated_text: the breaking of the left or middle tusk brings destruction of enemies; otherwise, the opposite.

children.text: skhalitagatir akasmāt trastakarṇo 'tidīnaḥ śvasiti mṛdu sudīrghaṃ nyastahastaḥ pṛthivyām/
children.translated_text: An [elephant] whose gait stumbles, whose ears are suddenly frightened, who is very dejected, who breathes softly and very deeply, with trunk placed on the ground,

children.text: drutamukulitadṛṣṭiḥ svapnaśīlo vilomo bhayakṛd ahitabhakṣī naikaśo 'sṛak śakṛtkṛt//
children.translated_text: with rapidly shut eyes, prone to sleeping, moving backwards, causing fear, eating harmful things, and excreting blood and dung not all at once—

children.text: valmīkasthāṇugulmekṣutaruvimathanaḥ svecchayā hṛṣṭadṛṣṭir
