children.translated_text: One who crushes anthills, stumps, bushes, sugarcane, and trees, with eyes delighted of its own will,

children.text: yāyād yātrānulomaṃ tvaritapadagatir vaktram unnāmya coccaiḥ/
children.translated_text: who goes in the direction of the march with rapid steps, raising its face upward and high,

children.text: kakṣyāsadmāhakāl janayati ca muhuḥ śīkaraṃ bṛṃhate vā
children.translated_text: who generates sprays from its trunk-room repeatedly, or trumpets,

children.text: tatkālaṃ vā madāptir jayakṛd atha radaṃ veṣṭayan dakṣiṇaś ca//
children.translated_text: or obtains rut at that very time—[that elephant] brings victory; and also one who wraps [its trunk around] the right tusk.

children.text: praveśanaṃ vāriṇi vāraṇasya grāheṇa nāśāya bhaven nṛpasya/
children.translated_text: The entering of an elephant into water [and being seized] by a crocodile would bring destruction to the king;

children.text: grāhaṃ gṛhītvāt taraṇaṃ dvipasya toyāt sthale vṛddhikaraṃ nṛbhartuḥ//
children.translated_text: but the elephant's seizing the crocodile and crossing from the water to land brings increase to the lord of men.

children.text: raṇe jitvā śatrūn bhavati nṛpalakṣmīḥ kṣitibhṛtāṃ
children.translated_text: Having defeated enemies in battle, the royal glory of kings comes [to those]

children.text: jayas teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ madamalinagaṇḍāḥ karivarāḥ/
children.translated_text: whose excellent elephants have cheeks soiled with rut-fluid; they achieve victory.

children.text: bhinaty eko mattaḥ paravalamamattebhabahulaṃ
children.translated_text: A single elephant in rut shatters the enemy's army [even if] full of unintoxicated elephants—

children.text: yato 'to 'haṃ vakṣye karimadakaraṃ dravyanicayam//
children.translated_text: therefore I shall now describe the collection of substances that produce rut in elephants.

children.text: jātīguḍūcīkadalītilānām āsphotakarpāsavalānvitānām/
children.translated_text: Of <s>jātī</s> (jasmine), <s>guḍūcī</s>, banana, and sesame, combined with <s>āsphoṭa</s>, cotton-plant, and <s>bala</s>,

children.text: mārgī sanīlīgirikarṇikānāṃ dhattūskasyandanamāṣabhāgaḥ//
children.translated_text: and <s>mārgī</s>, with indigo, <s>girikarṇikā</s>—and a portion of <s>dhattūra</s>, <s>skanda</s>, and black gram.

children.text: kalambukā karṇakamāpaparṇīṃ punarnavā bhṛṅgarajo 'śvagandhāḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Kalambukā</s>, <s>karṇaka</s>, <s>āpaparṇī</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, pollen of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, and <s>aśvagandhā</s>;

children.text: śephālikāṃsoṭakakacchurāś ca kośātakī gokṣurakaṃ vidārī//
children.translated_text: <s>śephālikā</s>, <s>aṃsoṭaka</s>, <s>kacchura</s>, <s>kośātakī</s>, <s>gokṣuraka</s>, and <s>vidārī</s>.

children.text: viṣṇukrāntā dugdhikā śālaparṇī khaṭvāpādī vākucī vastagandhā/
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>dugdhikā</s>, <s>śālaparṇī</s>, <s>khaṭvāpādī</s>, <s>vākucī</s>, and <s>vastagandhā</s>;

children.text: vyāghrī ca syāt pṛṣṇiparṇī mṛṇālaṃ paṭorakaḥ sallakī tandulīyaḥ//
children.translated_text: <s>vyāghrī</s>, <s>pṛṣṇiparṇī</s>, lotus-root, <s>paṭoraka</s>, <s>sallakī</s>, and <s>tandulīya</s>.

children.text: etair yathāsaṃbhavasamprayuktair mattasya nāgasya madābhivṛddhiḥ/
children.translated_text: With these [herbs] combined as available, there is increase of rut in an already intoxicated elephant,

children.text: dānapramedaś ca madojjhitasya sarvāṅgaśobhā ca mukhe 'tiriktā//
children.translated_text: as well as flow of rut-fluid in one whose rut has ceased, and beauty of all limbs, especially in the face.

children.text: jīvakamadhūkadhanvanapaṭerakaṅkolakadaliṛṣabhāṇām/
children.translated_text: The roots of <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>madhūka</s>, <s>dhanvana</s>, <s>paṭera</s>, <s>kaṅkola</s>, banana, and <s>ṛṣabha</s>,

children.text: saubhāñjananimbeṅgudaparuṣakāṇāñ ca mūlāni//
children.translated_text: and of <s>saubhāñjana</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>iṅguda</s>, and <s>paruṣaka</s>,

children.text: mūlāni śatāvaryāḥ kākolī kṣīrasaṃjñakākolī/
children.translated_text: and the roots of <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, the milk-named <s>kākolī</s>,

children.text: śleṣmāntakaśālmaliśallakījaṭāḥ syur bimdāyaś ca//
children.translated_text: <s>śleṣmāntaka</s>, <s>śālmalī</s>, <s>śallakī</s> bark, and also <s>bimdā</s>,

children.text: kāśīsāśmantakarājamāṣamūlāni caivam etāni/
children.translated_text: and the roots of <s>kāśīsa</s>, <s>aśmantaka</s>, and <s>rājamāṣa</s>—all of these

children.text: sarvāṇi vaktraśābhāṃ janayanti sadaiva nāgānām//
children.translated_text: always produce beauty of the face in elephants.

children.text: nīlīpatraiś cūrṇitair māṣacūrṇo dadhnā yukto māhiṣeṇaiva piṇḍaḥ/
children.translated_text: A ball of powdered indigo leaves mixed with black gram powder, combined with buffalo curd—

children.text: nāgendrāṇām āśu ghatte madāptiṃ nīlyekaiva dravyavarge pradhānā//
children.translated_text: swiftly produces rut in lordly elephants; indigo alone is the chief among the group of substances.

children.text: ekaiva karoti kākajaṅghā hy ekekaiva ca māṣamudgaparṇī/
children.translated_text: <s>Kākajaṅghā</s> alone produces [rut], and <s>māṣamudgaparṇī</s> alone as well;

children.text: tāmbūlavanārdravṛścikālṣaś caikaikā madadās tathaiva mustāḥ//
children.translated_text: <s>tāmbūla</s>, fresh <s>vṛścikālī</s>, each singly produces rut; likewise <s>mustā</s> (cyperus).

children.text: kārpāsyekā cañcusaṃyojitā vā jñeyā caikā kaṇṭakī śailikākhyā/
children.translated_text: <s>Kārpāsī</s> alone, or combined with <s>cañcu</s>; one should know also the single thorny [plant] called <s>śailikā</s>;

children.text: ekaḥ śasto balkalaḥ sphūrjakasya jātī bhṛṅgenānvito vā kuṭheraḥ//
children.translated_text: the bark of <s>sphūrjaka</s> alone is praised; [also] <s>jātī</s> combined with <s>bhṛṅga</s>, or <s>kuṭhera</s>.

children.text: evam eveṅgudīmūlaṃ madaprācuryakārakam/
children.translated_text: Likewise, the root of <s>iṅgudī</s> alone produces abundance of rut;

children.text: ekā ca śvetakāmbojī śvetā caikā 'parājitā//
children.translated_text: and one [application of] white <s>kāmbojī</s>, and one [application of] white <s>aparājitā</s>.

children.text: samūlo vīraṇastambaḥ samūlā mallikā tathā/
children.translated_text: <s>Vīraṇa</s> grass with its root, and <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine) with its root likewise,

children.text: madaprācuyasauramyaṃ kurvantīndīvarāṇi ca//
children.translated_text: and <s>indīvara</s> (blue lotus)—these produce abundance and beauty of rut.

children.text: surasā gaṇḍasaṃyuktā punar navā gomaye 'thavā svinnā/
children.translated_text: <s>Surasā</s> (holy basil) combined with the cheek [rub], or <s>punarnavā</s> heated in cow dung,

children.text: vārāhīmūlāni ca nindanti guḍena yuktāni//
children.translated_text: and the roots of <s>vārāhī</s> combined with jaggery—these surpass [all others].

children.text: madhvālukā madhuyutā mukhaśobhām ātanoti nāgānām/
children.translated_text: <s>Madhvālukā</s> combined with honey extends the beauty of the face in elephants;

children.text: nekṣvāhārasya hito guḍena piṇḍo hito dadhnā//
children.translated_text: for those not eating sugarcane, a ball with jaggery is beneficial; with curd is beneficial.

children.text: māṣāśināṃ guḍayutastṛṇāśināṃ śasyate vasāyuktaḥ/
children.translated_text: For those eating black gram, [a ball] combined with jaggery; for those eating grass, [a ball] combined with fat is recommended;

children.text: vyatimiśrāhārāṇāṃ vijñāya balābalaṃ dadyāt//
children.translated_text: for those with mixed diet, one should give [the remedy] after ascertaining their strength and weakness.

children.text: prāyo madasya pavanaḥ kurute vighātaṃ srotāṃsy ato ghṛtayutair bahuśo 'sya piṇḍaiḥ/
children.translated_text: Generally, wind causes the obstruction of rut; therefore, with many balls mixed with ghee,

children.text: sa svedayed bhavati yena madapravṛddhir bhinnasya cāpi madavṛddhikarāṇi dadyāt//E81
children.translated_text: one should make the elephant sweat, by which the increase of rut occurs; and even to one whose [rut has] broken, one should give rut-increasing [substances].

children.text: dīrghagrīvākṣikūtas trikahṛdayapṛthus tāmratālvoṣṭhajihvaḥ(Bṣ 65.1)
children.translated_text: Long-necked, with prominent brow-ridge, broad in the withers, chest, and heart, with copper-colored palate, lips, and tongue,

children.text: sūkṣmatvakkeśavālaḥ suśaphagatimukho hrasvakarṇoṣṭhapucchaḥ/
children.translated_text: with fine skin, hair, and tail-hair, with good hooves, gait, and mouth, with short ears, lips, and tail,

children.text: jaṃghājānūruvṛttaḥ samasitadaśanaś cārusaṃsthānarūpo
children.translated_text: with round shanks, knees, and thighs, with even white teeth, of beautiful form and appearance—

children.text: vājī sarvāṅgaśuddho bhavati narapateḥ śatrunāśāya nityam//
children.translated_text: a horse pure in all limbs is always [fit] for the destruction of the king's enemies.

children.text: utsargān na śubhadam āsanāparasthaṃ vāme ca jvalanam ato 'paraṃ praśastam/(Bṣ 92.1)
children.translated_text: A horse with spontaneous [fiery marks] is not auspicious; [fire] behind the seat, and on the left, blazing—beyond that is praiseworthy;

children.text: sarvāṅgajvalanam avṛddhidaṃ hayānāṃ dve varṣe dahanakaṇāś ca dhūpanaṃ vā//
children.translated_text: blazing of all limbs is not growth-giving for horses; and fiery sparks or fumigation [are inauspicious] for two years.

children.text: antaḥpuraṃ nāśam upaiti meḍhre kośakṣayaṃ yāty udare pradīpte/(Bṣ 92.2)
children.translated_text: The inner quarters meet destruction when [fire appears] on the penis; the treasury diminishes when the belly is blazing;

children.text: pāyau ca pucche ca parājayaḥ syād vaktrottamāṅgajvalane jayaś ca//
children.translated_text: at the anus and tail, defeat would occur; and when the face and top of the head blaze, victory.

children.text: skandhāsanāṃśajvalanaṃ jayāya bandhāya pādajvalanaṃ pradiṣṭam/(Bṣ 92.3)
children.translated_text: Blazing of the shoulders, seat, and flanks is designated for victory; blazing of the feet is designated for captivity;

children.text: lalāṭavakṣo'kṣibhuje ca dhūmaḥ parābhavāya jvalanaṃ jayāya//
children.translated_text: smoke on the forehead, chest, eyes, and forelegs is for defeat; blazing is for victory.

children.text: nāsāpuṭaprothaśiro'śrupātanetre ca rātrau jvalanaṃ jayāya/(Bṣ 92.4)
children.translated_text: Blazing at night on the nostrils, muzzle, head, tears, and eyes is for victory;

children.text: pālāśatāmrāsitakarburāṇāṃ nityaṃ śukābhasya sitasya ceṣṭam//
children.translated_text: among [horses of] tawny, copper, dark, and piebald [colors], the parrot-colored and white are always desired.

children.text: pradveṣo yavasāmbhasāṃ prapatanaṃ svedo nimittād vinā(Bṣ 92.5)
children.translated_text: Aversion to barley and water, falling without cause, sweating without reason,

children.text: kampo vā vadanāc ca raktapatanaṃ dhūmasya vā saṃbhavaḥ/
children.translated_text: or trembling, and the falling of blood from the mouth, or the appearance of smoke,

children.text: asvapnaś ca virudhyatā niśi divā nidrālasadhyānatā
children.translated_text: and sleeplessness and hostility at night, and drowsiness and absent-mindedness during the day,

children.text: sādo 'dhomukhatā viceṣṭitam idaṃ neṣṭaṃ smṛtaṃ vājinām//
children.translated_text: dejection and hanging of the head—this behavior is declared inauspicious for horses.

children.text: ārohaṇam anyavājināṃ paryāṇādiyutasya vājinaḥ/(Bṣ 92.6)
children.translated_text: The mounting of other horses upon a horse that is equipped with saddle and other gear,

children.text: upavāhya turaṅgamasya vā kalpasyaiva vipanna śobhanā//
children.translated_text: or of a carriage horse—when the horse of that very equipment is ruined, that is auspicious.

children.text: krauñcavad ripuvadhāya hreṣitaṃ grīvayā tv acalayā ca sonmukham/(Bṣ 92.7)
children.translated_text: Neighing like a <s>krauñca</s> (heron) [indicates] the slaying of enemies; [neighing] with a motionless neck and facing forward,

children.text: snigdham uccam anunādi hṛṣṭavad grāsaruddhavadanaś ca vājibhiḥ//
children.translated_text: smooth, loud, resonant, and joyful, while the horse's mouth is full of food—[this is auspicious].

children.text: pūrṇapātradadhivipradevatā gandhapuṣpaphalakāñcanādi ca/(Bṣ 92.8)
children.translated_text: A full vessel, curd, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a deity, incense, flowers, fruits, gold, and similar [objects],

children.text: dravyamiṣṭam athavāparaṃ bhaved hreṣatā yadi samīpato jayaḥ//
children.translated_text: or other desired objects—if [a horse] neighs near [these], it means victory.

children.text: bhakṣyapānakhalinābhinandinaḥ patyur aupayikanandino 'thavā/(Bṣ 92.9)
children.translated_text: Horses that delight in their food, drink, and bridle, or that delight in what is suitable for their master,

children.text: savyapārśvagatadṛṣṭayo 'thavā vāñchirārthaphaladās turaṅgamāḥ//
children.translated_text: or that look to the left side—[these] horses yield the desired result.

children.text: vāmaiś ca pādair abhitāḍayanto mahīṃ pravāsāya bhavanti bharttuḥ/(Bṣ 92.10)
children.translated_text: Those that strike the ground with their left feet bring [their] master on a foreign journey;

children.text: sandhyāsu dīptām avalokayanto hreṣanti ced vandhaparājayāya//
children.translated_text: if they neigh while gazing at a blazing twilight, [it portends] defeat in captivity.

children.text: atīva hreṣanti kiranti bālān nidrāratāś ca pravadanti yātrām/(Bṣ 92.11)
children.translated_text: If they neigh excessively, scatter their young, are addicted to sleep, and announce a march,

children.text: romatyajā dīnakharasvarāṃś ca prāṃśūn grasantaś ca bhayāya diṣṭāḥ//
children.translated_text: shed their hair, make wretched harsh sounds, and consume tall [grass]—they are destined for danger.

children.text: samudgavad dakṣiṇapārśvaśāyinaḥ pādaṃ samutkṣipya ca dakṣiṇaṃ sthitāḥ/(Bṣ 92.12)
children.translated_text: Those that sleep on their right side like a casket, and that stand with the right foot raised,

children.text: jayāya śeṣeṣv api vāhaneṣv idaṃ phalaṃ yathāsaṃbhavam ādiśed budhaḥ//
children.translated_text: [indicate] victory; the wise should predict this result, as applicable, for other vehicles as well.

children.text: ārohati kṣitipatau vinayopapanno yātrā 'nugo 'nyaturagaṃ prati hreṣitaś ca/(Bṣ 92.13)
children.translated_text: When the king mounts [a horse] that is well-trained, that follows the march, that neighs toward another horse,

children.text: vakreṇa vā spṛśati dakṣiṇam ātmapārśvaṃ yo 'śvaḥ sa bhartur acirāt pracinoti lakṣmīm//
children.translated_text: or that touches its own right flank with a curve [of its neck]—that horse quickly gathers fortune for its master.

children.text: muhurmuhur mūtraśakṛt karoti na tāḍyamāno 'py anulomayāyī/
children.translated_text: One that repeatedly passes urine and dung, that goes in the right direction even when not beaten,

children.text: akāryabhīto 'śruvilocanaś ca śivaṃ na bharttus turago 'bhidhatte//E15
children.translated_text: that is afraid of wrongdoing and has tearful eyes—that horse does not bring welfare to its master.

children.text: aṅgulaśatārddham uttama ūnaḥ syāt pañcaviṃśatiḥ khaḍgaḥ/(Bṣ 49.1)
children.translated_text: Half of a hundred <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths) is the best [length]; a sword of twenty-five [<s>aṅgulas</s>] would be less;

children.text: aṃgulamānāj jñeyaḥ samāṃgulastho vraṇaḥ śubhadaḥ//
children.translated_text: it should be known by the <s>aṅgula</s> measure; a mark [<s>vraṇa</s>] situated at an even <s>aṅgula</s> is auspicious.

children.text: śrīvṛkṣavardhamānātapatraśivaliṅgakuṇḍalābjānām/(Bṣ 49.2)
children.translated_text: Marks resembling [the signs of] <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), a tree, <s>vardhamāna</s>, a parasol, a <s>Śivaliṅga</s>, an earring, and a lotus

children.text: sadṛśā vraṇāḥ praśastā dhvajāyudhasvastikānāṃ ca//
children.translated_text: are praiseworthy, as are [marks resembling] a banner, weapon, and <s>svastika</s>.

children.text: kṛkalāsakākakaṅkakravyādakabandhavṛścikākṛtayaḥ/(Bṣ 49.3)
children.translated_text: Marks on a sword resembling a lizard, crow, heron, vulture, headless trunk, and scorpion

children.text: khaḍge vraṇā na śubhadā vaṃśānugatāḥ prabhūtāś ca//
children.translated_text: are not auspicious; nor are those that follow the lineage [pattern] or are too numerous.

children.text: sphuṭito hrasvaḥ kuṇṭho vaṃśacchinno na dṛṅmano 'nugataḥ/(Bṣ 49.4)
children.translated_text: A sword that is cracked, short, blunt, broken in the blade, not following the eye and mind [in its swing],

children.text: asvara iti cāniṣṭaḥ proktaviparyasta iṣṭaphalaḥ//
children.translated_text: and soundless—is declared inauspicious; the opposite of what has been stated gives auspicious results.

children.text: kvaṇitaṃ maraṇāyoktaṃ parājayāyāpravarttanam kośāt/(Bṣ 49.5)
children.translated_text: Vibrating [of a sword] is declared [to portend] death; non-emergence from the sheath [portends] defeat;

children.text: svayam udgīrṇe yuddhaṃ jvalite vijayo bhavati khaḍge//
children.translated_text: when a sword emerges on its own, [it portends] battle; when the sword blazes, there is victory.

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ vivṛṇuyān na vighaṭṭayec ca paśyen na tatra vadanaṃ na vadec ca mūlyam/(Bṣ 49.6)
children.translated_text: One should not unsheathe it without reason, nor strike it; one should not look at one's face in it, nor state its price;

children.text: deśaṃ na vāsya kathayet pratimānayec ca naiva spṛśen nṛpatir aprayato 'siyaṣṭim//
children.translated_text: one should not mention its origin, but should pay respect to it; the king should not touch the sword-handle while impure.

children.text: gojihvāsaṃsthāno nīlotpalavaṃśapatrasadṛśaś ca/(Bṣ 49.7)
children.translated_text: A sword shaped like a cow's tongue, or resembling a blue lotus leaf, or a bamboo leaf,

children.text: karavīrapatrasadṛśaś candramaṇḍalāgraḥ praśastaś ca//
children.translated_text: or resembling a <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) leaf, with a crescent-shaped tip—is praiseworthy.

children.text: niṣpanno na chedyo nikaṣaiḥ kāryaḥ pramāṇayuktaḥ saḥ/(Bṣ 49.8)
children.translated_text: Once forged, it should not be cut; it should be tested on touchstones; it should be of proper measure;

children.text: mṛte mriyate svāmī jananī tasyāgrataś chinne//
children.translated_text: when it dies [breaks], the master dies; when its tip is cut, [the king's] mother [dies].

children.text: yasmin tsarupradeśe vraṇo bhavet tadvad eva khaḍgasya/(Bṣ 49.9)
children.translated_text: Whatever mark exists on the handle portion of the sword, the same [mark applies] to the sword [in divination];

children.text: vanitānām iva tilakaṃ guhye vācyo mukhe dṛṣṭvā//
children.translated_text: like a beauty mark on women—what is on the face should be stated about the hidden [part], upon seeing it.

children.text: athavā spṛśati yad aṅgaṃ praṣṭā nistriṃśabhṛt tad avadhārya/(Bṣ 49.10)
children.translated_text: Or else, whichever limb the inquirer touches while holding the sword—having noted that,

children.text: kośasthasyādeśyo vraṇo 'siśāstraṃ viditvedam//
children.translated_text: the mark should be predicted for the sheathed [sword], knowing this sword-science.

children.text: śirasi spṛṣṭe prathame 'ṅgule dvitīye lalāṭasaṃsparśe/(Bṣ 49.11)
children.translated_text: When the head is touched, [the mark is] at the first <s>aṅgula</s>; at the second, when the forehead is touched;

children.text: bhrūmadhye ca tṛtīye netre spṛṣṭe caturthe ca//
children.translated_text: at the third, in the middle of the eyebrows; at the fourth, when the eye is touched;

children.text: nāsauṣṭhakapolahanuśravaṇagrīvāṃśakeṣu pañcādyāḥ/(Bṣ 49.12)
children.translated_text: the nose, lip, cheek, chin, ear, neck, and shoulder [correspond to the] fifth onward.

children.text: urasi dvādaśasaṃsthaḥ trayodaśe kakṣayor jñeyaḥ//
children.translated_text: placed in the twelfth [position], it is on the chest; in the thirteenth, it should be known as on the armpits.

children.text: stanahṛdayodarakukṣau nābhau ca caturdaśādayo jñeyāḥ/(Bṣ 49.13)
children.translated_text: In the fourteenth and following [positions], it should be known as on the breasts, heart, belly, flanks, and navel. (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.13)

children.text: nābhīmūle kaṭyāṃ guhye caikonaviṃśatitaḥ syāt//
children.translated_text: At the base of the navel, on the waist, and on the genitals—from the nineteenth [position] onward.

children.text: ūrvor dvāviṃśe syād ūrvor madhye vraṇas trayoviṃśe/(Bṣ 49.14)
children.translated_text: The twenty-second is on the thighs; in the twenty-third, the wound is in the middle of the thighs. (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.14)

children.text: jānuni ca caturviṃśe jaghāyāṃ pañcaviṃśe syāt//
children.translated_text: In the twenty-fourth, on the knee; in the twenty-fifth, it is on the lower leg.

children.text: jaṅghāmadhye gulphe pārṣṇyāṃ pāde tathāṅgulīṣv api ca/(Bṣ 49.5)
children.translated_text: In the middle of the calf, on the ankle, on the heel, on the foot, and also on the toes— (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.5[=15])

children.text: ṣaḍviṃśādiṣu yāvat triṃśād iti matena gargasya//
children.translated_text: from the twenty-sixth onward up to the thirtieth, according to the view of <s>Garga</s>.

children.text: putramaraṇaṃ dhanāptir dhanahāniḥ sampadaś ca vadhaś ca/(Bṣ 49.16)
children.translated_text: Death of a son, gain of wealth, loss of wealth, prosperity, and slaughter— (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.16)

children.text: ekādyaṃgulasaṃsthair vraṇaiḥ phalaṃ nirdiśet kramaśaḥ//
children.translated_text: the results should be predicted in order according to wounds situated on the first and subsequent fingers.

children.text: sutalābhaḥ kalaho hastilayaḥ putramaraṇadhanalābhau/(Bṣ 49.17)
children.translated_text: Gain of a son, quarrel, loss of an elephant, death of a son, and gain of wealth— (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.17)

children.text: kramaśo vināśavanitāpticittaduḥkhāni ṣaṭprabhṛti//
children.translated_text: in order: ruin, acquisition of a woman, mental sorrow—from the sixth onward.

children.text: labdhir hānistrīlayo vadho vṛdhimaraṇaparitoṣāḥ/(Bṣ 49.18)
children.translated_text: Gain, loss, loss of a wife, slaughter, increase, death, and contentment— (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.18)

children.text: jñeyāś ca caturdaśādiṣu dhanahāniś caikaviṃśe syāt//
children.translated_text: should be known from the fourteenth onward; in the twenty-first, there would be loss of wealth.

children.text: vittāptir anirvāṇaṃ dhanāgamo mṛtyusampado 'svatvam/(Bṣ 49.19)
children.translated_text: Acquisition of wealth, distress, arrival of wealth, death, prosperity, loss of sovereignty, (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.19)

children.text: aiśvaryamṛtyurājyāni ca kramāt triṃśad iti yāvat//
children.translated_text: sovereignty, death, and kingdoms—in order up to the thirtieth.

children.text: parato na viśeṣaphalaṃ viṣamasamasthāś ca pāpaśubhaphaladāḥ/(Bṣ 49.20)
children.translated_text: Beyond that, there is no specific result; [wounds] in odd and even positions yield inauspicious and auspicious results [respectively]. (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.20)

children.text: kaiś cid aphalāḥ pradiṣṭās triṃśat parato 'gram iti yāvat//
children.translated_text: By some, those beyond thirty up to the tip are declared to be without result.

children.text: karavīrotpalagajamadaghṛtakuṃkumakundacampakasugandhiḥ/(Bṣ 49.21)
children.translated_text: A scent resembling <s>karavīra</s> (oleander), <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), elephant-rut fluid, ghee, <s>kuṃkuma</s> (saffron), <s>kunda</s> (jasmine), and <s>campaka</s>— (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.21)

children.text: śubhado gomūtraharitālapaṅkamedasadṛśagandhiḥ//
children.translated_text: such a fragrance is auspicious; one resembling cow-urine, yellow orpiment, mud, or fat—

children.text: kūrmavasā 'sṭakakṣāropamaś ca bhayaduḥkhado bhavati gandhaḥ/(Bṣ 49.22)
children.translated_text: and one resembling tortoise-fat, <s>aṣṭaka</s>-alkali—such a scent causes fear and sorrow. (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.22)

children.text: vaidūryakanakavidyutprabho jayārogyavṛddhikaraḥ//
children.translated_text: A radiance like <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), gold, or lightning bestows victory, health, and prosperity.

children.text: idam aiśanasañ ca śastrapānaṃ rudhireṇa śriyam icchataḥ pradīptām/(Bṣ 49.23)
children.translated_text: This <s>aiśāna</s> (northeastern) [ritual] involves the drinking of the weapon [prepared] with blood for one who desires blazing glory; (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.23)

children.text: haviṣā guṇavat sutābhilipsoḥ salilenākṣayam icchataś ca vittam//
children.translated_text: with <s>havis</s> (oblation), it is beneficial for one desiring virtuous sons; with water, for one desiring inexhaustible wealth.

children.text: vaḍavoṣṭrakareṇadugdhapānaṃ yadi pāpena samīhate 'rthasidhiḥ/(Bṣ 49.24)
children.translated_text: If one seeks accomplishment of one's goal through evil means, [one should use] the drinking of mare's, camel's, or she-elephant's milk; (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.24)

children.text: jhaṣapittamṛgāśvavastadugdhaiḥ karihastacchidaye satālagarbhaiḥ/
children.translated_text: with the bile of fish, the milk of deer, horse, and goat—for piercing the trunk of an elephant, mixed with <s>tālagarbha</s> (palm pith).

children.text: ārkaṃ payo huḍaviṣāṇamaṣīsametaṃ pārāvatākhuśakṛtā ca yutaṃ praleṣaḥ/(Bṣ 49.25)
children.translated_text: Milk of the <s>arka</s> plant, mixed with buffalo horn and lampblack, combined with pigeon and mouse dung, used as a coating— (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.25)

children.text: śastrasya tailamathitasya tato 'sya pānaṃ paścāc chritasya na śilāsu bhaved vighātaḥ//
children.translated_text: then the drinking of the weapon after its oil has been churned and subsequently heated—it will not break on stones.

children.text: kṣāre kadanyā mathitena yukte dinoṣite pāyutamāyasaṃ yat/(Bṣ 49.26)
children.translated_text: When iron is made to drink [a solution of] alkali mixed with churned <s>kadanya</s> (millet), heated for a day— (Bṛhatsaṃhitā 49.26)

children.text: samyak chiritaṃ cāśmani naiti bhaṅgam na cānyalauheṣv api tasya kauṣṭhyam//E26
children.translated_text: when properly cooled on stone, it does not break, nor does it become brittle against other metals.

children.text: antaḥpurād vā svaniveśanād vā siṃhāsanād agniparistarād vā/
children.translated_text: From the inner chambers, or from his own residence, or from the throne, or from the fire-altar,

children.text: kuryān narendraḥ prathamaṃ prayāṇaṃ vipraiḥ śatāgraiḥ kṛtamaṅgalāśīḥ//
children.translated_text: the king should make his first departure, with auspicious blessings recited by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> led by hundreds.

children.text: dvijo viṣṇukramād bhūyaṃ mantreṇānena dāpayet/
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should then cause [the king] to take the <s>Viṣṇukrama</s> (strides of <s>Viṣṇu</s>) with this <s>mantra</s>:

children.text: idaṃ viṣṇur vicakrama ity evaṃ pādam uddharet//
children.translated_text: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode forth thus'—with these words he should raise his foot.

children.text: amukasya vadhāyeti dakṣiṇaṃ kṣitipo nyaset/% Kane V. 621
children.translated_text: 'For the slaying of [enemy name]'—thus the king should place his right [foot].

children.text: maṅgalāni tataḥ paśyan spṛśan śṛṇvan nṛpo vrajet//
children.translated_text: Then the king should proceed, seeing, touching, and hearing auspicious things.

children.text: vedāṅgavedadhvaniśaṅkhabherīmṛdaṅgapuṇyāhapurāṇaśabdāḥ/
children.translated_text: The sounds of the <s>Vedāṅgas</s> and <s>Vedas</s>, conch shells, <s>bherī</s> drums, <s>mṛdaṅga</s> drums, auspicious recitations (<s>puṇyāha</s>), and <s>Purāṇa</s> texts,

children.text: dharmarthaśāstrāṇi ca bhārataṃ ca rāmāyaṇaṃ maṅgalakīrttanāni//
children.translated_text: treatises on <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>, the <s>Bhārata</s>, the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, and auspicious songs—

children.text: vācaḥ śubhāḥ sārasacāṣavarhiṇaḥ kādambahaṃsāś ca sajīvajīvakāḥ/
children.translated_text: auspicious words; the <s>sārasa</s> (crane), <s>cāṣa</s> (blue jay), peacock, <s>kādamba</s> (wild goose), swans, and <s>jīvajīvaka</s> birds;

children.text: kākaś ca paṅkāktavarāhapṛṣṭhagaḥ śrīvṛkṣavālavyajanāni candanam//
children.translated_text: a crow standing on the back of a mud-smeared boar; the <s>śrīvṛkṣa</s> (holy fig tree), <s>vāla</s>-fans, and sandalwood;

children.text: gaurvatsalā 'jo rucakaḥ p(r)iyaṅgulājā nṛyuktaś ca rathāḥ patākā/
children.translated_text: a cow with her calf, a goat, a gold piece (<s>rucaka</s>), <s>priyaṅgu</s> (millet), sesamum, a man-drawn chariot, banners,

children.text: sarvauṣadhī svastikapūrṇapātrāṇy aśvo 'tha dūrvādrakagomayaṃ ca//
children.translated_text: all herbs, <s>svastika</s> symbols, full vessels, a horse, <s>dūrvā</s> grass, ginger, and cow-dung;

children.text: sarāṃsy aśoṣyāni saritsamudrā rudrendralokeśamahīdhranāgāḥ/
children.translated_text: lakes that never dry up, rivers, oceans; <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the guardians of the world, and great mountains and <s>Nāgas</s>;

children.text: diśo graharkṣāṇi śivaḥ suparṇaḥ skando viśākho marutaś ca sādhyāḥ//
children.translated_text: the directions, planets and stars, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Suparṇa</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Viśākha</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, and the <s>Sādhyas</s>;

children.text: bhūr dvādaśārkā vasavo 'śvinau ca svāhā śācī mātṛgaṇo bhavānī/
children.translated_text: the Earth, the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>, <s>Śacī</s>, the host of Mothers (<s>Mātṛgaṇa</s>), <s>Bhavānī</s>,

children.text: patnyo jananyaś ca surāsurāṇāṃ sādhyogaṇāś cāpsarasaḥ savidyāḥ//
children.translated_text: the wives and mothers of gods and <s>Asuras</s>, the hosts of <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Apsarases</s> together with the <s>Vidyās</s>,

children.text: yakṣāḥ sasiddhā munayaḥ sajāyāḥ parjanyakampadrumamārutāś ca/
children.translated_text: <s>Yakṣas</s> together with <s>Siddhas</s>, sages with their wives, <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god), earthquakes, trees, and winds,

children.text: prajāpatiḥ sarvagataś ca viṣṇuḥ śivāya te bhūpa bhavantu yāne//
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> who pervades all—may they all be for your welfare, O King, on your campaign!

children.text: siddhārthakādarśapayoñjanāni baddhaikapaśvāmiṣapūrṇakumbhāḥ/
children.translated_text: White mustard seeds, mirrors, milk, collyrium, a bound single animal, full pots of meat,

children.text: uṣṇīṣabhṛṅgāranṛvardhamānapuṃyānavīṇātapavāraṇāni//
children.translated_text: turbans, water-pitchers, men, a <s>vardhamāna</s> (prosperity vessel), male vehicles, <s>vīṇās</s>, and parasols;

children.text: dadhi madhu ghṛta rocanā kumārī dhvajakanakāmbujabhadrapīṭhaśaṅkhāḥ/
children.translated_text: curds, honey, ghee, <s>gorocanā</s>, a young girl, banners, gold, lotuses, an auspicious seat (<s>bhadrapīṭha</s>), conch shells,

children.text: sitavṛṣakusumāmbarāṇi mīnadvijagaṇikāptajanāś ca cāruveṣāḥ//
children.translated_text: a white bull, flowers, white garments, fish, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, courtesans, trusted people—all beautifully attired;

children.text: jvalitaśikhiphalākṣatekṣubhakṣyā dviradamṛdaṅkuśacāmarāyudhāni/
children.translated_text: blazing fire, peacock-tail [fans], unbroken rice (<s>akṣata</s>), sugarcane, eatables, elephants, drums, goads, <s>cāmara</s> whisks, weapons,

children.text: marakatakuruvindapadmarāgāḥ sphatikamaṇipramukhāś ca ratnamedāḥ//
children.translated_text: emeralds, rubies, padmarāga gems, crystal, and other jewels and precious stones—

children.text: svayam atha racitāny ayatnato vā yadi kathitāni bhavanti maṅgalāni/
children.translated_text: if these auspicious things are found arranged by oneself or occurring without effort,

children.text: sa jayati sakalāṃ tato dharitrīṃ prahaṇadṛgālabhanaśrutair upāsya//
children.translated_text: then he conquers the entire earth, having attended to [them] through seeing, touching, and hearing.

children.text: kārpāsauṣadhakṛṣṇadhānyalavaṇaklīvāsthitailaṃ vasā
children.translated_text: Cotton, herbs, black grain, salt, a eunuch, bones, oil, fat,

children.text: paṅkāṅgāraguḍāhicarmaśakṛtaḥ keśāya savyādhitāḥ/
children.translated_text: mud, charcoal, jaggery, snakeskin, dung, hair, and the sick;

children.text: vāntonmattajaḍendhanatṛṇatuṣakṣutkṣāmatakrārayo
children.translated_text: one who has vomited, the insane, the dull-witted, firewood, grass, chaff, the hungry, the emaciated, buttermilk, enemies,

children.text: muṇḍābhyaktavimuktakeśapatitāḥ kāṣāvinaś cāśubhāḥ//
children.translated_text: those with shaved heads, the anointed, those with loose hair, the fallen, and those in saffron garments—these are inauspicious.

children.text: paṭupaṭahamṛdaṅgaśaṅkhabherīvaṇavaradaṃ sapatākatoraṇāgram/
children.translated_text: He should proceed on a road that resounds with sharp drums, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, conch shells, <s>bherīs</s>, and <s>paṇava</s> drums, with flags and arched gateways at its head,

children.text: pracurakusumatoyaśāntareṇuṃ surabhisuveṣajanaṃ vrajec ca mārgam//
children.translated_text: abundant with flowers and water, dust settled, fragrant, with well-dressed people.

children.text: yāny atra maṅgalāmaṅgalāni nirgacchatāṃ pradiṣṭāni/
children.translated_text: The auspicious and inauspicious [signs] taught here for those setting out

children.text: svapneṣv apy etāni śubhāśubhāni viḍlepanaṃ dhanyam//
children.translated_text: are the same auspicious and inauspicious ones in dreams as well; smearing with dung is auspicious [in dreams].

children.text: chuchundarī śūkarikā śivā ca śyāmā ralā piṅgalikā 'nyapuṣṭā/
children.translated_text: The musk-shrew, sow, jackal-bird (<s>śivā</s>), the dark one (<s>śyāmā</s>), <s>ralā</s>, the tawny one (<s>piṅgalikā</s>), the cuckoo (<s>anyapuṣṭā</s>),

children.text: vāmā praśastā gṛhagodhikā ca puṃsaṃjñakā ye ca patatriṇaḥ syuḥ//
children.translated_text: the wagtail (<s>vāmā</s>) is auspicious, as is the house-lizard (<s>gṛhagodhikā</s>), and those birds that bear masculine names.

children.text: śyeno ruruḥ pūrṇakuṭaḥ kapiś ca śrīkarṇachikkārakapippikā 'jāḥ/
children.translated_text: The hawk (<s>śyena</s>), the <s>ruru</s> deer, the <s>pūrṇakuṭa</s> bird, the monkey,

children.text: strīsaṃjñakā ye ca śikhidvipau ca yāne hitā dakṣiṇabhāgasaṃsthāḥ//
children.translated_text: the <s>śrīkarṇa</s>, <s>chikkāraka</s>, <s>pippikā</s>, goats, those bearing feminine names, and the peacock and elephant—these are beneficial on a march when positioned on the right side.

children.text: āsphoṭitākṣveḍitaśaṅkhatūryapuṃyāhavedadhvanigītaśabdāḥ/
children.translated_text: The sounds of clapping, shouting, conch shells, trumpets, auspicious recitations (<s>puṃyāha</s>), Vedic chanting, and singing—

children.text: vāmāḥ prayāṇe śubhadā narāṇām ākranditaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ pareṣām//
children.translated_text: these on the left are auspicious for men on a march; the crying [of these] from the right [is auspicious] for the enemies.

children.text: bhāradvājyajavarhicāṣanakulāḥ saṅkīrttanād darśanāt
children.translated_text: The lark (<s>bhāradvājī</s>), the partridge, the peacock, the blue jay (<s>cāṣa</s>), and the mongoose—by being named, seen,

children.text: krośantaś ca śubhapradā na saraṭo dṛṣṭaḥ śivāya kvacit/
children.translated_text: or crying out, they are auspicious; the chameleon (<s>saraṭa</s>) is never seen as auspicious.

children.text: godhāśūkarajāhakāhiśaśakāḥ pāṣā rutālokane
children.translated_text: The monitor lizard (<s>godhā</s>), boar, <s>jāhaka</s> bird, snake, and hare—by their sound and sight [give different results];

children.text: dhanyaṃ kīrttanam ṛkṣavānaraphalaṃ tad vyatyayāc chobhanam//
children.translated_text: their mention is auspicious; bear and monkey [give] the same result; the opposite is also good.

children.text: nakulasya mṛgasya pakṣiṇāṃ vāmād dakṣiṇabhāgasevanam/
children.translated_text: For the mongoose, deer, and birds, attending from left to right

children.text: śubhadaṃ śvaśṛgālayor idaṃ vyatyāsena phalaṃ praśasyate//
children.translated_text: is auspicious; for the dog and jackal, the result is praised in the reverse order.

children.text: cāṣo nakulaś ca vāmagau divasārdhāt parataḥ śubhapradau/
children.translated_text: The blue jay (<s>cāṣa</s>) and mongoose moving leftward are auspicious after midday;

children.text: mṛgavac ca vaneṣu kukkurāḥ śatapatro 'stamaye ca dakṣiṇaḥ//
children.translated_text: dogs in forests [behave] like deer; the <s>śatapatra</s> (woodpecker) at sunset on the right [is auspicious].

children.text: naṣṭāvalokanasamāgamayuddhakramaveśmapraveśam anujeśvaradarśaneṣu/
children.translated_text: In matters of [finding] the lost, gaining sight, encounters, battles, marching, entering a dwelling, and meeting a lord,

children.text: yānapratīpavidhinā śubhadā bhavanti kecij jagur gamanavan nṛpadarśaneṣu//
children.translated_text: the omens are auspicious by the reverse method of the march; some have said that in audiences with kings, [they work] as in marching.

children.text: nirupahatamanojñavṛkṣasaṃsthaḥ śucirucirāvanisasyasaṃsthitāś ca/
children.translated_text: Situated on undamaged, beautiful trees, or standing on clean, beautiful, crop-bearing land,

children.text: śubhatithidivasarkṣalagnakāleṣv aśubhaphalo 'pi śubhapradaḥ pradiṣṭaḥ//
children.translated_text: even an inauspicious [bird] is declared to give auspicious results on auspicious <s>tithis</s>, days, <s>nakṣatras</s>, <s>lagnas</s>, and times.

children.text: prabhagnaśuṣkadrumakaṇṭakeṣu śmaśānabhasmāsthituṣākuleṣu/
children.translated_text: On broken, dry trees with thorns, in cremation grounds strewn with ashes, bones, and husks,

children.text: prākāraśūnyālayadurdṛśeṣu saumyo 'pi pāpaḥ śakunaḥ pradiṣṭaḥ//
children.translated_text: near ruined walls, empty buildings, and ill-looking places—even a benign bird is declared inauspicious.

children.text: aṅgāriṇī dig raviṇā pramuktā yasyāṃ ravis tiṣṭhati sā pradīptā/
children.translated_text: The direction released by the Sun bears embers (<s>aṅgāriṇī</s>); the one where the Sun stands is blazing (<s>pradīptā</s>);

children.text: pradhūmitā yāsyati yāṃ dineśaḥ śeṣāś ca śāntāḥ śubhadāś ca tāḥ syuḥ//
children.translated_text: the one the Sun will go to is smoky (<s>pradhūmitā</s>); the remaining ones are peaceful and auspicious.

children.text: yātaṃ muktāyāṃ sāmprataṃ dīpitāyām eṣyaṃ jñeyaṃ dhūmitāyām aniṣṭam/
children.translated_text: Travel in the released [direction] is [auspicious]; inauspicious in the blazing one at the present time; in the smoky one, the coming [result] should be known as unfavorable.

children.text: śāntāsv evaṃ dikṣu tatpañcamāsu pratyāsannaṃ śeṣayoḥ śāntadīptam//
children.translated_text: In the peaceful directions, and in the fifth from each of those—the result is near [in time]; in the remaining two, [the result is] peaceful and blazing [respectively].

children.text: piśitāśucibhojanaḥ pradīptas tṛṇaphalabhuk ca nisargataḥ praśāntaḥ/
children.translated_text: One that eats flesh and impure food is blazing by nature; one that eats grass and fruits is peaceful by nature;

children.text: ubhayaḥ kathitas tathānnabhojī diksthānodayakālataś ca cintyāḥ//
children.translated_text: one that eats both is declared [to be of] both [natures], as also a food-eater; [these] should be considered according to direction, position, rising, and time.

children.text: dvandvārttarogārditabhītamattavairārttayuddhāmiṣakāṃkṣiṇaś ca/
children.translated_text: Those afflicted by mating, pain, disease, injury, fear, or intoxication, those distressed by enmity, in battle, or seeking food,

children.text: sīmāntanadyantaritāś ca serve na cintanīyāḥ sadasatphaleṣu//
children.translated_text: and all those separated by a boundary, stream, or river—these should not be considered for auspicious or inauspicious results.

children.text: rikto 'nukūlaḥ kalaśo jalārtham abhyudyataḥ siddhikaraḥ prayāṇe/
children.translated_text: An empty [vessel seen] facing [the traveler] is a water-pot; one coming toward [the traveler] who is about to set forth brings success on the journey,

children.text: vidyārthināṃ cauryasamudyatānāṃ vaṇikkriyābhyudyaminām atīva//
children.translated_text: especially for those seeking knowledge, those about to commit theft, merchants, and those engaged in trade.

children.text: śyāmāśyenaśaśaghnavañjalaśikhiśrīkarṇacakrāhvayāś
children.translated_text: The <s>śyāmā</s>, hawk (<s>śyena</s>), hare-killer, <s>vañjala</s>, peacock, <s>śrīkarṇa</s>, <s>cakra</s> (ruddy sheldrake),

children.text: cāṣāṇdīrakakhañjarīṭakaśukāḥ dhvāṃkṣaḥ kapotās trayaḥ/
children.translated_text: the blue jay (<s>cāṣa</s>), <s>āṇḍīraka</s>, wagtail (<s>khañjarīṭaka</s>), parrot, crow, and three types of pigeon;

children.text: bhāradvājakulālakukkuṭakharā hārītagṛdhrau kapis
children.translated_text: the lark (<s>bhāradvāja</s>), potter-bird (<s>kulāla</s>), rooster, donkey, green pigeon (<s>hārīta</s>), vulture, monkey,

children.text: pheṭau kukkurapūrṇakūṭacaṭakāś coktā divāsaṃcarāḥ//
children.translated_text: the <s>pheṭa</s> (owl), dog, <s>pūrṇakūṭa</s>, and sparrow—these are declared to be active during the day.

children.text: lomāsikā piṅgalachappikākhyau valgulyulūkau śaśakaś ca rātrau/
children.translated_text: The <s>lomāsikā</s>, <s>piṅgala</s>, <s>chappikā</s>, the bat (<s>valgulī</s>), the owl (<s>ulūka</s>), and the hare—these are active at night.

children.text: sarve svakālotkramacāriṇaḥ syur daśasya nāśāya nṛpān tadā vā//
children.translated_text: All those moving outside their proper time would [portend] the destruction of the army, or of the king at that time.

children.text: hayanarabhujagoṣṭradvīpisiṃharkṣagodhāvṛkanakulakuraṅgaśvājagovyāghrahaṃsāḥ/
children.translated_text: Horse, man, snake, buffalo, elephant, lion, bear, monitor lizard, wolf, mongoose, antelope, dog, goat, cow, tiger, swan,

children.text: pṛṣatamṛgaśṛgālaśvāvidhākhyā 'nyapuṣṭā dyuniśam api viḍālaḥ sārasaḥ śūkaraś ca//
children.translated_text: spotted deer, jackal, porcupine (so-called <s>anyapuṣṭā</s>)—and the cat and crane (<s>sārasa</s>) and boar are active both day and night.

children.text: dyuniśobhayacāriṇaḥ svakāle puravanamiśracarāḥ svabhūmisaṃsthāḥ/
children.translated_text: Those active both day and night, when in their own time, moving in town, forest, or mixed terrain, in their own proper ground,

children.text: saphalā viphalā viparyayasthā gamanepsoḥ purapārthivāśubhās te//
children.translated_text: yield results; placed contrarily, they are fruitless; for one desiring to march, those in the city are inauspicious for the king.

children.text: yānaṃ dhureṇa patitaṃ bṛhatī ca kanyā garbheṇa cātimahatā purataḥ sthito strī/
children.translated_text: A vehicle fallen on its yoke, a very tall maiden, a woman standing in front with a very large belly,

children.text: āgaccha tiṣṭha viśa gacchasi vā kim arthaṃ śabdāḥ sthiraś ca gamanaṃ pratiṣedhayanti//
children.translated_text: 'Come! Stop! Enter! Where are you going?'—such words, and a firm [obstacle], prevent the journey.

children.text: gāndhāraṣaḍjaṛṣabhāḥ khalu madhyamaś ca yāne svarāḥ śubhakarā na tu ye 'tra śeṣāḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Gāndhāra</s>, <s>Ṣaḍja</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, and <s>Madhyama</s>—these are the musical notes (<s>svaras</s>) auspicious for a march; the remaining ones are not.

children.text: grāmau śubhāv api ca madhyamaṣaḍjasañjñau gāndhāragītam api bhadram uśanti devāḥ//
children.translated_text: The two scales (<s>grāmas</s>) called <s>Madhyama</s> and <s>Ṣaḍja</s> are auspicious; singing in the <s>Gāndhāra</s> [scale] is also regarded as auspicious by the gods.

children.text: sarvatra pāpaṃ kṣutam uddiśanti gos tu kṣutaṃ mṛtyukaraṃ yiyāsoḥ/
children.translated_text: Everywhere, sneezing is declared inauspicious; but the sneezing of a cow is death-producing for one about to march.

children.text: mārjārarāvaskhalanaṃ ca yātur vastrasya bhaṅgaś ca na śobhanāni//
children.translated_text: The cry of a cat, stumbling of the traveler, and tearing of a garment are not auspicious.

children.text: jalakaraśvakarau na śubhau prāgghātakaśastrakarau yamadiksthau/
children.translated_text: One carrying water or a hand-saw is not auspicious in the east; a butcher or one carrying weapons standing in the south (<s>Yama</s>'s direction) [is inauspicious];

children.text: ṣaṇḍhakamadyakarāv api paścāt āsanasīrakhalaiḥ saha codak//
children.translated_text: a eunuch or one carrying liquor in the west; and in the north, one with a seat, a plough, or a threshing floor.

children.text: dravyāṇi śuklāni turaṅgamaś ca pūrveṇa yāmyena śavaṃ samāsam/
children.translated_text: White objects and a horse in the east; a corpse, briefly, in the south;

children.text: paścāt kumārī dadhi cātiśastaṃ saumyena gobrāhmaṇasādhavaś ca//
children.translated_text: in the west, a maiden and curds are very auspicious; in the north, cows, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and virtuous people.

children.text: yaḥ pūrṇakūṭaḥ sakarāyikākhyo vāmaḥ praśastaḥ sa ca pūrvadeśe/
children.translated_text: The <s>pūrṇakūṭa</s> bird, also called <s>karāyikā</s>, on the left is auspicious and [particularly so] in the eastern quarter;

children.text: kākaḥ śubho dakṣiṇataś ca teṣām anyeṣu deśeṣu viparyayeṇa//
children.translated_text: the crow is auspicious on the right; in other directions, the reverse applies.

children.text: vāme śasto dhanvanaḥ siddhidātā prottuṅgaś ced dhastamātram jayāya/
children.translated_text: The rainbow on the left is auspicious, granting success; if raised high to the height of a hand, it means victory;

children.text: ākāyaś ced unnato vāmabhāge pṛthvīlābhaṃ dhanvanāgaḥ karoti//
children.translated_text: if the rainbow rises high on the left side while being bodiless [i.e., not touching the ground], it brings acquisition of territory.

children.text: naraturagagajātapatrakumbhadhvajaśayanāsanapuṣpacāmarāṇi/
children.translated_text: If a man, horse, elephant, bird, pot, banner, bed, seat, flower, or <s>cāmara</s> whisk

children.text: vrajati yadi puro 'vamūtrya yātuḥ kṣapayati śatrubalaṃ tato narendraḥ//
children.translated_text: passes before the marcher after urinating, the king thereby destroys the enemy's army.

children.text: viṣakaṇṭakiśuṣkavṛkṣaloṣṭān avamūtryāsthicitena yāti cec chvā/
children.translated_text: If a dog passes after urinating on poison, thorny plants, dry trees, or clods of earth,

children.text: na śubho 'bhimukho bhaṣan vidhunvan yudhyan gāṃ vilikhan nakhair vamaṃś ca//
children.translated_text: or stands on bones—it is not auspicious. [Nor is it auspicious when a dog comes] facing [the traveler], barking, shaking, fighting, scratching the ground with its nails, or vomiting.

children.text: uttānāpādaḥ svapate ca pāpo vilokya sūryaṃ viruvaṃś ca dīnam/
children.translated_text: One sleeping with paws upward is inauspicious; looking at the sun and howling pitifully [is inauspicious];

children.text: śuṣkāsthilābhābhimukhaś ca kaṣṭo māṃsādibhiḥ pūrṇamukhaś ca śastaḥ//
children.translated_text: one approaching dry bones is dire; but one with its mouth full of meat and such is auspicious.

children.text: pūrṇānano yasya kroti cāṣaḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ svastikam eva vā khe/
children.translated_text: When a blue jay (<s>cāṣa</s>), with its beak full, makes a clockwise circuit or a <s>svastika</s> pattern in the sky [around the traveler],

children.text: lābho mahāntasya parābhavāya kālena bhaṅgo vijayo jayo 'sya//
children.translated_text: there is gain for the great one and defeat for the enemy; in time, his reversal [turns into] victory.

children.text: kāryantu mūlaśakune 'ntaraje tad ahni vindyāt phalaṃ niyatam evam ime vicintyāḥ/
children.translated_text: The result of the root omen and the intermediate omen should be known on that [same] day without fail; these should be considered thus.

children.text: prāraṃbhayānasamayeṣu tathā praveśe grāhyaṃ kṣutan na śubhadaṃ kvacid apy uśanti//
children.translated_text: At the times of beginning, departure, and entry—sneezing is not declared auspicious anywhere.

children.text: krośād ūrdhvaṃ śakunavirutaṃ niṣphalaṃ prāhur eke
children.translated_text: Some say that the cry of a bird beyond a <s>krośa</s> (about 2 miles) is fruitless;

children.text: tatrāniṣṭe prathamaśakune mānayet pañca ṣaṭ ca/
children.translated_text: when the first omen is inauspicious, one should honor five or six

children.text: prāṇāyāmān nṛpatir aśubhe ṣoḍaśaivaṃ dvitīye
children.translated_text: <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls); if the second is inauspicious, [honor] sixteen; if the king [encounters inauspiciousness thus],

children.text: pratyāgacchet svabhavanam ato yady aniṣṭas tṛtīyaḥ//
children.translated_text: he should return to his own residence if the third [omen] is also inauspicious.

children.text: śubhaṃ daśāpākam avighnasiddhiṃ mūlābhirakṣām athavā sahāyān/
children.translated_text: The auspicious [results are]: favorable period-results (<s>daśāpāka</s>), accomplishment without obstacles, protection of the base,

children.text: duṣṭasya saṃsiddhim anāmayatvaṃ vadanti te mānayitur nṛpasya//E32
children.translated_text: or allies, accomplishment of what was difficult, and freedom from illness—these are declared for the king who honors [the omens].

children.text: śūrakṛtāsramahākulajātāḥ svāmihitā balinaḥ kṛtayogyāḥ/
children.translated_text: Born of illustrious families of warriors, devoted to their lord, strong, well-trained,

children.text: dṛṣṭaguṇā bahubāndhavamitrā nāgakarorubhujāḥ kaṭhināṅgāḥ//
children.translated_text: of proven merit, having many kinsmen and friends, with arms like elephant trunks, thighs [like pillars], of hard limbs;

children.text: vyāghramṛgeśvaragovṛṣanādāḥ śyenadṛśaḥ śukasannibhanāsāḥ/
children.translated_text: roaring like tigers, lions, or bulls; with eyes like hawks, noses like parrots;

children.text: kekarajihmanimīlitanetrāḥ puṇyakṛtāṃ samareṣu sahāyāḥ//
children.translated_text: those with squinting, crooked, or half-closed eyes—these are the allies of the meritorious in battles.

children.text: deśaguṇaiḥ prathitāś ca purogās te bahavo guṇalakṣaṇalakṣyāḥ/
children.translated_text: Those renowned for the qualities of their region, serving as vanguards, many of them marked by virtues and characteristics,

children.text: kālabhṛto bhṛkuṭīkṛtavakrāvamabhṛto vividhāyudhahastāḥ//
children.translated_text: those paid regular wages, with furrowed brows and fierce faces, those maintained on rations, bearing various weapons in hand—

children.text: daṇḍoragau ravisutasya raves tu cakraṃ śukrasya padmaśakaṭau garuḍo budhasya/
children.translated_text: The staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>) and serpent formations are <s>Saturn</s>'s; the wheel (<s>cakra</s>) belongs to the <s>Sun</s>; the lotus and cart formations belong to <s>Venus</s>; the eagle (<s>garuḍa</s>) belongs to <s>Mercury</s>;

children.text: vyūhau tu sūcimakarau dharaṇīsutasya śyeno guroḥ śiśiragor api maṇḍalākhyaḥ//
children.translated_text: the needle (<s>sūci</s>) and crocodile (<s>makara</s>) formations belong to <s>Mars</s>; the hawk (<s>śyena</s>) belongs to <s>Jupiter</s>; and <s>Moon</s>'s is called the circle (<s>maṇḍala</s>).

children.text: vyūham ātmaśubhadagrahasya yad vidviṣām aśubhasaṃsthitasya vā/
children.translated_text: The formation [corresponding to] one's own auspicious planet, or that [corresponding to] the enemy's inauspiciously positioned [planet],

children.text: tatprayojyam ariyojitasya vā ghātanaṃ tadaribhir balottaraiḥ//
children.translated_text: should be employed; or for destroying the formation deployed by the enemy, [one should use] that which is superior in strength to the enemy's.

children.text: raṇe pratyāsanne sadasi nṛpatir mantrividitaṃ
children.translated_text: When battle is imminent, the king in his assembly should inspire

children.text: balotsāhaṃ kuryād ahitavalavidrāvaṇakaram/
children.translated_text: courage and enthusiasm in the army, known through counsel, so as to scatter the enemy's forces.

children.text: jayaṃ no daivajñaḥ kathayati janaḥ satyavacano
children.translated_text: 'The astrologer declares our victory; he is a man of true speech;

children.text: nimittānīṣṭāni dvipaturagayodhādiṣu ca me//
children.translated_text: and the omens are favorable regarding elephants, horses, warriors, and others on my side.'

children.text: abhijanayutā yūyaṃ sauryaṃ janāḥ kathayanti vo
children.translated_text: 'You are of noble birth; people speak of your valor.

children.text: dhanuṣi kaṇaye cakre śaktyām asau ca kṛtaśramāḥ/
children.translated_text: You are trained in the bow, the arrow, the discus, and the spear.

children.text: mayi ca bhavatām asti snehaḥ kathan na jayo mama
children.translated_text: And you have affection for me—how can victory not be mine,

children.text: dviradaturagaṃ syād ākrāntaṃ bhavadbhir idaṃ yadā//
children.translated_text: when you would have mounted upon elephants and horses?'

children.text: bṛṃhanti heṣanti śivaṃ bruvanti dīpyanti śocanti mudānvitāś ca/
children.translated_text: 'The elephants trumpet, the horses neigh auspiciously, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> speak blessings, the fire blazes, the enemy grieves, and the warriors are filled with joy—

children.text: nāgāśvaviprānalaśatruyodhāḥ kaḥ saṃśayaś cātra raṇe jayasya//
children.translated_text: what doubt is there of victory in battle?'

children.text: dveṣāyanena muninā manunā ca dharmā yuddheṣu ye nigaditā viditās tu te vaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The <s>dharmas</s> in warfare proclaimed by the sage <s>Manu</s>, who [taught] out of compassion, are known to you.

children.text: svāmyarthagodvijahite tyajatāṃ śarīraṃ lokā bhavanti sulabhā vipulaṃ jayaś ca//
children.translated_text: Let those who abandon their bodies for the sake of their lord, cattle, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> [know that] the [heavenly] worlds are easily obtained, and victory is great.'

children.text: tapasvibhir yā sucireṇa labhyate prayatnataḥ satribhir ijyayā ca yā/
children.translated_text: 'That [heavenly] destination which is obtained by ascetics only after a long time and with effort, and by virtuous women through worship—

children.text: vrajanti tām āśu gatiṃ manasvino raṇāśvamedhe paśutām upāgataḥ//
children.translated_text: the spirited ones who have assumed the role of sacrificial animals in the battle-<s>aśvamedha</s> (horse-sacrifice) quickly attain that.'

children.text: yasya tapo na janāḥ kathayanti no maraṇaṃ samare vijayañ ca/
children.translated_text: 'He of whom people speak neither of austerity, nor of death in battle, nor of victory,

children.text: na śrutadānamahādhanatāṃ vā tasya bhavaḥ kṛmikīṭasamānaḥ//
children.translated_text: nor of fame from learning, generosity, or great wealth—his existence is equal to that of a worm or an insect.'

children.text: sarakṣyamāṇam api nāśam upaity avaśyam etac charīram apahāya suhṛtsutārthān/
children.translated_text: 'Even when protected, this body inevitably goes to destruction, carrying away dear friends, sons, and wealth.

children.text: tat kiṃ varaṃ pralapatāṃ suhṛdāṃ samakṣaṃ kiṃ nidhnataḥ parabalaṃ bhṛkuṭīmukhasya//
children.translated_text: Then what is better: [dying] in the sight of lamenting friends, or [dying] while crushing the enemy's army with a fierce, frowning face?'

children.text: hā tāta māteti ca vedanārtthāḥ dhavaṇañ chakṛnmūtrakaphānuliptaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Crying "Alas father! Alas mother!" in agony, smeared with the running of excrement, urine, and phlegm—

children.text: varaṃ mṛtaḥ kiṃ bhavane kim ājau sandaṣṭadantacchadabhīmavaktraḥ//
children.translated_text: is it better to die thus at home, or in battle with teeth clenched and face terrifying?'

children.text: lokaḥ śubhas tiṣṭhatu tāvad anyaḥ parāṅmukhānāṃ samareṣu puṃsām/
children.translated_text: 'Let the other auspicious world stand aside—for men who turn their backs in battle,

children.text: patnyo 'pi teṣāṃ na hriyā mukhāni puraḥ sakhīnām avalokayanti//
children.translated_text: even their wives, out of shame, do not look at their faces in the presence of their friends.'

children.text: śatrusainyam avadārya varttatāṃ yat sukhantu kathayāmi tādṛśam/
children.translated_text: 'Having torn apart the enemy's army, let me speak of the happiness that follows—

children.text: śṛṇvatāṃ svayaśasograpallavān digbadhūvadanakarṇapūrakān//
children.translated_text: hearing one's own glorious praises, fierce like shoots, filling the ears of the bride-faces of the directions.'

children.text: nipatati śirasi dvipasya siṃhaḥ svatanuśatādhikamāṃsarāśimūrtteḥ/
children.translated_text: 'A lion falls upon the head of an elephant, a mass of flesh exceeding a hundred of its own bodies,

children.text: pibati ca tadasṛgmadeṣṭagandhaṃ vadanagatāṃś ca śanaiḥ prasṛjya muktān//
children.translated_text: and drinks its blood, fragrant with rut-fluid, slowly releasing from its mouth [the flesh] that had entered.'

children.text: maṇikanakavibhūṣitā yuvatyo dvipaturagaṃ vasu cāmarānilaś ca/
children.translated_text: 'Women adorned with jewels and gold, elephants, horses, wealth, the breeze of <s>cāmara</s> (yak-tail) fans,

children.text: aviralaśaśikānti cātapatraṃ bhavati na mātṛmukhasya yuddhabhīroḥ//
children.translated_text: and a parasol shining like the unbroken moon—these are not for one afraid of battle who cries for his mother.'

children.text: rucimatku bāhupañjare harinākṣyaḥ pravarorupīḍanam/
children.translated_text: 'In the beautiful cage of his arms, doe-eyed women, pressing upon his excellent thighs,

children.text: ramayanti vimānasaṃsthitāḥ surabadhvo 'timudā raṇārjitāḥ//
children.translated_text: delight him who is seated in a celestial chariot—the wives of the gods, won through battle, with supreme joy.'

children.text: ekato 'sya surasundarījanaḥ śrīḥ pratīcchati yuyutsuto 'nyaḥ/
children.translated_text: 'On one side, the host of divine beauties and <s>Śrī</s> (glory) welcomes the one who desires to fight; on the other,

children.text: padmayā saha palāyate yaśaś caikataḥ kulakalaṅkakārakam//
children.translated_text: fame flees along with <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>)—that which brings disgrace to the family.'

children.text: ārāmadevakulakūpataḍāgayajñā ye vaḥ kṛtā bilasitañ ca nṛpaprasādāt/
children.translated_text: 'The gardens, temples, wells, reservoirs, and sacrifices that you have performed, and the enjoyments [gained] through the king's favor—

children.text: tad vo vṛtho yadi na niśchalamājimadhye vidyullatāvikasitāni karoti vo 'siḥ//
children.translated_text: all that is in vain if your sword does not make lightning-vine-like flashes amidst the steady battlefield.'

children.text: citraṃ kim asmin vada sāhasaṃ vā yat svāmino 'rthe ganayanti nāsūn/
children.translated_text: 'Tell me, what is remarkable or daring in this—that [warriors] do not count their lives for their lord's sake?

children.text: yuddhāt pranaṣṭo vidito 'rimadhye yadvāliśa staṣṭhati sāhasaṃ tat//
children.translated_text: One who has fled from battle and is recognized amid the enemies—the fact that he lives is the [real] daring.'

children.text: na kevalaṃ gātravibhūṣaṇāni kṣatāni śūrasya raṇe kṛtāni/
children.translated_text: 'The wounds made on the hero's body in battle are not mere ornaments of the limbs—

children.text: yaśastaror mūlakṛṣikṣatāni tāny eva vaṃśasya vibhūṣaṇāni//
children.translated_text: they are the ploughings at the root of the tree of fame, and they are the very ornaments of the dynasty.'

children.text: bhagneṣu yodheṣv avapūrya śastrāṇy ājau pravṛttā vyasavaḥ kṛtā ye/
children.translated_text: 'Those who, when warriors have been broken, taking up weapons, enter the fray and give up their lives,

children.text: ūrdhvānanā vājimakhāptalokās teṣāṃ vimānāny avalokayanti//
children.translated_text: with faces turned upward, they behold the celestial chariots of the worlds attained through the horse-sacrifice.'

children.text: yair śvamedhe 'bhihitaṃ phalaṃ vā devair dvijair vā śrutiśāstrakāraiḥ/
children.translated_text: 'The very reward that has been declared for the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse-sacrifice) by the gods, by the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, or by the authors of <s>śruti</s> and <s>śāstras</s>—

children.text: tair eva bhaṅge pratilomagasya pade pade vājimakhaḥ pradiṣṭaḥ//
children.translated_text: by those same [authorities], at every step of one who goes against the retreating [enemy], a horse-sacrifice is proclaimed.'

children.text: svargasya mārgā bahavaḥ pradiṣṭās te kṛcchrasādhyāḥ kuṭilāḥ savighnāḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Many paths to heaven have been proclaimed, [but] they are difficult to accomplish, crooked, and full of obstacles.

children.text: nimeṣamātreṇa mahāphalo 'yam ṛjuś ca panthāḥ samare vyāsutvam//
children.translated_text: This path in battle—giving up one's life—is straight and of great reward in the blink of an eye.'

children.text: dṛṣṭāiśvaryaṃ svāmigobrāhmaṇārthe tyaktāsūnāṃ saṅgare saṅgatānām/
children.translated_text: 'Those who have abandoned their lives in battle for the sake of their lord, cattle, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>—their witnessed glory [is such that]

children.text: kṛcchropāyair arjitasvargalokāḥ janmecchanti kṣipram evājilobhāt//
children.translated_text: those who have won the heavenly worlds through difficult means desire birth again swiftly, out of eagerness for battle.'

children.text: saṃmūrcchitaṃ saṃyugasaṃprahāraiḥ paśyanti suptapratibuddhatulyam/
children.translated_text: 'Stunned by the blows of combat, they see themselves—like one awakened from sleep—

children.text: ātmānam aṅkeṣu surāṅganānāṃ mandākinīmārutabījitāṅgāḥ//
children.translated_text: in the laps of celestial women, their limbs fanned by the breezes of the <s>Mandākinī</s> (celestial Ganges).'

children.text: jīvito 'pi nihatasya vā raṇe dharma eva hi narasya yudhyataḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Whether one lives or is slain in battle, <s>dharma</s> alone [accrues] for the man who fights.

children.text: niścayān na maraṇāṃ hi saṅgare naiva bhīrujarāmaraḥ kvacit//
children.translated_text: Certainly, death is not certain in battle, and the coward is never immortal.'

children.text: mānamātram avalambya yudhyate kīṭako 'pi vihago 'tha vā paśuḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Holding onto nothing but pride, even an insect fights, or a bird, or an animal.

children.text: ko hi nāma puruṣas tyajed raṇaṃ svagamānasukhakīrttivittadam//
children.translated_text: What man, then, would abandon battle, which gives heaven, pleasure, fame, and wealth?'

children.text: yad abhāvi na me 'sti tat kvacit sadasadbhāvi na me kva yāsyati/
children.translated_text: 'What was not to be will not be for me anywhere; what is to be, whether good or bad, will not go away from me—

children.text: iti saṃparicintya paṇḍitāḥ parasainyāni viśanty aviklavāḥ//
children.translated_text: thinking thus, the wise enter the enemy armies without agitation.'

children.text: uraḥ kṛtvā vedyāṃ maṇiphalakagāḍhasthitakucaṃ bhujā vālambyair hītyamaravanitā vyomagṛhagāḥ/
children.translated_text: 'Making the chest a sacrificial altar, with breasts firmly set like jeweled boards, celestial women dwelling in sky-palaces grasp the arms [of the fallen hero]; thus with swift steps, through the very door of calamity, others

children.text: apadvāreṇaivaṃ tvaritapadam atyāhur aparā hataṃ hastālaghvair harati suraloko raṇamukhāt//
children.translated_text: with quick hands snatch the slain one from the battlefield—the heavenly world carries him away.'

children.text: haṃsāḍhayaṃ maṇivedikākuharakavyālaṃ bihārāmbaraṃ
children.translated_text: 'Filled with <s>haṃsas</s> (swans), with jeweled platforms and serpent-shaped alcoves, with vast pleasure-grounds,

children.text: nirvyūhasthitaratnacitrakanakaṃ stambhāśritaṃ vyālakam/
children.translated_text: with jewels and variegated gold set in arrays, with serpent-forms clinging to pillars,

children.text: ghaṇṭākiṅkiṇicārucāmarayutastrīgītanṛtyānvitaṃ
children.translated_text: with bells, tinkling ornaments, beautiful <s>cāmara</s> fans, accompanied by the singing and dancing of women—

children.text: bālārkopamam āviśanty abhimukhā yuddhe vimānaṃ hatāḥ//E32
children.translated_text: those slain in battle enter such a celestial chariot, resplendent as the young sun, face forward.'

children.text: atra dhvajapraharaṇāny abhimantritāni kurvanti śatrukadana ripuvāhinīnām/
children.translated_text: Here [the text describes how] they consecrate banners and weapons with <s>mantras</s>, causing the destruction of the enemy in hostile armies.

children.text: mantraṃ jagāda bhagavān uśanāḥ svaśāstre yal likhyate sa iha pūrvavidhikrameṇa//
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Uśanas</s> (<s>Śukra</s>) taught in his own <s>śāstra</s> is written here in the order of the previous procedure:

children.text: <oṃ indro 'gnir indravajradharo 'yaṃ hariṇo 'bhiniryāya paraṃ hana hana daha daha svāhā>/
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ Indro 'gnir Indravajradharo 'yaṃ hariṇo 'bhiniryāya paraṃ hana hana daha daha svāhā</s>

children.text: pracalitagajavājiśūrayodhaṃ samabhimukhodyataśastram abhyupetam/
children.translated_text: When the enemy army has approached with elephants, horses, and brave warriors set in motion, with weapons raised and facing [you],

children.text: abhimukhadinakṛtprabhañjanaṃ ca sthirahṛdayo 'ribala sukhaṃ nihanyāt//
children.translated_text: and with the sun and the storm-wind facing [the enemy], the steady-hearted [king] should easily slay the enemy's army.

children.text: aśubhakhagamṛgaṃ ca dakṣiṇe nipatati ketupatākabheva vā/
children.translated_text: And if inauspicious birds and animals [appear] on the right, or if banners and flags fall,

children.text: paruṣaviṣamamandajarjaro yadi khalu tūryaravo 'sya vāmataḥ//
children.translated_text: and if on his left the sound of the war-drums is harsh, uneven, slow, and broken—

children.text: yat pṛṣṭhataḥ seṣugajāśvayodham niṣṭhitavyūhamarātisainyam/
children.translated_text: that enemy army which has its archers, elephants, horses, and warriors in the rear, with its battle-formation completed,

children.text: yasyendracāpaṃ ca lalāṭasaṃstha tat pṛṣṭhabhāgaḥ kuśalo 'bhihanyāt//
children.translated_text: and which has <s>Indra</s>'s rainbow stationed at its forehead—a skilled [commander] should strike that from behind.

children.text: nārttā na bhītā na tṛṇānanāś ca vimuktaśastrāḥ prapalayamānāḥ/
children.translated_text: Those who are wounded, frightened, with faces [turned away like] grass, who have dropped their weapons, who are fleeing,

children.text: kṣīṇāyudhā vājigajāvatīrṇā hy ete na badhyā na ca pīḍanīyāḥ//
children.translated_text: whose weapons are exhausted, or who have dismounted from horses and elephants—these should not be killed nor tormented.

children.text: kulaikatantuḥ śaraṇāgato vā kṛtāñjaliryaś ca vadet tava 'smi/
children.translated_text: One who is the last thread of his family, one who has come for refuge, one who with joined palms says 'I am yours,'

children.text: ayudhyamānān avagamya hanyāś na pālakān strīparirakṣitāṃś ca//
children.translated_text: those who are not fighting, those who are recognized as protectors, and those guarded by women—should not be slain.

children.text: digdāhakṣitijarajośmavṛṣṭipātair nirghātakṣiticalanādivaikṛtaiś ca/
children.translated_text: By the burning of directions, earthquakes, dust-storms, heat, rainfall, thunderbolts, earth-tremors, and other portents,

children.text: yuddhānte mṛgaśakunaiś ca dīptanādair no bhadraṃ bhavati jaye 'pi pārthivasya//
children.translated_text: and by animals and birds with blazing cries at the end of battle—there is no auspiciousness for the king, even in victory.

children.text: śubhā mṛgapatatriṇo mṛdusamīraṇohlādakṛd grahāḥ sphuṭamarīcayo vigatareṇudigmaṇḍalam/
children.translated_text: When animals and birds are auspicious, the breeze is gentle and delightful, the planets have clear rays, and the horizon is free from dust,

children.text: yad anyam api vaikṛtan na vijayāvasāne yadā tadā sukham akaṇṭakaṃ nṛpatir atti deśaṃ ripoḥ//
children.translated_text: and when there are no other portents at the conclusion of victory—then the king enjoys the enemy's land happily, free from thorns.

children.text: paraviṣayapurāptau sādhudevadvijasvaṃ kulajanavanitāś ca kṣmādhipo noparundhyāt/
children.translated_text: Upon obtaining the enemy's territory and cities, the lord of the earth should not obstruct the property of virtuous people, gods, or <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, nor the women of good families.

children.text: janapadahitayuktān pūjayet pauramukhyān śubhatithikaraṇarkṣe hṛṣṭasainyo viśoc ca//
children.translated_text: He should honor the leaders of the citizens who are devoted to the welfare of the people, and should enter [the city] on an auspicious <s>tithi</s>, <s>karaṇa</s>, and <s>nakṣatra</s>, with his army jubilant.

children.text: dṛti manujapatir yathopadeśaṃ bhagaṇavidāṃ prakaroti yo vacāṃsi/
children.translated_text: The lord of men who, with resolve, acts according to the instructions and the words of the astronomers—

children.text: sa sakalamahimaṇḍalādhipatyaṃ vrajati divīva purandaro 'cireṇa//
children.translated_text: he attains sovereignty over the entire circle of the earth swiftly, like <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) in heaven.

children.text: alabdhalipsā prathamaṃ nṛpasya labdhasya saṃrakṣaṇasampravṛddhī/
children.translated_text: First, the king's desire to obtain what is not yet gained; then the protection and increase of what has been gained;

children.text: samyak pravṛddhasya ca lābhako 'yaṃ tīrtheṣu samyak patipādanāni//
children.translated_text: and for what has been properly increased, this is the gain—the proper establishment [of rule] in the sacred sites.

children.text: kendreṣu saumyair guruśukralagne pāpeṣu kendrāṣṭamavarjitesu/
children.translated_text: With benefics in the <s>kendras</s>, <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) and <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) in the <s>lagna</s>, malefics not in the <s>kendras</s> or eighth house,

children.text: prāmye sthire vā 'nidhane ca lagne gṛhaṃ viśec chrītakare 'nukūle/
children.translated_text: with the <s>lagna</s> in the afternoon or in a fixed sign, and not in the eighth house, one should enter the house when the cold season is favorable.

children.text: pauṣṇe dhaniṣṭhāsv atha vāruṇeṣu svāyambhuvarkṣeṣu triṣūttarāsu/
children.translated_text: Under [the <s>nakṣatras</s>] <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (Revatī), <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, or the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (Śatabhiṣaj) [group], or under <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [asterisms], or the three <s>Uttarā</s> [asterisms],

children.text: akṣīṇacandre śubhavāsare ca tithāv arikte ca gṛhapraveśaḥ//
children.translated_text: with the Moon not waning, on an auspicious weekday, and on a <s>tithi</s> that is not empty—[this is the time for] entering the house.

children.text: dharmeṇa pṛthvīṃ kila pālayitvā jalāśayārāmasurālayāḍhyām/
children.translated_text: Having protected the earth through <s>dharma</s>, having made it rich with reservoirs, gardens, and temples,

children.text: kṛtvā sakūpāṃ citibhiś citāñ ca jayanti lokān amareśvarasya//
children.translated_text: and having adorned it with wells and funeral pyres—they conquer the worlds of the lord of the immortals.

children.text: svaviṣayam upagamya mānavendro vallim upayācitakāni cādhikāni/
children.translated_text: Having returned to his own territory, the king of honor should give offerings and additional [gifts]—

children.text: nigaditavidhinaiva sampradadyāt pramathagaṇāsurabhūtadevatābhyaḥ//
children.translated_text: as prescribed by the stated procedure—to the hosts of <s>Pramathas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Bhūtas</s>, and deities.

children.text: yātrāvatāra ādāv ācāraś vābhiyojyako deśaḥ/
children.translated_text: The introduction to the <s>Yātrā</s> (campaign), the conduct or the region to be attacked,

children.text: yogādhyāyo bhiṣakabalyupahārau tathā snānam//
children.translated_text: the chapter on <s>yogas</s>, the physician, the <s>bali</s>-offering and oblation, and the bath;

children.text: agninimittaṃ nakṣatrakaindubhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tathā vāryāḥ/
children.translated_text: the fire-omens, the <s>nakṣatra</s> [chapter], the lunar [chapter], the characteristics of the army;

children.text: śālāvidhir gajeṅgitamadakaraṇaṃ vājiceṣṭā ca//
children.translated_text: the procedure for buildings, the gestures and rut-periods of elephants, and the behavior of horses;

children.text: khaḍgavidhiḥ prasthānaṃ śākunam utsāhapuraniveśaś ca/
children.translated_text: the procedure for swords, the march, ornithomancy, the [chapter on] enthusiasm, and the arrangement of the camp—

children.text: adhyāyasaṃpraho 'yaṃ samāsataś cātra nirdiṣṭaḥ//E18
children.translated_text: this is the summary of chapters, and here it is concisely set forth.
